evidence.title: Tata Electronics flags supply chain, talent gaps in ₹1.18 lakh crore semiconductor push
evidence.text:
Tata Electronics, which is investing up to ₹1.18 lakh crore in semiconductor manufacturing facilities in Gujarat and Assam, is grappling with challenges ranging from developing a local supplier ecosystem and transporting specialised equipment to bridging the gap between available talent and industry readiness.
Srinivas Satya, President of Components Business and Supply Chain at Tata Electronics, said on Tuesday that building semiconductor manufacturing capabilities in India required addressing several supply-side constraints, even as the company scaled up its operations.
The company is setting up a semiconductor fabrication facility at Dholera, Gujarat, with an investment of up to ₹91,000 crore and a planned capacity of 50,000 wafers a month. In Assam, it is developing a ₹27,000-crore Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) facility at Jagiroad in Morigaon district.
Speaking at a keynote session at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, Mr. Satya said the Assam facility would have around one million sq. ft. of cleanroom space across two production plants. The first plant has been completed, while work on the second is beginning.
Tata Electronics is currently engaging with 1,200-1,300 suppliers across its electronics and semiconductor businesses, with more than 500 involved in construction alone. Describing the broader supply chain as “still not fully mature”, Mr. Satya said construction activities required for the company’s operations were also yet to be completed.
Logistics presents significant challenges. With specialised equipment and materials sourced across geographies stretching from the U.S. to the Far East, cross-border movement has become a critical component of the company’s supply chain.
To strengthen domestic capabilities, Tata Electronics has signed memoranda of understanding with global semiconductor and packaging companies. These partnerships cover local capability development, setting up sales and service centres, and training employees as well as India’s wider talent pool.
Mr. Satya said the company would replicate, with suitable modifications, its approach in electronics manufacturing, where it identified small engineering firms, exposed them to factory operations and helped them develop solutions.
On manpower, he acknowledged a “quite a chasm” between India’s “phenomenal talent pool” and the skills required by the semiconductor industry. However, he termed the gap “not an insurmountable challenge by any means”.
Tata Electronics has assembled talent from 14-15 countries and is sending young engineers to a partner fabrication facility in Taiwan for three to six months of on-the-job training. It has also partnered with IIT Bombay, IIT Gandhinagar and IIT Guwahati.
The Gujarat fab is being designed as “AI first, AI ready right from the beginning”, with artificial intelligence being integrated at equipment, plant and workforce levels to improve manufacturing yield and productivity.
The economics of semiconductor manufacturing make such improvements critical. Individual equipment can cost $1 million-$3 million, taking the total equipment investment to $5 billion-$6 billion. Annual operating expenses have been estimated at around $500 million, Mr. Satya said.
Published - November 18, 2026 04:58 pm IST

evidence.title: Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles Get A New Dealer In Syria
evidence.text:
Tata Motors, one of the world’s leading automotive manufacturers has announced its partnership with Ghassan Aboud Automotive, through its subsidiary, Grand Auto & Machinery Co. (GAMCO), as their distributor for their commercial vehicles in Syria. Through thispartnership, Tata Motors will introduce its range of advanced commercial vehicles, from sub-1-tonne to 60 tonnes in cargo segment, and mass mobility solutions, from 9 to 71 seats to customers in Syria, supported by sales and service across the country.
Commenting on the announcement, Mr. Asif Shamim, Head – International Business, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles, said “We are pleased to partner with Ghassan Aboud Automotive and GAMCO as we introduce our advanced mobility solutions in Syria. The company brings deep industry expertise, a strong customer-first approach and an established footprint in the region. With roadtransport serving as the backbone of Syria’s freight movement, we are confident that our wide range of Tata Motors’ dependable commercial vehicles will find strong response in the country. Tata Motors’ portfolio is globally recognised for delivering high productivity,robust performance and low total cost of ownership, backed by comprehensive sales and aftermarket support. This partnership marks an important step in expanding our presence in the region, empowering local businesses across both cargo logistics and mass-mobilityapplications.”
Saud Abbasi, CEO – Emerging Markets at Ghassan Aboud Holding,said, “We are delighted to partner with Tata Motors and welcome a globally recognised name to our growing portfolio in Syria. We believe Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle range is well aligned with the needs and requirements of the Syrian market, offeringreliable and practical solutions to support businesses across different sectors. We have high expectations for the brand and its potential in Syria and look forward to building a successful partnership that creates long-term value for our customers and partnerswhile contributing to the country’s development.”
With more than eight decades of expertise, Tata Motors is present inover 50 countries spread across Africa, Middle East South and Southeast Asia, South America and CIS, among others. The company’s state-of-the-art research and development facilities have steadily worked to engineer innovative mobility solutions powered byalternate fuel technology, including battery-electric, hybrid, CNG, LNG and Hydrogen Fuel Cell technology. Backed by advanced R&D capabilities and deep experience across diverse operating conditions, the company is well positioned to support Syria’s growthambitions – with the Middle East standing out as a core pillar of Tata Motors’ global strategy and a region where long‑term partnership, local capability and future‑ready mobility solutions converge.

evidence.title: Tata Group draws interest from Honda, Hyundai for vehicle and technology sharing
evidence.text:
The Tata Group is drawing interest from global automakers seeking cooperation in vehicles, engineering and technology, with conversations involving Honda Motor Company and Hyundai Motor Company taking place over the past year.
Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran met Honda’s senior management in Japan in 2025, including Honda Motor Company president Toshihiro Mibe and Toshiyuki Yanagisawa, according to people familiar with the meeting. Yanagisawa led Honda’s India Strategic Development Office before taking over as president and CEO of Honda Cars India on October 1, 2026.
Separately, Hyundai Motor Company president and CEO Jose Munoz met Chandrasekaran at his Mumbai office. People familiar with the meeting described it as a courtesy visit, during which possible areas of business cooperation may have come up.
Honda talks span several Tata businesses
Honda’s discussions have involved Tata Motors, Tata AutoComp, battery maker Agratas, Tata Technologies, TCS and Tata Elxsi, according to industry sources familiar with the talks.
Honda’s discussions have progressed further with Tata Consultancy Services and Tata Technologies. Its talks with Tata Motors remain exploratory and have included the possibility of selling Tata vehicles, including EVs, under the Honda badge in India, the people said. The companies have yet to agree on a model, a supply arrangement or a timetable, the sources said.
Honda has identified India as one of three priority markets for growth, alongside Japan and North America. It is also working on a vehicle developed for India that it plans to launch in 2028.
Using an existing vehicle or platform could help Honda add models in India at a lower development cost and bring them to market sooner. For Tata Motors, additional volumes could help recover its engineering investment. A deal would depend, in part, on how much capacity Tata Motors could commit while increasing output for its own models.
In response to a query from our sister publication, Autocar Professional, Honda Cars India said, “As a policy, we cannot comment on such speculations.”
The Honda connection goes back to 1985
Tata pursued a car-manufacturing tie-up with Honda in 1985. Records at the Tata Central Archives show that Honda president Tadashi Kume and TELCO’s Sumant Moolgaokar signed an agreement on July 10 that year. However, the project never went ahead.
Four decades later, the two sides have discussed whether Honda could sell a Tata-developed vehicle under its own badge in India.
Hyundai’s India investment opens scope for local partnerships
Hyundai Motor Group has committed $15.5 billion in investments in India between 2026 and 2032. The plan covers manufacturing expansion at Hyundai and Kia, research and development, and investments in local suppliers and future mobility businesses. The group plans to set up a dedicated investment entity in India to identify local partners and support strategic partnerships.
Tata’s businesses span much of the automotive value chain, from vehicle manufacturing at Tata Motors and components at Tata AutoComp to batteries at Agratas, engineering at Tata Technologies, and software and digital services at Tata Elxsi and TCS. Those capabilities may have come up during the courtesy visit. The meeting, however, did not yield a specific project.
Emails seeking comment from Tata Motors and Hyundai Motor Company remained unanswered at the time of writing.
Stellantis signs up for Tata vehicle technology
Not just Honda and Hyundai, but Jeep too has announced concrete plans of vehicle and technology sharing with Tata Motors. Earlier this year, Stellantis, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Tata Passenger Electric Mobility announced a definitive agreement on vehicle technology and product development.
Stellantis will use Tata Motors’ product technology and architecture, alongside its own engineering capabilities, to develop vehicles for more than 50 markets. The vehicles will be built at Fiat India Automobiles, their 50:50 manufacturing joint venture.
At Stellantis’ Investor Day in May, Gregoire Olivier, then the company’s Asia-Pacific chief operating officer, said Tata Motors would “provide a highly competitive platform to develop a new Jeep car”. He said the vehicle would be developed and assembled in India for global markets. We have reported that a Jeep SUV based on the Tata Sierra’s ARGOS architecture is taking shape under the partnership.

evidence.title: Honda, Hyundai In Talks With Tata For Parts, Vehicles, Platforms Collab – Report
evidence.text:
For collaborative projects with other OEMs, Tata Group companies such as Tata AutoComp, Agratas, Tata Technologies, Tata Elxsi and TCS could also play a key role
To reduce development and production costs, shorten time to market, and explore export opportunities, carmakers are increasingly looking at partnerships with Indian auto companies. A relevant example is Tata Motors, which already has a platform sharing agreement with Stellantis. Tata Group company Tata Technologies is also progressing with its project to develop a new vehicle platform for Honda.
And that’s not all. Latest reports reveal that Honda and Hyundai are in direct talks with Tata Motors for new collaborations involving vehicles, components, engineering and technology. However, there is no formal acknowledgment of these developments by any company.
Honda-Tata collab discussions
It is reported that discussions were held between Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran and Honda’s senior management. This was during a meeting in Japan last year. From Honda’s side, the representation was from Honda Motor Company president Toshihiro Mibe and the current President and CEO of Honda Cars India, Toshiyuki Yanagisawa.
In addition to its ongoing project with Tata Technologies, Honda has reportedly held talks with other Tata Group companies. These include the battery manufacturer Agratas, automotive components manufacturer Tata AutoComp, design-led technology and engineering services company Tata Elxsi and software major Tata Consultancy Services (TCS). Discussions with Tata Technologies and TCS are progressing further.
Honda has also held direct talks with Tata Motors, although these remain exploratory at this point in time. These talks reportedly included discussions about Honda selling Tata vehicles under its own badge in India. Possibilities for both ICE and EVs were likely explored during the discussion. Since there is no formal acknowledgement from Honda or Tata, it is difficult to determine the progress of these proposed collaborations.
Honda has identified the Indian market as one of its key growth drivers. Japan and North America are the other two important markets for Honda. Collaborations within India can help reduce development costs and introduce new models at a steady pace. Honda has big ambitions for India, with 10 new models planned by 2030. Tata Motors is also working on a major product offensive, with 15 ICE cars and 10 EVs planned by FY31.
Hyundai-Tata talks
Hyundai-Tata talks were reportedly held between N Chandrasekaran and Hyundai Motor Company President and CEO Jose Munoz in Mumbai. While it was described as a courtesy visit, there could have been discussions about potential collaborative ventures. Since both companies have outlined major portfolio expansion plans, joint efforts could potentially deliver better results for both. Hyundai can probably benefit from the large auto ecosystem created by Tata Group companies.
Hyundai has planned 26 models and updates by 2030. The company has announced an investment of USD 15.5 billion (approx. Rs 1,47,089.65 crore) for India, spread across 2026-2032. evidence.title: Tata Sierra EV Gets 5-Star Safety Rating In Bharat NCAP Crash Tests: Watch Video
evidence.text:
The Tata Sierra EV has undergone Bharat NCAP crash tests and earned a 5-star safety rating. The electric Tata SUV scored 30.62 points out of a total of 32 for adult occupant protection and 45 out of 49 for child occupant protection. The test car was the top-spec Empowered 75kWh QWD, but the rating applies to every variant of the SUV. The tested model was the top-spec Empowered 75kWh QWD. That said, the rating is applicable across all variants. The Sierra EV is the new Tata to be part of the top-rated Bharat NCAP cars in India, and it gives EV buyers in India one more reason to put it on their shortlist. Prices for the Sierra EV range begins at Rs 18.79 lakh and goes up to Rs 25.99 lakh (Both, ex-showroom).
Tata Sierra EV Bharat NCAP Ratings Explained
During the adult occupant protection evaluation, the Tata Sierra EV scored 30.62 points out of 32. The SUV earned a perfect score (16/16) in the side movable deformable barrier assessment. It earned 14.62 points in the frontal offset test, where the driver and front passenger received good protection across most body regions. Their tibiae were rated adequate and the driver's feet marginal. The SUV also did well during the side pole impact assessment.As for child safety, the Sierra EV earned a score of 45 out of a total of 49 points. It gained full marks in both the dynamic crash assessment (24/24) and CRS installation tests (12/12). The evaluation was carried out using rearward-facing child dummies representing 18-month-old and 3-year-old occupants, both of whom earned full scores in side impact testing. The SUV missed four points in the vehicle assessment, with 9 points out of a total of 13.
The Sierra EV earned 30.62 points in adult occupant protection category.
Tata Sierra EV Battery And Safety Features
The electric SUV is available with two battery pack options, a 63kWh unit and a larger 75kWh pack. It is also the second electric SUV from Tata Motors, after the Harrier EV, to come with a Quad Wheel Drive (QWD) system, offering power delivery to all four wheels.Tata has equipped the Sierra EV with a wide spectrum of safety features as standard across its variants. These are ABS with EBD, hill hold assist, six airbags, an Electronic Stability Program (ESP), and traction control. Other amenities include a tyre pressure monitoring system (TPMS), all-wheel disc brakes, ISOFIX child-seat mounts, and an electronic parking brake with auto hold.

evidence.title: What Is Tata Motors Trying To Do With Jaguar Land Rover?
evidence.text:
For a company famous for making some of the world's best-known luxury SUVs, Jaguar Land Rover is facing a surprisingly basic problem. It is selling luxury cars, but not making enough money from them. And its owner, Tata Motors, is now trying to change far more than the cars themselves.
New electric Range Rovers, a completely different Jaguar, a bigger push into America and a major cost-cutting programme are all part of the same plan. Tata wants JLR to grow, charge more for its vehicles and become less vulnerable when demand slows.
But this transformation is arriving at an awkward time, with profits under pressure, debt rising and billions of pounds still being spent on new products.
This is especially important for Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, which now owns JLR after separating its commercial vehicle business. In Q2 FY27, JLR contributed Rs. 75,420 crore of the group's Rs. 96,920 crore revenue from operations.
What happens to this British business can therefore have a much bigger impact on Tata's financial results than its Indian passenger-car operations alone.
Why Does Tata Want To Change JLR?
JLR's recent numbers help explain the urgency. In FY26, it recorded revenue of around GBP 23 billion, but its adjusted EBIT margin was only 0.7 percent. Its free cash flow was negative by about GBP 2.2 billion.
This was a sharp contrast to Q4 FY26, when operations recovered enough to deliver a 9.2 percent EBIT margin and GBP 829 million of positive free cash flow. The business can make money, but its results have become unpredictable.
Some of the problems were temporary. A cyber incident disrupted production in September 2025 and continued affecting the following quarter. Management estimated that the incident cost around 50,000 vehicles in production during Q3 FY26.
More from the author: Could The End Of The Middle East War Be L&T's Biggest Growth Trigger?
US tariffs, supply disruptions and the run-down of old Jaguar models added further pressure. Yet other problems, including tougher competition, higher costs and weaker Chinese demand, may not disappear as quickly.
This explains why management is pursuing two goals together. It wants double-digit annual revenue growth, but also wants to reduce how many vehicles JLR must sell before its cash costs are covered.
Simply increasing sales is not enough if every new model needs enormous investment and every slowdown pushes the company back into losses.
A key part of the answer is selling a richer mix of vehicles. Range Rover, Range Rover Sport and Defender have been JLR's strongest products. In Q1 FY26, these three accounted for more than 77 percent of wholesale volumes, while average revenue per vehicle reached around GBP 76,000.
Management believes that new high-end launches can push this figure above GBP 80,000 over time. The idea is not necessarily to sell the greatest possible number of cars, but to earn more from the cars it does sell.
A New Jaguar And An Electric Range Rover
The clearest example is Jaguar. Rather than continuing with its older range of sedans and SUVs, JLR has been winding down those models and rebuilding the brand around an entirely new product. With its new Jaguar Type 01, the company wants to enter a more expensive segment of the electric luxury car market.
That creates both an opportunity and a risk. A successful new Jaguar could give JLR a stronger position in a higher-priced segment. But withdrawing older models means accepting lower sales today in the hope of better sales and pricing later.
In H1 FY27, Jaguar wholesales fell to just 1,600 vehicles from 3,900 a year earlier. Management reported about 370,000 online configurations of the Type 01 after its reveal, but interest in designing a car online is not the same as confirmed orders or delivered vehicles.
Meanwhile, JLR is using the better-established Range Rover name to enter the luxury electric market. It introduced the Range Rover Electric and Range Rover Sport Electric during Q2 FY27, with vehicles expected to reach showrooms from December.
Together, they had attracted roughly 4,300 orders by the latest results. Another new model, the Range Rover GT, is planned to arrive as an electric vehicle, with a hybrid version to follow later.
The wider plan is not to abandon petrol and hybrid vehicles overnight. JLR has acknowledged that electric-car adoption is moving at different speeds across markets. It is therefore preparing a mix of technologies, including hybrid options for future models, rather than assuming that every luxury buyer is ready to switch to a fully electric car.
Importantly, these launches must do more than make the brand look modern. JLR has announced a five-year investment programme of roughly GBP 15-18 billion, and by Q2 FY27 management said GBP 11.5 billion had already been invested.
Much of this spending is tied to vehicles only now approaching customers. The financial returns remain largely ahead.
Why America Matters More As China Struggles
The next change is geographical. China was once an important source of high-value demand for JLR, but that market has become much harder. In Q2 FY27, JLR's China wholesales fell roughly 45 percent year-on-year.
Management blamed pressure on luxury demand, local competition and changes in taxation, while noting that Chinese manufacturers were taking share from established international brands.
JLR's response is significant. Local production through its Chinese joint venture stopped in June 2026. Instead of chasing large sales volumes there, management wants to concentrate on higher-value imported luxury models, a smaller dealer network and more personalised vehicles for wealthy customers.
More from the author: Everyone Might Be Looking At The Wrong FMCG Stocks
At the same time, it has licensed the Freelander brand to its partner Chery, giving it another way to participate in China. JLR expects licence income from this arrangement rather than consolidating the partner's entire vehicle revenue.
That does not mean Tata is giving up on China. Management has explicitly said the country remains important, while acknowledging that it needs time to understand whether the changes are temporary or lasting. But relying on China to deliver the growth it once did would be increasingly risky.
America, on the other hand, is becoming a major focus. JLR's North American wholesale volumes grew 20 percent year-on-year in H1 FY27, and the region represented around a third of global wholesales in Q2. Management sees an opportunity in wealthy customers who favour large SUVs, particularly Range Rover and Defender.
Its American plans go beyond advertisements or new showrooms. They include better availability of vehicles, launches timed around local buying patterns, stronger after-sales service and more personalisation.
A new bespoke studio is planned for North America in the calendar year 2027. These details matter because luxury buyers expect a premium experience long after paying for the car.
Still, shifting focus to America does not remove all the problems. Tariffs can affect prices, incentives can reduce margins and even wealthy customers can delay purchases. Success will depend on what JLR earns per vehicle, not just the number shipped to American dealers.
The GBP 1.7 Billion Plan To Cut Costs
Selling more expensive cars is only half the strategy. JLR is also trying to make the business cheaper to run. Management says the number of vehicles needed to cover cash costs rose from around 345,000 in FY25 to 425,000 in FY26. That leaves little room for error when full-year wholesales were about 308,000 vehicles in FY26.
Its goal is to bring this cash break-even level back towards 300,000 vehicles within two years. To get there, JLR is targeting GBP 1.7 billion in savings compared with FY26.
Of that, GBP 625 million is expected from lower material, manufacturing and logistics costs; another GBP 625 million from reducing warranty-related spending; and GBP 450 million from wider operating efficiencies.
Warranty costs are another area JLR wants to improve. Luxury cars are expensive to repair, and problems with quality can reduce the profit earned from each vehicle. JLR wants to lower these costs by improving how it handles repairs, fixing problems earlier and recovering more money from suppliers when faulty parts cause issues.
Stock target: Small Cap stock to Buy Now for an Upside of 26%; Recommended by Trade Brains Portal
The hardest part involves people. Management aims to reduce salaried headcount by around 4,000 through voluntary departures. In the latest earnings call, it expected roughly 3,000 departures during FY27 and the remaining 1,000 in the following year.
Management estimates these reductions could eventually save about GBP 400 million annually, although not all the benefits will show directly in the profit and loss account because some engineering expenses would otherwise have been capitalised.
These decisions are already affecting reported results. JLR booked a GBP 530 million exceptional charge in Q2 FY27, including GBP 295 million connected with the voluntary redundancy programme. Cutting costs today therefore carries a bill of its own, even if it creates savings later.
Why Are The Financial Numbers Still So Weak?
JLR's latest results show why the turnaround cannot be judged by launch announcements alone. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.3 percent year-on-year to GBP 5.9 billion, but that comparison was against a quarter disrupted by the cyber incident. Compared with Q1 FY27, revenue actually slipped 1.3 percent even though wholesale volumes increased.
More importantly, adjusted EBIT margin fell from 2.8 percent in Q1 to 1.1 percent in Q2. Profit before tax and exceptional items dropped from GBP 109 million to just GBP 6 million. After exceptional charges and tax, JLR reported a GBP 451 million loss for the quarter.
The problem was largely what JLR sold and where it sold it. Deliveries shifted away from higher-margin China and Middle East markets, while the share of less profitable Discovery vehicles increased.
Sales incentives also rose, with variable marketing expenses increasing from 7.6 percent to 8.2 percent between the two quarters. More vehicles do not automatically mean more profit if the company must offer discounts or sells a weaker mix of models.
Cash is an equally important warning sign. JLR spent GBP 1.77 billion on investment during H1 FY27 and recorded negative free cash flow of approximately GBP 1.54 billion. Its net debt reached around GBP 4.2 billion by September 2026.
At the wider Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles group, net debt stood at roughly Rs. 50,800 crore, although the Indian passenger-vehicle business remained in a net cash position.
The company is not without financial flexibility. JLR reported around GBP 6 billion in total liquidity at the end of September, including cash and available borrowing facilities. But the difference between having access to funds and generating cash from operations is crucial. Borrowing can help finance new launches; it cannot permanently replace profits from selling cars.
Can Tata's Plan Finally Pay Off?
Management has already revised its financial expectations for FY27. It now forecasts around GBP 25 billion in revenue, an adjusted EBIT margin of 2-3 percent and negative free cash flow of approximately GBP 1.25 billion. For FY28, the goal is a double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin and positive free cash flow, followed by a return to net cash by the end of FY30.
The logic behind those targets is understandable. Investment spending should gradually ease as new vehicles enter production, while sales of the electric Range Rovers, Jaguar Type 01 and other upcoming models could lift revenue. Savings from lower manufacturing, warranty and staff costs should help more of that revenue turn into cash.
More from the author: Can Hyundai's New Bayon And Creta Drive Its Stock Back Towards Highs?

evidence.title: PB Balaji drove Tata Motors out of debt. JLR is dragging it back in
evidence.text:
P.B. Balaji made his name driving debt reduction at Tata Motors Ltd before its demerger. A year into his role as chief executive of British luxury carmaker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), debt is back.
In 2025, Tata Sons chairman Natarajan Chandrasekaran held up Tata Motors’ turnaround, from ₹62,000 crore of debt in 2017 to a net cash position, as an example of what the conglomerate could achieve. Much of it happened under Balaji, the automaker’s chief financial officer for nearly eight years.
The tables have turned. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd is back in debt, burning cash, and facing mounting pressure on profitability, largely due to its British subsidiary.
Balaji completes his first year as JLR’s CEO on Tuesday. He has tightened financial controls, restructured the leadership team and launched an aggressive cost-cutting programme, but the business is yet to arrest its decline.
Investors have taken note. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles shares fell as much as 9% on Monday after JLR cut its full-year earnings guidance on Friday, having already set a target in June that fell well short of its near-term goal.
A JLR spokesperson said Balaji outlined the strategy focused on growth and resilience in June. “We are targeting medium-term double-digit revenue growth by leveraging our House of Brands, providing greater propulsion choice and increasing our focus on North America, where we see significant growth potential,” the spokesperson said.
“With three new luxury electric vehicles recently unveiled and two more launching next year, alongside approximately £1.7 billion of targeted savings over two years through our Enterprise Missions to reduce breakeven point to 300,000 units, we are focused on returning to double-digit Ebitda margins and positive cash flow from FY28,” the spokesperson added.
Sudoku management
A person familiar with the company’s workings compared Balaji’s management style to a Sudoku puzzle. It uses a “line and column” approach, where every part of the organization must explain its financial results.
“Control the purse and squeeze the money” has become JLR’s underlying philosophy under Balaji, the executive said on condition of anonymity. For executives at the luxury car maker, international travel is on hold unless essential; vendors are being pressed for discounts, and employee costs are being cut.
Balaji believes most management problems ultimately come down to financial health, the person added.
That reflects his background. The 57-year-old IIT-Madras and IIM-Calcutta alumnus began his career at Unilever Plc in 1995, holding finance and supply-chain roles across several countries. He was CFO of Hindustan Unilever Ltd before joining Tata Motors as group CFO in November 2017. In November 2025, he became the first Indian to lead JLR.
The question is whether controlling costs alone can save a luxury carmaker struggling with low demand, product quality issues, and intensifying competition.
“JLR was facing challenges when Balaji took over. The continuously declining trajectory has not been arrested. A year later, one can say cold has become pneumonia for the brand,” the executive said.
Finances
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles’ consolidated net debt rose to ₹50,800 crore at the end of September, from ₹30,700 crore at the end of fiscal year 2025-26 (FY26), largely driven by JLR. The British carmaker accounted for ₹53,000 crore of net debt, while TML Holdings had another ₹6,000 crore. These were partly offset by ₹7,900 crore in net cash at the domestic passenger vehicle business and ₹300 crore at other entities.
Operations gave little hope. JLR’s revenue for the September quarter rose 20.3% to £5.9 billion, partly because the year-ago quarter was affected by a cyberattack that stopped production. But its adjusted profit margin fell to 1.1% from 2.8% in the June quarter. It reported a net loss of £451 million, compared to £559 million a year ago, hurt by £530 million in special restructuring costs.
JLR’s forecast has also dropped. Its FY27 profit margin prediction has fallen from about 4% earlier this year to 2-3%, far below its short-term goal of 10%. It also lowered its revenue forecast to £25 billion from £26 billion.
Cash has been even harder to achieve. JLR had earlier said it aimed to break even on cash in FY27. It now expects to spend about £1.25 billion more than it earns this year, following £540 million in spending in the September quarter alone.
Balaji’s tenure also saw a major US recall of more than 170,000 vehicles over a defect that could cause a complete loss of drive power, adding to concerns about customer confidence.
Cuts, and their limits
JLR has responded with a £1.7 billion cost-saving plan over two years, focusing on material costs, warranty expenses, and fixed costs. It is also reducing staff and controlling purchases to lower its break-even volume to about 300,000 vehicles over the next two years.
However, that may not be enough. “In luxury automotive, efficiency protects margins, but desirability creates them. Customers pay a premium for a Range Rover or Defender because they want the product, not because JLR has a lean cost structure,” said Vinay Piparsania, founder of MillenStrat Advisory and Research and a former Ford India executive.
JLR needs to protect its flagship products, rebuild competitiveness in markets where it is losing ground, and make its Jaguar reinvention and its electric vehicle and software offerings compelling, Piparsania said.
“JLR doesn’t just need to become leaner. It needs to become more desirable, more competitive and better executed. Cost discipline can steady the ship; only products and brands that customers truly desire can restore sustainable growth and margins.”
The challenges go beyond JLR’s own costs. In a 15 November note, Elara Capital pointed out weak global demand and growing competition from Chinese brands in the luxury market.
A new top team
Balaji has also tried to simplify decision-making, creating an executive committee in April that gives the leadership team more freedom to operate. Senior leaders who left include chief creative officer Gerry McGovern and chief strategy officer Swarna Ramanathan. He has hired Balaje Rajan as group chief strategy officer and Naveen Krishna as chief information and digital officer.
JLR is counting on new launches and savings to repair its finances, targeting double-digit Ebitda and positive free cash flow in FY28. Ebitda is short for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization.
But he must now translate tighter financial controls into a sustained turnaround at JLR. As the person familiar with the company put it: “The troika of Balaji, Rajan and Naveen Krishna, who are believed to be running the company, are up for the challenge of their lives.”

evidence.title: Tata Motors Crashes 9%: Rs 5,451 crore loss to JLR guidance cut; 4 brokerages reduce targets
evidence.text:
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) shares cracked 9 per cent intraday on Monday, November 16, after automobile firm disappointed investors and analysts in the July-September quarter of FY27 with a net loss of Rs 5,451 crore, against expectations of a profit of around Rs 1,700 crore.
Margins at both Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) and the India passenger vehicle business came in below estimates.
TMPV shares traded 8.54 per cent lower Rs 262 per share at noon.
TMPV last week reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the quarter ended September 30. The loss included a one-time charge in exceptional charges worth Rs 6,738 crore. For the corresponding period a year ago, the Tata group PV business had registered a net profit of Rs 76,170 crore.
Its consolidated revenue grew 34.3 per cent on a year-on-year basis to Rs 96,340 crore, according to a regulatory filing.
TMPV said that despite strong growth, margins continue to be compressed on account of adverse commodities and forex impact.
It also noted that global geopolitical volatilities, luxury segment demand trends, pace of EV adoption and commodity costs continue to be key monitorables.
On a standalone basis, TMPV recorded its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 20,423 crore, marking a 50.9 per cent year-on-year rise.
A cyberattack disrupted production at sales in Tata Motors PV's British unit, Jaguar Land Rover (JLR), last year. Analysts view subsidiary JLR's performance as critical to the carmaker's profitability.
JLR's standalone revenue rose 20.3 per cent on year to 5.9 billion British pounds. Its EBITDA margin stood at 6.6 per cent.
Tata Motors PV said that for JLR, near-term focus areas will be to build sales momentum from new EV launches and demonstrate meaningful progress in enterprise missions plan.
The businesses, it noted, are focused on executing the long-term strategic plans.
Jaguar Land Rover has lowered its full-year FY27 guidance, citing rising geopolitical risks and higher restructuring costs.
The luxury carmaker has revised its revenue guidance to 25 billion pounds from the earlier estimate of 26 billion pounds.
It has also lowered its pre-tax margin outlook to 2-3 per cent from 4 per cent. The company's free cash flow (FCF) guidance has been cut from breakeven to negative 1.25 billion pounds.
The revised outlook reflects the challenges facing the business, with weaker-than-expected operating performance adding to pressure on its financial estimates.
Margins in India's passenger vehicle business also remained below market expectations.
Following the weak quarterly performance and JLR's revised guidance, brokerages have lowered their earnings estimates and target prices for Tata Motors.
Brokerages have cut their FY27 EBITDA estimates by around 20 per cent and FY28 estimates by 11 per cent.
Citi: Maintains a 'Sell' rating and cuts the target price to Rs 235 from Rs 270.
Jefferies: Maintains an 'Underperform' rating and reduces the target price to Rs 240 from Rs 290.
Morgan Stanley: Maintains an 'Equal-weight' rating and cuts the target price to Rs 273 from Rs 367.
CLSA: Maintains an 'Accumulate' rating and lowers the target price to Rs 369 from Rs 452.
The reduction in earnings estimates reflects concerns over weaker margins, JLR's revised business outlook and the pressure on operating performance.
Despite the near-term challenges, the outlook for FY28 appears relatively better, with expectations of an improvement in profitability and free cash flow.
The launch of new electric passenger vehicles is also expected to support the company's growth prospects and strengthen its position in the electric vehicle market.

Tata Motors stock faces Nomura target cut after weak results
Published on 11/20/2026 at 02:53 | Editorial responsibility: Rafael Müller, Editor-in-Chief AD HOC NEWSAnalyst trims outlook after results
- Nomura retained its Neutral rating after Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles missed estimates in the second quarter.
- Jaguar Land Rover lowered its fiscal-year revenue and operating-margin outlook.
- India's passenger-vehicle business continues to report strong demand for electric and CNG models.
Nomura lowered its Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles target price to 287 rupees on November 17, 2026, while retaining a Neutral rating, according to Moneycontrol. The brokerage cited pressure on margins at Jaguar Land Rover and the India passenger-vehicle business after the second-quarter performance missed its estimates.
Nomura flags margin pressure
Nomura said Jaguar Land Rover's EBIT margin was 1.1%, compared with its 2.6% estimate, while Tata Motors' India passenger-vehicle EBITDA margin was 3.9%, below the brokerage's 4.6% forecast. Jaguar Land Rover's average selling price fell 5.2% sequentially to 71,500 pounds, while its EBITDA margin declined to 6.6%.
Jaguar Land Rover cut fiscal-year revenue guidance to 25 billion pounds from 26 billion pounds and reduced EBIT-margin guidance to 2-3% from 4%. Free cash flow is now projected at negative 1.25 billion pounds, compared with the earlier breakeven outlook. Management expects five new vehicle launches over the next 18 months and is targeting 1.7 billion pounds in cost savings.
India business remains a counterweight
Nomura reported India passenger-vehicle revenue of 210 billion rupees, up 53% year over year, while EBITDA rose 4% to 8.2 billion rupees. Electric vehicles represented 30% of bookings, and planned monthly EV production is set to rise from 16,000 to 20,000 units. Commodity costs are expected to remain elevated in the third quarter of fiscal 2027.
Tata Motors' mobility portfolio
Tata Motors develops vehicles and integrated smart e-mobility solutions, with a global presence and operations spanning passenger and commercial mobility. Its portfolio includes conventional, electric and connected mobility products. In India, it competes with Maruti Suzuki, Mahindra & Mahindra and Hyundai Motor India among the country's major vehicle manufacturers.

evidence.title: JSW Motors To Displace Tata Motors As Biggest Exhibitor At Bharat Mobility Expo 2027
evidence.text:
JSW Group could have a bigger presence than Tata Motors at Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027. According to a Financial Express report citing industry sources, the group is likely to occupy Hall 1 and assemble its different automotive businesses in a pavilion that could be larger than Tata's display at the previous edition.
That would be a major statement from a group still building its identity as an automotive manufacturer. But there is an important distinction: the exhibitor plan has been reported, not formally confirmed. Also, a large display is also not the same thing as being the country's largest carmaker. Tata already has an extensive passenger-vehicle business, while JSW is preparing to introduce products under its own brand.
A Bigger Pavilion Than Tata's
The 2027 expo is scheduled for February 4-9 at Bharat Mandapam and Yashobhoomi in New Delhi. Tata Motors occupied approximately 6,000 square metres at the 2025 edition, making its pavilion one of the largest. JSW is now reportedly aiming for an even larger footprint.
The size is easier to understand when one considers that JSW would not be displaying cars from a single manufacturer. Its automotive interests cover several distinct businesses, ranging from mass-market and premium passenger vehicles to commercial electric transport. Bringing them together can quickly fill a large hall.
Three Businesses Under One Roof
First is JSW MG Motor India, the joint venture behind MG's passenger vehicles. That part of the display could include existing models as well as upcoming cars, with MG's more premium Select retail channel also expected to feature. Models such as the M9 and Cyberster have already given MG a presence beyond mainstream SUVs.
Second is JSW Motors, the group's separate passenger-vehicle venture. This brand is not the same business as JSW MG Motor India. It is preparing its own line-up, with an SUV based on the Jetour T2 among the products previously linked to its plans. Reports suggest that at least four vehicles could be shown under the JSW Motors umbrella at the expo, although the exact line-up remains unconfirmed.
Third is JSW Greentech, which is working in commercial mobility. The proposed exhibit could include electric buses and trucks, potentially giving the hall a very different character from a conventional car stand. A large electric bus occupies substantially more floor space than a passenger car, so the total area alone can be misleading as a comparison between brands.
Why JSW Wants Such A Big Stage
For an established manufacturer, a motor show provides an opportunity to reveal new models. For a new manufacturer, it does something more basic: it tells dealers, component suppliers, investors and prospective customers that the business intends to stay. JSW has ambitious localisation and product plans, and the expo offers a chance to put its different projects in one place.
That matters because a new nameplate has a lot to prove. Buyers need confidence in its cars, after-sales network, spare-parts availability and long-term support. An impressive stand can attract attention, but the harder work begins when those vehicles reach showrooms. The more interesting questions will concern actual prices, delivery dates, local manufacturing content and service coverage.
What About Volkswagen?
The Financial Express report also raises the possibility of Volkswagen vehicles appearing if a proposed JSW partnership with the German manufacturer is finalised in time. That is a conditional possibility, not confirmation that an agreement has been signed or that any specific Volkswagen will be displayed. It would be premature to build the event's story around that prospect.
An Expo With A Broader Brief
Bharat Mobility Global Expo is no longer just a traditional passenger-car exhibition. The organisers expect more than 1,750 exhibitors across 11 concurrent shows, covering batteries, components, commercial vehicles, mobility technology and other transport sectors. That wider format favours industrial groups with businesses spanning several categories.
JSW's potential move into the biggest pavilion would certainly be symbolic. Tata Motors has traditionally been one of the event's most prominent participants, and a newcomer taking more space would attract plenty of attention.

evidence.title: Tata's 5 Upcoming Electric Cars: Safari.EV To Kuno
evidence.text:
Tata Motors is currently one of the biggest electric car manufacturers in India. The company has managed to capture around 40 percent of the electric passenger vehicle market. However, despite already having multiple electric cars in its portfolio, Tata Motors is now getting ready to launch more new EV models. So, without any more wastage of your time, here’s a look at five upcoming electric cars from Tata Motors.
Tata Safari.ev - New 7-Seater Electric SUV
First on this list is the Tata Safari.ev, which is expected to launch in January 2027. It is expected to be offered in both 6-seater and 7-seater configurations. And the SUV will be based on Tata's Acti.ev+ platform, which is already being used by the Harrier.ev.
Now, coming to the battery options, the Safari EV could get 65 kWh and 75 kWh battery packs from the Harrier EV. However, reports suggest that Tata could also introduce a larger 80 kWh battery pack with the top variants. Currently, the Harrier.ev with its 75 kWh battery offers a claimed range of 627 km in RWD and 622 km in AWD configurations.
Mechanically, the Safari.ev could also borrow the Harrier.ev's electric motors. Its RWD version produces 238 PS and 315 Nm. Meanwhile, the AWD version offers 504 Nm of torque. On the inside, the Safari.ev is expected to get a triple-screen dashboard, panoramic sunroof, ventilated seats, Level 2 ADAS and a 540-degree camera. As for pricing, it could start at around Rs 20 lakh and go up to Rs 32 lakh (ex-showroom).
Tata Avinya X - New Premium Electric SUV
Next on this list is the Tata Avinya X, which is expected to launch in 2027. This will reportedly be the first production model under Tata's premium Avinya electric vehicle brand. Tata Motors has recently confirmed that its upcoming Avinya range will use the E0X platform, which is associated with the Chery-JLR Freelander EV programme.
Recently, a camouflaged Exeed Sterra ET SUV was spotted testing in India. Although initially it was believed to be an Avinya prototype, reports later clarified that Tata was using this vehicle to test the underlying architecture. For those who may not be aware, the Sterra ET uses an 800V electrical architecture in its electric version and supports battery packs of up to 100 kWh.
It also offers a claimed range of up to 760 km under the Chinese CLTC testing cycle. However, these are specifications of the Exeed SUV and not the upcoming Avinya X. Presently, Tata has not revealed the battery, range or motor specifications of its new premium electric SUV.
Tata Kuno - New Rival For MG Windsor EV
The third electric SUV on this list is an entirely new model which Tata Motors is reportedly developing under the codename Kuno. This upcoming SUV will measure around 4.3 metres in length. And it will be positioned between the next-generation Nexon.ev and Sierra.ev. Its main rival will be the MG Windsor EV, which measures 4,295 mm in length.
Tata is developing this SUV with a focus on interior space, rear-seat comfort and practicality. It is expected to use the Acti.ev platform and could get a conventional SUV design instead of the coupe-like roofline of the Curvv.ev. Moving inside, it could offer a large touchscreen, digital instrument cluster, panoramic sunroof and Level 2 ADAS.
As for the battery, Tata has not revealed any specifications. However, reports suggest that the company could target a claimed range of more than 450 km. Kuno could be manufactured at Sanand in Gujarat, with a planned annual production capacity of 80,000 to 1 lakh units. It is expected to launch between 2027 and 2028. And its prices could range from Rs 17 lakh to Rs 25 lakh (ex-showroom).
Next-Generation Tata Nexon.ev - New Design And Bigger Battery
Next on this list is the next-generation Tata Nexon.ev, which has recently been spotted testing for the first time. The new Nexon project is internally codenamed Garud and is expected to launch in 2027. The new electric version was also recently spotted being transported on a flatbed truck. And its battery enclosure and orange high-voltage cables were visible underneath.
The upcoming Nexon.ev is expected to use the new ATLAS platform, which is a heavily re-engineered version of the existing X1 architecture. Design-wise, the SUV will get a flatter roofline, a more upright tailgate and revised body proportions. These changes could also improve the rear-seat headroom and boot space.
Now, coming to the battery, the current Nexon.ev gets 30 kWh and 45 kWh options. The larger battery offers a claimed range of up to 489 km. Tata, however, could introduce a bigger battery with the next-generation model. The new Nexon.ev is expected to arrive sometime in 2027.
Tata Curvv.ev Facelift - More Features And Range
Finally, the last electric car on this list is the Tata Curvv.ev facelift. Reports suggest that Tata Motors could introduce an updated version of its electric SUV-coupe towards the end of 2027. However, the company has not officially confirmed this update.
In terms of design, the facelift could get redesigned bumpers, revised LED lighting, new alloy wheels and additional exterior colours. Meanwhile, the interior could offer updated cabin materials, an improved infotainment system and additional features. Tata could also upgrade its Level 2 ADAS suite.
Mechanically, the current Curvv.ev SeriesX version gets a 55 kWh battery pack, which offers a claimed range of 502 km. This version starts at Rs 16.99 lakh (ex-showroom). However, reports suggest that Tata could introduce a larger 65 kWh battery pack with the facelift.

evidence.title: Tata Power ramps up marketing investments as it looks to build a consumer-facing energy solutions business
evidence.text:
- Marketing
- 9 min read
Tata Power ramps up marketing investments as it looks to build a consumer-facing energy solutions business
                    Despite increasing awareness about rooftop solar technology in India, many remain hesitant to install it. Tata Power recognizes this gap and is stepping up its marketing and education initiatives. The company aims to demystify the buying experience and enhance financial accessibility, thereby solidifying its position and expanding its share in the ever-evolving solar sector.
                                    
            
        Highlights
- 57 per cent of households aware but only 1.4 per cent completed installations.
- Tata Power shifts to omnichannel marketing strategy for rooftop solar.
- Financing options crucial for bridging the rooftop solar adoption gap.
                    
                    
                    
                                        For a category where awareness does not necessarily translate into adoption, the marketing challenge goes beyond building brand recall. Rooftop solar companies must first help consumers understand the technology, its savings potential and the installation process before convincing them to choose a particular provider.
A pan-India survey by the Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW), covering 17,094 households across 21 states and one Union Territory, highlights this conversion gap. While 57 per cent of households had specific awareness of residential rooftop solar, only 26 per cent of the total sample was willing to consider adoption. Just 5 per cent had initiated the installation process and 1.4 per cent had completed it. The study found that 71 per cent of households that were aware and willing to adopt had not taken the first step, largely due to a lack of accessible and trusted guidance. Affordability remains another barrier, with 73 per cent of households that perceived rooftop solar as expensive unaware of available financing options.
The market opportunity, however, is expanding. Under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, 65.26 lakh households had benefited from rooftop solar installations by November 2, 2026, with 19.1 GW of capacity commissioned. Tata Power's rooftop solar business had crossed 5.75 lakh cumulative installations by October 2026.
Against this backdrop, Tata Power is ramping up marketing investments across its consumer-facing businesses as it looks to move beyond its traditional identity as an electricity utility and establish itself as a broader energy solutions brand.
Jyoti Bansal, chief - brand and communications, Tata Power, said the company's marketing approach has evolved alongside its business transformation. Television, print, digital, social media, public relations and on-ground activations now form part of a broader omnichannel strategy, with investments across rooftop solar, electric vehicle (EV) charging and smart home automation ramped up over the last few years.
Bansal said, "we were not an advertising-oriented organisation earlier. A lot of our visibility used to come from PR, earned media and social visibility. Now, our mindset, DNA and internal thinking are moving towards becoming a customer-facing organisation and behaving like one. Hence, the marketing mix has expanded to include an omnichannel approach.”
The company's traditional and digital media investments are now broadly in the 50:50 range, according to Bansal, although the overall mix also includes ground-level activities. Tata Power continues to use print because its products often require explanation, while digital has assumed a larger role in line with changing consumer media consumption.
Its marketing presence has also expanded to include podcasts, radio, moment marketing, topical campaigns and activations at large festivals and public gatherings. The company revamped its website around two years ago and is increasingly adopting consumer-facing communication formats. The transition is also reflected in campaign frequency. While Tata Power earlier undertook approximately one large consumer-facing campaign annually, these have become more regular and are expected to increase further over the next two to three years.
Bringing diverse businesses under one brand proposition
The shift in marketing is part of a larger effort to bring Tata Power's diverse consumer offerings under a common brand proposition. The company began building out its consumer brands a few years ago, moving beyond its earlier positioning as a utility-focused organisation.
Its portfolio now spans rooftop solar and battery storage, EV charging solutions under EZ Charge and smart home automation products under Easy Home.
Bansal said Tata Power first established its corporate master brand through the proposition 'Sustainable is Attainable', positioning the company as a renewable energy-led business making sustainable choices accessible to consumers. It subsequently introduced 'Lifelong' to create a common thread across its businesses, reflecting the long-term nature of its products and service requirements.
The proposition connects the consumer journey from product consideration and purchase to usage and after-sales service, while bringing together solutions such as rooftop solar, battery storage, EV charging and smart home automation. It also extends Tata Power's historical promise of reliable electricity to a wider energy ecosystem.
With businesses catering to different audiences, marketing budgets are allocated based on category growth, market share and consumer potential, alongside platform reach, costs and the ability to drive awareness, consideration and enquiries.
Tata Power's influencer strategy also goes beyond celebrities and social media creators to include existing customers, trusted individuals and industry-body members. The company has experimented with conventional social media influencer partnerships on a limited scale, with some success in driving engagement.
It has also entered the microdrama format with a six-episode series on rooftop solar, using longer narratives to address consumer concerns while integrating its end-to-end offering, from product quality and installation to after-sales service.
The company has also adopted a phased approach to AI, starting with small experiments before developing a smart content engine to produce content at scale, speed and accuracy while maintaining brand consistency. Bansal said the company works with multiple partners and combines AI with real-shot content, animation and other production techniques, depending on campaign objectives. The approach has helped reduce production costs and turnaround time, although conventional content creation continues to play a role. She added that the company does not use AI for its own sake, but where it is relevant.
From savings-led messaging to category education
Bansal said the company's early campaigns focused on financial savings, with its first campaign, 'Save Here, Spend There', highlighting how lower electricity bills could free up money for other aspirations. Its messaging has since evolved to combine rational benefits with emotional storytelling through the 'Lifelong' proposition.
"In a category like this, while the rational benefit is very important, it is also important to create a place for the brand in the consumer's life. Otherwise, it becomes a very transactional approach. We have now evolved towards communicating emotionally and layering that with the rational," Bansal said.
She said the bigger challenge remains educating consumers about rooftop solar, its benefits and the installation process, rather than simply building preference for Tata Power. The company launched its 'Solar is Simple' social media series to explain the category, address misconceptions and make the adoption process easier to understand.
Residential rooftop solar demand has grown considerably over the last three years following the introduction of the PM Surya Ghar scheme. Demand is also emerging from the MSME segment, where rising electricity consumption and costs are making solar an attractive proposition. Bansal expects the category to expand further over the next five years, with Tata Power aiming to capture more than its fair share of growth.
The company's rooftop solar business reported revenue of Rs 1,356 crore in Q2 FY27, up 20 per cent year on year. It added 426 MWp of capacity during the quarter, a 15 per cent increase, while installations rose 33 per cent to 88,397.
At the consolidated level, Tata Power reported revenue of Rs 19,886 crore in Q2 FY27, up 26 per cent year on year, while reported profit after tax rose 33 per cent to Rs 1,652 crore. The company had completed 5,19,673 rooftop solar installations as of July 31, 2026, representing a 14 per cent market share, and is targeting 30 lakh installations by 2029.
Tier two and tier three markets gain importance
Smaller cities are an important part of this opportunity, given the availability of independent houses with rooftop space and the presence of smaller industrial and commercial establishments.
Tata Power's rooftop solar distribution network had expanded to 736 channel partners and more than 3,800 retailers as of Q2 FY27. Its new-age energy solutions portfolio has a presence across more than 700 cities and towns, according to its FY26 annual report. The company sees its distribution network as important to expanding in tier two and tier three markets, where residential and MSME demand is emerging.
Bansal said consumers who do not have the space to install rooftop solar can also explore other solutions offered by the company, allowing them to participate in the broader shift towards solar energy.
Financing and consumer hand-holding key to adoption
However, converting consumer interest into actual purchases remains a challenge. Unlike a conventional consumer product, rooftop solar involves a technical engineering solution, requiring consumers to understand the product, installation process, financial implications and long-term benefits.
Bansal said three factors will be important in accelerating adoption: making the product easier to understand, simplifying ownership and improving access to finance.
Drawing a comparison with the automobile industry, she said the availability of financing played an important role in expanding car ownership. Tata Power has consequently built what Bansal described as the widest network of financing partners among rooftop solar brands in India to improve access to finance for consumers.
She added, "the other thing is that because it is a technical solution and not just a product you buy off the shelf, some amount of understanding and hand-holding of the consumer is needed. evidence.title: TMPV share price falls as company reports loss of Rs 5,531 crore amid JLR restructuring costs
evidence.text:
Shares of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL) fell significantly on Monday, October 16, 2026, after the company reported a consolidated loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the second quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026. The stock opened at Rs 272.40, with a fall of Rs 14.6 per cent or 5.08 per cent from the previous close of Rs 287 on the BSE. It fell further to touch a low of Rs 260.50, down Rs 26.5 or 9.23 per cent. This is just Rs 1.3 or 0.50 per cent away from the 52-week low of Rs 259.20, hit on October 28, 2026. The 52-week high of the counter is Rs 408.20, touched on May 29, 2026.
Last seen, the stock was trading at Rs 263, with a fall of Rs 24 or 8.36 per cent and the market cap of the company stood at Rs 96,862.69 crore.
The counter has been losing for the last three days and has fallen 11.24 per cent in the period. It has underperformed the sector by 6.79 per cent.
Tata Motors PV quarterly results
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd (TMPVL) reported a consolidated loss of Rs 5,531 crore for the September quarter compared with a profit of Rs 76,170 crore in the year-ago period. TMPV reported exceptional items of Rs 6,738 crore, primarily comprising Rs 3,776 crore in employee separation costs and Rs 2,856 crore in asset impairment.
The company said its luxury brand Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) recorded exceptional items of £530 million in the quarter, reflecting restructuring activities, including separation costs and the write-down of intangible assets under development.
The company's consolidated revenue from operations rose 34 per cent on year to Rs 96,920 crore. The company said its EBITDA margin rose 630 basis points to 6.2 per cent during the period.
Total expenses for the quarter rose to Rs 97,827 crore from Rs 79,310 crore a year earlier, while material costs rose to Rs 58,825 crore from Rs 36,300 crore.
Share price history
The stock has corrected 17.96 per cent in 5 years and 32.83 per cent in one year. Year to date (YTD), it has dipped 28.40 per cent, compared with a 3.85 per cent fall in the benchmark index.

evidence.title: Kotak MF, BlackRock, others buy stake worth Rs 1,905 cr in Groww
evidence.text:
- Articles
- 4 min read
Kotak MF, BlackRock, others buy stake worth Rs 1,905 cr in Groww
                    Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund (MF) led the buying spree, acquiring 2.05 crore shares or a 0.33 per cent stake, for Rs 448.95 crore, making it the biggest buyer in the transaction.
                                    
            
        Domestic and global institutional investors like Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund and BlackRock increased their stake in Groww by acquiring shares worth Rs 1,905 crore, according to NSE block deal data.
The investors collectively purchased 8.70 crore equity shares, representing a 1.38 per cent stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, at an average price of Rs 219 apiece on Tuesday.
Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund (MF) led the buying spree, acquiring 2.05 crore shares or a 0.33 per cent stake, for Rs 448.95 crore, making it the biggest buyer in the transaction.
The share purchase increased Kotak MF's stake in Groww to 2.21 per cent from 1.89 per cent.
Other domestic institutional investors participating in the transaction included Tata Mutual Fund, National Pension System (NPS) Trust, and HDFC Life Insurance.
The overseas buyers included Societe Generale, BNP Paribas, Fidelity Investments, Viridian Asset Management, Susquehanna International Group, Canada's RBC Global Asset Management, Swiss banking major UBS, Morgan Stanley, and Ghisallo Capital Management.
London-based Investment management firm Redwheel, Australia's largest superannuation fund Rest Super, Teachers' Retirement System of the State of Illinois and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global were also among the buyers.
On the selling side of the deal, US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital, through two of its affiliates, offloaded 8.70 crore equity shares at the same price, as per the data.
After the latest transaction, Ribbit Capital's combined stake in Groww declined to 6.91 per cent from 8.29 per cent.
The churn in Groww's shareholding comes as its early investors continue to unlock value following the company's stock market debut in November 2025.
The latest transaction follows a series of stake sales by its early backers, who have been gradually trimming their holdings even as a wider pool of institutional investors builds exposure to the online brokerage platform.
In May this year, early investors Peak XV Partners, Ribbit Capital and Y Combinator collectively sold a 4.71 per cent stake in Groww for Rs 5,326 crore following the expiry of the six-month post-IPO lock-in period.
The stake sale continued in the following months. Early-stage startup accelerator Y Combinator divested nearly a 1.2 per cent stake for Rs 1,435 crore in August, while Ribbit Capital sold a 1 per cent stake in a transaction valued at Rs 2,217 crore during the same month.
In September, Peak XV Partners offloaded a 1.46 per cent stake in Groww for Rs 1,756 crore, reducing its holding in the firm to 14.22 per cent from 15.68 per cent.
Earlier this month, Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator and Goldman Sachs sold shares worth a combined Rs 2,457 crore, representing a 1.84 per cent stake in the company.
According to market analysts, the successive stake sales have not meant a complete departure of the early backers, who continued to hold substantial stakes at the end of the September quarter.
Peak XV Partners, through its affiliates, remained Groww's largest public shareholder with a 15.54 per cent stake in the country's largest broking firm by active investors.
Y Combinator held a combined 8.61 per cent stake, while Tiger Global Management, another early investor, owned 3.27 per cent.
Other minority public shareholders included San Francisco-based ICONIQ Capital, which held a 1.27 per cent stake, and Singapore's sovereign wealth fund GIC, with a 1.07 per cent holding.
Groww's founders and promoters also have a significant ownership position.
Co-founder, promoter and Chief Executive Officer Lalit Keshre, along with the other promoters, collectively held 27.13 per cent in Groww at the end of the September quarter.
The investor reshuffle has its roots in Groww's Rs 6,632-crore IPO, through which its parent company Billionbrains Garage Ventures went public with a fresh issue and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of over 55.72 crore shares.
Peak XV Partners was the largest seller in the OFS, offloading shares worth Rs 1,582.81 crore, followed by Ribbit Capital at Rs 1,181.32 crore and Y Combinator at Rs 1,054.82 crore.
Shares of Groww pared early gains and settled 1.66 per cent lower at Rs 223.75 apiece on the National Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

evidence.title: Mahindra to use £1 million Earthshot Prize to train women drivers, says Rajesh Jejurikar
evidence.text:
Mahindra to use £1 million Earthshot Prize to train women drivers, says Rajesh Jejurikar
- Edited byalphadesk
- Published OnNov 18, 2026 | 14:30 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 18, 2026 | 14:30 IST
Rajesh Jejurikar, Chairman, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Executive Director & CEO–Auto & Farm Sector at Mahindra & Mahindra expects electric three-wheeler penetration to rise from 40% to 70% in the next two to three years, while exploring global partnerships to expand its business.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility will deploy its £1 million Earthshot Prize funds to train and skill women electric vehicle (EV) drivers, according to Rajesh Jejurikar, Chairman of Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Executive Director and CEO of the Auto and Farm Sector at Mahindra & Mahindra.
The company recently won the environmental award in the "Clean Our Air" category, after being selected from over 7,000 nominations across 165 countries. The recognition validates the commercial viability of electric three-wheelers, a segment where the automaker has already sold more than 400,000 units. These vehicles have collectively covered 9 billion kilometers and prevented 185,000 metric tonne of carbon dioxide emissions.
Initially, customers adopted electric vehicles primarily as a cost-saving and profit-generating avenue. However, the demographic has shifted, with many women entering the category as drivers, aligning with broader empowerment goals.
"We believe that this money and these funds should be redeployed to support women drivers, encouraging and training and skilling women drivers to come into the fold," Jejurikar noted. The company plans to back non-governmental organisations to facilitate this transition and improve livelihoods, demonstrating that "it is possible to do good and create a business proposition out of that."
Beyond the immediate deployment of prize capital, the management is accelerating its broader business strategy. Current electric vehicle penetration in the category stands at about 40%, a figure projected to reach 70% over the next two to three years. This rapid adoption is expected to make it the most penetrated electric segment in the country.
The global endorsement from the Earthshot platform is also opening doors for international expansion. Suman, Chief Executive Officer of the business, has initiated discussions with multiple stakeholders regarding potential global tie-ups. Several international partners have already reached out, and the company plans to evaluate the feasibility of each opportunity to replicate its domestic impact overseas.
Addressing the company's stated target of growing electric three-wheeler volumes 25 times between 2019-20 (FY20) and 2029-30 (FY30), the chairman confirmed the trajectory remains intact, driven by the fact that "EV penetration has been very good in the three-wheeler segment."
Watch the full conversation here
Despite strong nationwide adoption, a significant growth hurdle remains in major urban centres. Penetration in metro cities lags behind the rest of the country, primarily constrained by a lack of dedicated parking space for electric vehicles. While noting that the Delhi government is taking action, the automaker is urging other state governments to address these infrastructure bottlenecks to further curb urban pollution and help achieve long-term mobility goals.

The £1 million prize money will support initiatives to create more women drivers.
Scaling and future growth
On whether the last-mile mobility now a scale business or still a build the moat business, Jejurikar said, “We think it is close to scaling. I mean it is scaled right now. We think metros is a big growth opportunity. Right now, metro penetration in India is just 5 per cent. I think it will transform the environment from a pollution standpoint by having that many more electric vehicles.”
YouTube Video Loading...
Operational strategy
“We have been making profits but the point is that the objective for the business here is to drive growth and scale and that is the overriding priority over the next few years,” Jejurikar added.
Loading social widget...
M&M Q2 results
Mahindra & Mahindra reported a standalone net profit of Rs 5,102 crore in Q2FY27. The automobile giant's net profit for the reporting quarter surged 13 per cent year-over-year from Rs 4,521 crore in Q2FY26.
The company's revenue from operations surged to 42,477 crore in Q2FY27, increasing 27 per cent YoY from Rs 33,422 crore in Q2FY26. The revenue figures of Q2FY27 beat ET Now estimates of Rs 41,372 crore.
On the operating front, the company's Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) is 2 per cent to Rs 4,912 crore in Q2FY27, below ET Now estimates of Rs 4,997 crore. However, M&M's EBITDA fell 4 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ). Its EBITDA margin contracted to 11.6 per cent in Q2FY27, as against ET NOW Poll of 12.1 per cent. 
In the same quarter a year ago, the company's EBITDA margin stood at 14.4 per cent.
On a consolidated basis, the company's net profit surged by 25 per cent YoY to Rs 4,588 crore in Q2FY27, compared to Rs 3,673 crore in Q2FY26. Its revenue from operations rose by 25 per cent as well to Rs 57,553 crore in Q2FY27, as against Rs 46,106 crore in Q2FY26.
"Auto Business delivered strong performance while Farm business continues to demonstrate strong resilience in Q2F27. SUV volume grew 26% YoY and retained market leadership in revenue market share. The EV product range continues to show momentum while maintaining #1 position in revenue market share for the 1st half of the year. Auto consolidated PBIT margin grew to 8.8%, 110 bps up QoQ and Farm consolidated PBIT margin grew 20 bps QoQ despite significant hike in commodity prices,” Jejurikar had said.

evidence.title: Want an Electric Auto? Mahindra and Uber Have a New Plan
evidence.text:
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Uber have partnered to support the adoption of 5,000 electric three-wheelers in India over the next 12 months. The initiative aims to make electric autos more accessible to drivers through better financing options and other support measures.
The partnership was revealed by the companies in Mumbai on November 16. The collaboration will be undertaken under the program named ‘EV Auto Advantage.’ This program will initially target those markets where electric vehicle usage is relatively less.
The collaboration is going to be on the basis of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU). It will help to overcome financial constraints that usually keep the commercial drivers from using electric vehicles.
Also Read: Tech Mahindra and SpaceXSI Join Hands to Modernize Enterprise Software
Under the program, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Uber will work to improve access to financing for drivers interested in purchasing electric three-wheelers. The companies will also explore other measures to make the transition easier for drivers and entrepreneurs.
Suman Mishra, Managing Director and CEO of Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, said, “Sustainable mobility will scale when it works for the driver first. By making electric mobility a better economic choice for drivers and entrepreneurs, we are creating impact that is both sustainable and scalable. Through this partnership with Uber we want to push the transition further, especially in parts of India where EV adoption remains low.”
According to Uber’s Head of Mobility Pradeep Parameswaran, electric mobility is advantageous for companies, passengers, and cities. He also emphasized the need for integration between public transit and shared mobility systems.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility said more than 4 lakh of its commercial electric vehicles are already on Indian roads. Its portfolio includes vehicles for passenger and cargo transportation.
The company is also among the finalists for the 2026 Earthshot Prize in the Clean Our Air category. The winner is scheduled to be announced in Mumbai on November 17. The partnership adds to efforts by both companies to expand electric mobility in India's last-mile transport sector.
