evidence.title: Mahindra names XUV marketing head as Neha Anand to lead farm division marketing
evidence.text:
ADVERTISEMENT
Mahindra & Mahindra has appointed Neha Anand, currently Vice President and Head of XUV Brand and International Operations Marketing, as Vice President and Head of Marketing for its Farm Division, effective December 1, 2026, as per the media sources. The appointment is part of a wider leadership reshuffle involving the company's farm marketing, machinery sales and customer experience functions.
The changes were communicated through an internal circular dated November 16, issued by Sanket Patil, Senior Vice President and Head of Human Resources for the Farm Division. Anand will report to Harsh Rai, CEO of the Farm Division and Gromax, and will become a member of the Farm Executive Council.
The restructuring comes as Mahindra looks to strengthen its marketing capabilities across tractors, farm machinery and technology, with a sharper focus on customer requirements and business execution.
Changes across marketing, sales and customer experience
As part of the changes, Parikshit Ghosh, who currently heads National Business Operations, will take on an expanded mandate covering customer experience. He will be redesignated Senior Vice President and Head of National Business Operations & Customer Experience and will continue reporting to Rai.
His expanded responsibilities will include overseeing the execution of sales plans, dealer engagement and customer servicing.
Meanwhile, Ujjwal Mukherjee, the current Head of Farm Division Marketing, will move to farm machinery sales as Senior General Manager, reporting to Ghosh. He will begin the transition on December 1, 2026, and formally assume the new position on April 1, 2027, according to the industry sources.
Ashish Kundra, currently heading farm machinery sales, has been appointed Head of Marketing for Trucks and Buses at SML Mahindra. He will also be designated Senior Management Personnel, with the appointment taking effect from April 1, 2027.
Anand's automotive and digital marketing experience
Anand's appointment brings a marketing executive with experience across automotive, technology, aviation and hospitality to the Farm Division. She joined Mahindra in 2021 and has held several leadership positions across digital marketing, public relations, global brand and communications, and international operations marketing.
Before the latest appointment, she was responsible for the XUV portfolio and international operations marketing. Her tenure in the automotive business included marketing responsibilities associated with launches such as the XUV700, Scorpio-N, XUV3XO and Thar ROXX, alongside the recently launched XUV7XO.
According to the internal communication, Anand brings over 24 years of professional experience across multiple industries.
The leadership changes come against the backdrop of Mahindra's position in the domestic tractor market. The company reported a 41.5% share of the Indian tractor market in the September quarter and sold 2.74 lakh tractors during the first half of FY27, registering growth of approximately 7% year-on-year.
However, domestic tractor sales declined 13% to 62,626 units in October. Mahindra attributed the decline primarily to the shift in Diwali celebrations to November.
The farm business leadership changes follow an earlier announcement by Mahindra on the reorganisation of its automotive business, indicating a wider series of structural changes across its business operations.

evidence.title: Mahindra Farm Machinery Launches First-in-Class 50HP Compact Harvester ‘Mahindra Harvest Yuva’
evidence.text:
Mahindra Farm Machinery Launches First-in-Class 50HP Compact Harvester ‘Mahindra Harvest Yuva’
Mahindra & Mahindra, the world’s largest tractor manufacturer by volume, has launched the Mahindra Harvest Yuva, a new first-in-class self-propelled 50HP compact harvester. Purpose-built for farmers with small and marginal landholdings, the machine is engineered to operate efficiently in regions where narrow approach roads restrict larger harvesters. Priced up to 25% (up to ₹7 lakhs) lower than larger self-propelled harvesters, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva offers a cost-effective entry point for small and mid-sized farmers as well as rural rental entrepreneurs. By accelerating harvesting operations over manual labor, it enables farmers to complete harvests on schedule, minimize weather-related crop losses, and enhance their overall income potential.
Multi-Crop Versatility and Compact Mobility:
Designed for adaptability and easy maintenance, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva features a lightweight 4-Wheel Drive (4WD) construction capable of harvesting multiple crops including paddy, wheat, soybean, and maize across both semi-wet and dry soil conditions. Equipped with an RTO-approved cutter bar available in 9.3-foot and 10.9-foot widths, a closed unloading tube, and a slim profile with an 8-foot short track width, the harvester easily navigates narrow village roads and tight field turns. Its compact cutter bar eliminates the need for repeated detachment and reattachment when moving between farms and roads, while clear front visibility ensures sharper cuts and reduced crop loss in lodged or uneven fields.
Operator Ergonomics and Advanced Harvesting Technology:
Built with operator comfort and operational efficiency in mind, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva incorporates a lower station height, a spacious platform with a co-driver seat, a self-cleaning radiator, and rear engine placement that keeps heat away from the operator during extended working hours. Additional technical highlights include hydraulic reel adjusters and prong cutters to adapt to varied crop heights and densities, along with a unique feeder reverser that allows operators to clear clogged material with the push of a lever. Furthermore, its lightweight, chain-driven mechanism with an inline front and rear wheel configuration minimizes soil compaction while preserving superior produce quality.
Leadership Perspective, Warranty, and Market Availability:
Commenting on the launch, Ravindra Shahane, Vice President & Business Head – Farm Machinery, Farm Equipment Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., stated that the Mahindra Harvest Yuva was designed from the ground up to address the unique requirements of small and mid-sized farmers, combining affordability, productivity, and reliability to improve farm economics. Powered by Mahindra’s trusted engine technology for extended operating hours and simplified servicing, the harvester comes backed by a 1-year warranty. The Mahindra Harvest Yuva is currently available for sale across key agricultural markets in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, and Uttar Pradesh.

Your fuel efficiency figures are broadly in line with what we would expect from the XUV 7XO petrol. The 5.7 kpl in the city is on the lower side, but it is not unusual for a large, heavy SUV with a turbocharged petrol engine, especially if your city driving involves heavy traffic, frequent stop-start conditions and short trips. The 12.6 kpl on the highway at 100 km/h is actually quite reasonable for this car, and suggests the engine is operating efficiently at a steady cruise.You can try a few things to improve city mileage: use the lightest possible throttle, anticipate traffic to minimise braking, and avoid idling with the air conditioning on for long periods. Also check tyre pressures regularly and keep the car well maintained. But fundamentally, this is a big, powerful petrol SUV and its fuel efficiency will never be its strongest suit. evidence.title: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility wins 2026 Earthshot Prize for clean air initiative
evidence.text:
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility has been named the winner of The Earthshot Prize 2026 in the ‘Clean Our Air’ category for its efforts to advance cleaner last-mile mobility while supporting drivers and small businesses.
Founded by Prince William, the prize money of 1 million pounds has been awarded to Mahindra Last Mile Mobility to scale its innovative solutions and drive greater impact, the company said on Tuesday.
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility has sold over 400,000 electric last-mile vehicles, helping avoid more than 185,000 metric tonnes of CO2 emissions, it added.
MLMML said it will channel the 1 million pound Earthshot Prize grant into accelerating inclusive electric mobility -- partnering with charities to train women drivers and enable access to affordable financing, working with cities to expand charging infrastructure into underserved areas, and collaborating with fellow Earthshot Finalists to take electric rickshaws to more communities.
Anish Shah, Group CEO and Managing Director, Mahindra Group, said, “Winning The Earthshot Prize is a tremendous honour and demonstration of what is possible when purpose is translated into action. We applaud Prince William’s pioneering leadership in creating a platform that recognises and accelerates solutions for our planet. Since 1945, Mahindra has sought to enable others to rise and drive positive change in communities”.
Rajesh Jejurikar, Chairman, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Ltd, and Executive Director & CEO -- Auto & Farm Sector, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd, said, “Being named as winner for The Earthshot Prize recognises a model where cleaner mobility, customer prosperity and scale can go together. It also strengthens our belief that solutions proven in India can have relevance across other markets.”
The Earthshot Prize aims to find solutions to climate change. The environmental initiative awards five winners USD 1.3 million each to expand solutions addressing climate change. Mumbai played host to the sixth Earthshot Prize Awards Night.

evidence.title: Mahindra XEV 9S Becomes India's Safest 7-seater SUV First 7-seater EV to achieve a 5-star Bharat NCAP Rating
evidence.text:
- Safety hat-trick for INGLO platform: The XEV 9S becomes the third EV on Mahindra's INGLO platform to secure a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating, following the XEV 9e and BE 6.
- A first and a best: The XEV 9S is India’s first 7-seater EV to earn the top 5-star rating, and the highest-scoring 7-seater (ICE or EV) tested to date, with 76.15 points.
Mumbai, November 17, 2026: Mahindra today announced that the XEV 9S has secured a 5-star rating under the Bharat New Car Assessment Programme (Bharat NCAP), making it India’s safest 7-seater SUV across both ICE and electric segments. It is also the first 7-seater EV in India to achieve the top rating.
The XEV 9S scored 31.15 out of 32 points in Adult Occupant Protection (AOP) and 45 out of 49 in Child Occupant Protection (COP), achieving the highest overall score of 76.15 points among all 7-seater vehicles tested under Bharat NCAP to date. The 5-star rating reinforces Mahindra's commitment to making safety a fundamental part of its SUV engineering and development philosophy.
With this result, all three Mahindra Electric Origin SUVs built on the INGLO platform have now earned 5-star Bharat NCAP ratings, further validating the platform’s robust safety engineering.
Dr Velusamy R, President, Automotive Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd. and Managing Director, Mahindra Electric Automobile Ltd. said, “We are grateful for the overwhelming response the XEV 9S has received from customers across the country. Becoming India’s No. 1 EV* reflects the trust customers have shown in the brand. The 5-star Bharat NCAP rating further strengthens that trust, assuring customers that they are choosing a vehicle that excels not only in design, performance and technology, but also in safety. We thank our customers for their continued confidence and remain committed to delivering products that exceed their expectations.”
Launched in November 2025 as “India’s Big New Electric,” the Mahindra XEV 9S combines 7-seat practicality with advanced safety features, including seven airbags, Level 2+ Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) with five radars and a vision camera, driver drowsiness detection with DOMS (Eyedentity), and Secure360 Pro with live view, recording and live communication features. This focus on occupant protection and everyday versatility has helped make it India’s best-selling electric vehicle*.
*As per wholesale volume of EV 4W PV volumes in Apr-Sep’26 (H1 FY 2027).

Mumbai: Shares of Mahindra Logistics plunged nearly 15 per cent on Monday, recording their steepest intra-day decline on record after the company announced the resignation of its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (MD & CEO) Hemant Sikka and named Mohammed Turra as his successor.
The stock fell as much as 14.5 per cent during the session after investors reacted to the leadership transition unveiled by the company on Friday.
Shares later traded 13.4 per cent lower at Rs 371.75 after hitting an intra-day low of Rs 367.60. The decline reduced the stock's gains for 2026 to around 17 per cent.

evidence.title: NSRCEL and Kotak Mahindra Bank Support 90 Women Entrepreneurs Through Startup Programme
evidence.text:
NSRCEL and Kotak Mahindra Bank Support 90 Women Entrepreneurs Through Startup Programme
New Delhi, November 16, 2026: NSRCEL at IIM Bangalore and Kotak Mahindra Bank have launched the sixth cohort of the Women Startup Program (WSP 6), supporting 90 women entrepreneurs across India. The seven-month incubation programme, powered by Kotak Bizlabs as a CSR initiative of Kotak Mahindra Bank, aims to help women founders strengthen their business models, access mentorship and prepare for sustainable growth.
The programme comes at a time when women entrepreneurs are contributing to innovation and economic development across sectors but continue to face challenges in accessing business expertise, market opportunities, mentorship and entrepreneurial networks.
Running from September 2026 to April 2027, WSP 6 follows a hybrid incubation model combining online learning sessions with practical workshops, bootcamps and exhibitions. It is designed for women founders who have developed a minimum viable product (MVP) and have started engaging with customers or generating revenue.
The programme will focus on strengthening business models, refining products and services, improving customer acquisition, developing brand identity and streamlining business operations. Participants will also receive guidance on legal compliance, team building, sustainable business practices, business planning and investor readiness.
The sixth cohort brings together women-led ventures from different regions and city tiers, representing a range of industries. The programme also aims to encourage peer learning, knowledge exchange and networking opportunities among participating entrepreneurs.
As part of the initiative, NSRCEL, under the Women Startup Program powered by Kotak BizLabs, organised Capital Connect: Investing in Women-Led Businesses, an investor roundtable and founder–investor networking session. The event brought together venture capital firms, including Kalaari Capital, Blume Ventures, Prosperity7 Ventures, WeWin VC, Multiply Ventures, LVX Ventures, Upaya Social Ventures and AudTen Ventures, along with other ecosystem participants.
The session provided an opportunity for founders and investors to discuss investment expectations, business fundamentals and the support required by women entrepreneurs to prepare for fundraising and business expansion.
Discussions during the roundtable highlighted five key considerations for entrepreneurs: founder capabilities and adaptability, strong business fundamentals, alignment with investors beyond valuation, opportunities for businesses from Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, and incubation support tailored to individual business requirements.
The discussions also emphasised the importance of customer validation, financial discipline, sustainable business models and effective distribution strategies before approaching investors.
Commenting on the programme, Rasika Prashant, CEO, NSRCEL, said, “Women entrepreneurs have a vital role to play in shaping India’s growth story. Beyond building businesses, they create jobs, strengthen the economy and drive positive social change. Through the sixth cohort of the Women Startup Program, we aim to equip women founders with the knowledge, skills and networks to build strong, sustainable businesses and scale their impact. By supporting women-led enterprises, we are investing in a stronger, more inclusive and prosperous India.”
Himanshu Nivsarkar, Head – ESG & CSR, Kotak Mahindra Bank, said, “At Kotak, we see women’s entrepreneurship as a powerful catalyst for change, creating a multiplier effect across communities and local economies. Through the Women Startup Program under Kotak Bizlabs, we aim to bridge gaps in access to knowledge, funder network and growth opportunities, enabling women founders across diverse backgrounds and geographies to realise their entrepreneurial ambitions. We are pleased to partner with NSRCEL to support women entrepreneurs as they build, scale and prepare for their next stage of growth.”
The Women Startup Program follows a four-stage support structure comprising Foundations of Entrepreneurship, Pre-Incubation, Incubation and Scale Hub. Through these stages, the initiative seeks to provide women entrepreneurs with structured support at different points in their business journeys.
With the sixth cohort, Kotak Mahindra Bank and NSRCEL aim to strengthen the entrepreneurial ecosystem for women-led businesses by expanding access to mentorship, business knowledge, investor networks and growth opportunities.

evidence.title: Mahindra Farm Machinery launches new first in class Self-propelled 50HP Compact Harvester – MAHINDRA HARVEST YUVA
evidence.text:
Mahindra & Mahindra, the world's largest tractor manufacturer by volume and one of India's largest farm equipment manufacturers, has launched a new compact harvester, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva. Purpose-built for farmers with small and marginal landholdings, the new Mahindra Harvest Yuva is designed for operations in regions where narrow approach roads restrict the use of larger harvesters. Affordable, adaptable, and easy to operate and maintain, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva is characterized by its compact size, lightweight construction, easy manoeuvrability, and specialty to harvest multiple crops. These include crops grown in semi-wet and dry soil conditions, such as paddy, wheat, soybean, and maize.
Priced up to 25 per cent (up to 7 lakhs) lower than some of the larger sized self-propelled harvesters, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva offers a cost-effective entry point for small and mid-sized farmers, as well as rural rental entrepreneurs. The new Mahindra Harvest Yuva offers affordable mechanized harvesting solutions for small farms and increases productivity over manual harvesting by accelerating harvesting operations. With the Mahindra Harvest Yuva, even small and mid-sized farms can be harvested efficiently, enabling farmers to complete harvesting on time, minimize weather-related losses, and enhance their income potential.
Commenting on the introduction, Ravindra Shahane, Vice President & Business Head – Farm Machinery, Farm Equipment Business, Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd., said, “The Mahindra Harvest Yuva has been designed ground up to address the unique needs of small and mid-sized farmers. With its compact dimensions, light weight design, convenient on-road transport width, ease of operation, and efficient harvesting performance, our new compact harvester enables farmers to access mechanized harvesting even in areas that are difficult to reach with larger machines. By combining affordability, productivity, and reliability, the Harvest Yuva provides farmers and rural entrepreneurs with a practical solution that can enhance operational efficiency and improve farm economics.”
Designed for ease of operations, with the operator in mind, the new Mahindra Harvest Yuva features a host of convenient features
- Lower station height
- A spacious platform with a co-driver seat
- Self-cleaning radiator for smoother operations
- Rear engine placement keeps heat from the engine away from the operator, reducing direct exposure during long working hours
With an RTO-approved cutter bar with a width of 9.3 and 10.9 feet, and a closed unloading tube, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva’s slim profile and short track width of 8 feet provide easy navigation along narrow village roads and tight turns. The 4 Wheel drive feature of the machine facilitates operations in wet paddy and soya field harvesting through proper traction. The compact cutter bar ensures that operators do not need to detach and reattach the cutter bar when moving from farm to farm, navigating small field entries, or travelling between the road and the field. Clear front visibility of the cutter bar enables better alignment and sharper cuts, helping reduce crop loss, particularly in lodged or uneven fields.
Hydraulic reel adjusters and prong cutters make it easy to switch between crops of different heights and densities, adapt to varied terrain, and handle different crop types. The harvester also features a unique feeder reverser, which helps operators remove clogged material at the push of a lever from the operator station. The lightweight, chain-driven mechanism with an inline front and rear wheel configuration minimizes soil compaction. This design enhances speed and agility, maximizes harvesting efficiency, reduces crop loss, and ensures superior produce quality for market delivery.
Powered by Mahindra's trusted engine technology, the Mahindra Harvest Yuva is designed for reliability, extended operating hours, and simplified servicing with minimal downtime. The harvester is backed by Mahindra’s warranty of 1 Year. The new Mahindra Harvest Yuva is now available for sale in key markets of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat & Uttar Pradesh.

evidence.title: Mahindra’s electric 3-wheeler biz may go public in 18 months; what investors should know
evidence.text:
Curated by: Alka Jain
Updated Nov 16, 2026 13:20 IST
Mahindra’s electric 3-wheeler biz may go public in 18 months; what investors should know
Mahindra & Mahindra is weighing a stock market debut of its electric three-wheeler business in the next 18 hours amid the growing demand for electric commercial vehicles due to rising fuel prices, according to Bloomberg reports. 
For the IPO, 
Mahindra Last Mile Mobility CEO Suman Mishra said that the company is looking at an 18-month window for a potential listing. However, the decision would depend on the business being ready. 
“The company would not rush into a listing as it could rely on its parent group to fund expansion. The group is going to fund us no matter which way,” she said at an event in Mumbai, as quoted by the newswire. 
The proposed IPO comes at a time when Mahindra’s last-mile mobility business expands its manufacturing capacity and looks to capitalise on rising electrification in 
India’s three-wheeler market. 
The company has also attracted external investors, with its latest fundraise valuing the business at over Rs 10,000 crore.
Mahindra EV biz’s unicorn valuation
In July, the company raised around Rs 322 crore in a funding round led by Lightrock, with existing investors International Finance Corporation (IFC) and India-Japan Fund also participating. With this fundraise round, the company’s valuation reached Rs 10,822 crore.
The company is also stepping up capacity expansion. Mishra said Mahindra had invested several hundred crore rupees in its latest expansion and was evaluating locations for a larger manufacturing facility.
The business has not yet achieved profitability without government incentives, but expects to reach that milestone in the next couple of years, Mishra said. A potential listing would therefore give investors an opportunity to assess the business's growth and profitability prospects as it scales up.
Mahindra’s EV market share
Higher fuel prices are encouraging commercial vehicle operators to consider electric three-wheelers, particularly those covering long daily distances. Mishra said more than 45 per cent of India's larger three-wheelers are now electric, with drivers increasingly attracted by the savings on operating costs.
The last mile mobility business saw a sixfold growth in sales of electric three-wheelers over the last four years. The company continues to be the market leader in the electric 3W category and demonstrated a volume growth of 85 per cent YoY in Q1 FY27. 
The company also recorded a milestone of 100,000 
electric 3-wheelers  in FY2026, a first for any electric commercial vehicle manufacturer in India. 
Mahindra is also facing intensifying competition from established automakers such as 
Bajaj Auto and TVS Motor, which have entered the electric three-wheeler market. Mishra said their participation had helped improve consumer confidence and expand demand.
The company has localised around 70-75 per cent of its manufacturing, although it continues to depend on imports for battery cells and semiconductors.
Mahindra & Mahindra financials
The company reported a standalone net profit of Rs 5,102 crore in Q2FY27, ahead of ET Now's estimates of Rs 4,529 crore. The 
automobile giant's net profit for the reporting quarter surged 13 per cent year-over-year from Rs 4,521 crore in Q2FY26.
The company's revenue from operations surged to 42,477 crore in Q2FY27, increasing 27 per cent YoY from Rs 33,422 crore in Q2FY26. The revenue figures of Q2FY27 beat ET Now estimates of Rs 41,372 crore.
On the operating front, the company's Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation, and Amortisation (EBITDA) is 2 per cent to Rs 4,912 crore in Q2FY27, below ET Now estimates of Rs 4,997 crore. However, M&M's EBITDA fell 4 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ). Its EBITDA margin contracted to 11.6 per cent in Q2FY27, as against ET NOW Poll of 12.1 per cent. In the same quarter a year ago, the company's EBITDA margin stood at 14.4 per cent.
On a consolidated basis, the company's net profit surged by 25 per cent YoY to Rs 4,588 crore in Q2FY27, compared to Rs 3,673 crore in Q2FY26. Its revenue from operations rose by 25 per cent as well to Rs 57,553 crore in Q2FY27, as against Rs 46,106 crore in Q2FY26.

evidence.title: SML Mahindra to raise upto Rs. 1450 crore through Rights Issue
evidence.text:
Mumbai, November 16, 2026: The Board of Directors of SML Mahindra Limited (SML Mahindra) on November 6, 2026, has approved raising of funds through the issuance of fully paid-up equity shares of the Company of the face value of Rs. 10/- each by way of a rights issue ("Rights Issue") for an amount not exceeding Rs. 1,450 Crore (Rupees One Thousand Four Hundred and Fifty Crore) to the eligible equity shareholders of the Company, subject to receipt of regulatory and statutory approvals.
Further, pursuant to the in-principle approval received from BSE Limited (“BSE”) and National Stock Exchange of India Limited (“NSE”), the Board of Directors has today fixed a rights issue price of Rs. 3,506 (Rupees Three Thousand Five Hundred and Six Only) per fully paid-up Rights Equity Share, leading to an entitlement of 2 (Two) fully paid-up Rights Equity Shares for every 7 (Seven) fully paid-up Equity Shares held by the eligible Equity Shareholders of the Company as on the Record Date i.e. Friday, 20th November, 2026.
The proceeds of the Rights Issue will primarily be utilised towards financing the acquisition of Mahindra Truck and Bus Division (MTBD) and supporting strategic growth initiatives aimed at building an integrated and future-ready commercial vehicle platform.
The acquisition of MTBD, announced in July 2026, is a key step in creating a scaled, unified and focused commercial vehicle platform. The integration of SML Mahindra and MTBD is expected to enhance product portfolio breadth, manufacturing capabilities, market reach, operating efficiencies and long-term competitiveness.
In addition, the Company will invest in capacity enhancement, manufacturing modernization, research and development on new product & aggregates, enhancement of existing products, product innovation and technology advancement, alternative fuel mobility solutions, connected vehicle technologies and engineering capability enhancement to accelerate the development of next-generation commercial vehicles and meet evolving customer expectations as well as applicable regulatory requirements.
Mahindra & Mahindra Limited, the promoter of the Company, has also confirmed to participate in the Rights Issue in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, demonstrating its continued commitment to SML Mahindra's growth strategy.
Mr. Vinod Sahay, Executive Chairman of SML Mahindra, said, "The proposed Rights Issue reflects our commitment to pursuing strategic growth opportunities while maintaining a prudent capital structure. The funds raised will strengthen our manufacturing capabilities, accelerate innovation, and provide additional financial flexibility to execute our long-term growth strategy. We remain focused on creating sustainable value for all our stakeholders.”

According to Vipin Kumar, AVP research at Globe Capital Market, the technical chart structure remains sideways with immediate supports placed around ₹360 levels. "A decisive close below the mentioned support could drag it towards the lower band of past 10 months congestion zone that is placed at ₹330 spot levels," he said. The sharp market reaction overshadowed the company's strong operational turnaround and substantial revenue and core earnings growth, highlighting investor concerns about the leadership transition despite the positive financial performance under Sikka's tenure.

evidence.title: TVS Star City Plus Discontinued in India After 12 Years
evidence.text:
For many buyers, a commuter motorcycle is all about daily use, low running costs and easy maintenance. The 110cc segment has served this purpose for years, with several manufacturers offering affordable options. TVS Motor also had three motorcycles in this category, the Sport, Radeon and Star City Plus. However, one name now appears to have reached the end of its journey in the Indian market.
The TVS Star City Plus has been removed from the company’s official website, suggesting that the motorcycle has been discontinued.
A Familiar Name Leaves the TVS Lineup
Launched in 2014, the Star City Plus spent more than a decade in the Indian two-wheeler market. It was positioned as an affordable commuter and competed with other entry-level motorcycles.
With its removal, TVS now has the Radeon and Sport as its two main 110cc commuter options. Both motorcycles continue to be listed on the company’s website.
The Star City Plus had also been struggling with sales for quite some time. Its reported sales figures during 2026 were particularly low.
These figures indicate that demand for the motorcycle had fallen considerably.
Engine and Features of the Star City Plus
The motorcycle used a 109.7cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled petrol engine. It was paired with a four-speed gearbox.
Here are its engine specifications:
- Engine capacity: 109.7cc
- Maximum power: 8.2hp at 7,350rpm
- Peak torque: 8.7Nm at 4,500rpm
- Gearbox: 4-speed
- Cooling system: Air-cooled
Despite being an entry-level motorcycle, TVS had equipped it with several useful features. These included an LED headlamp, a semi-digital instrument console and a USB charging port.
Other equipment included:
- Five-step adjustable rear suspension preload
- Self-start facility
- 17-inch alloy wheels
- Tubeless tyres
- Front disc and drum brake options
Its Last Major Update Came in 2021
The Star City Plus received its last significant update in March 2021, when TVS introduced the Roto Petal front disc brake. Later changes were largely limited to meeting emission regulations, including the BS6 update.
The Radeon, which caters to a similar group of buyers, also offers TVS another option in this segment.
With the Star City Plus disappearing from the official website and sales falling sharply, its journey in India appears to have come to an end. TVS has yet to make a formal announcement confirming its discontinuation.

evidence.title: TVS Star City Plus Likely Discontinued in India
evidence.text:
TVS Motor may have discontinued the Star City Plus in India. The commuter motorcycle no longer appears on the company's official Indian website. This move suggests that TVS could have decided to stop selling the motorcycle due to low demand.
The Star City Plus was part of TVS Motor's budget commuter motorcycle range. It competed with popular 110cc motorcycles from Hero MotoCorp, Honda and Bajaj. However, its sales have remained very low in recent months.
TVS Motor's official website currently lists a limited range of commuter motorcycles. The Star City Plus does not appear on the list anymore. Interestingly, the pre update Radeon still appears on the website.
The TVS Sport also does not appear on the current website. However, the company continues to offer the TVS Radeon. This change suggests that TVS may have started reducing its commuter motorcycle lineup. The biggest reason behind this decision is the Star City Plus's poor sales performance.
According to the available sales figures, TVS sold only 49 units of the Star City Plus between January and September 2026. Here is the month-wise sales breakup:
Here is the month-wise domestic sales performance for the TVS Star City Plus from January 2026 to September 2026. The table highlights a sharp decline in monthly dispatches, with zero units recorded between May and September 2026.
TVS first launched the Star City Plus in India in 2014. Its last major update arrived in March 2021. At that time, TVS introduced a Roto Petal front disc brake. Since then, the company has not introduced any major changes apart from engine updates for the latest emission rules.
The motorcycle used a 109.7cc, single-cylinder, air-cooled engine. It produced 8.2bhp of power and 8.7Nm of torque. A four-speed gearbox handled transmission duties.
Other features included an LED headlight, a semi-digital instrument cluster, a USB charging port and electric start. In addition, it came with 17 inch alloy wheels, tubeless tyres and attractive graphics on the fuel tank.
TVS has not officially confirmed the discontinuation of the Star City Plus. However, its removal from the website and weak sales suggest that the company may have ended its journey in India. For now, buyers looking for a TVS commuter bike can consider the Radeon. The company may also focus on its remaining commuter offerings going forward.

evidence.title: India Two-Wheeler Sales October 2026: Dispatches Rise 16.1% to 25.78 Lakh Units; Hero Leads, TVS Gains Market Share
evidence.text:
India Two-Wheeler Sales October 2026: Dispatches Rise 16.1% to 25.78 Lakh Units; Hero Leads, TVS Gains Market Share
India's two-wheeler industry recorded strong wholesale growth in October 2026, with Hero MotoCorp maintaining its leadership and TVS Motor strengthening its market position. However, a comparison with FADA retail registrations reveals a contrasting picture of market demand.
India's two-wheeler manufacturers dispatched 25,77,810 units in October 2026, registering a 16.1% year-on-year increase compared with 22,20,345 units in October 2025. Dispatches also increased 4.7% month-on-month from 24,63,103 units in September 2026.
Hero MotoCorp retained its leadership in the wholesale market with over 7.05 lakh units, followed by Honda Motorcycle & Scooter India at 6.65 lakh units. TVS Motor maintained third position with 5.15 lakh units, recording the strongest year-on-year growth among the three leading manufacturers.
The wholesale performance, however, contrasts sharply with the retail market. According to FADA registration data previously reported by AutoPunditz, October 2026 retail registrations declined 28.35% year-on-year to 23.21 lakh units.
The difference highlights why both wholesale dispatches and retail registrations are important for understanding India's two-wheeler industry.
India Two-Wheeler Dispatches – October 2026
- Hero MotoCorp: Led the wholesale market with 7,05,084 units, up 16.6% YoY. Market share increased marginally to 27.35%, despite a 4.6% MoM decline. 
- Honda: Ranked second with 6,64,831 units, growing 11.0% YoY and 4.4% MoM. Market share declined to 25.79%. 
- TVS Motor: Dispatched 5,14,764 units, registering strong 22.1% YoY growth. Market share gained 0.98 percentage points to reach 19.97%. 
- Bajaj Auto: Recorded 2,92,885 units, up 9.9% YoY and 22.2% MoM. Market share declined to 11.36%. 
- Suzuki: Registered 1,24,599 units, growing 20.4% YoY. Overtook Royal Enfield to secure fifth position with 4.83% market share. 
- Royal Enfield: Dispatched 1,21,527 motorcycles, up 4.0% YoY. Market share declined to 4.71%. 
- Yamaha: Recorded 91,151 units, registering 33.3% YoY growth. Market share improved to 3.54%. 
- Ather Energy: Dispatched 33,786 electric two-wheelers, growing 30.8% YoY and 12.2% MoM. 
- Greaves Electric Mobility: Recorded 15,885 units, more than doubling its dispatches with 108.8% YoY growth. 
- River: Dispatched 7,544 units, registering the highest YoY growth among listed manufacturers at 275.0%. 
Key Takeaway: Hero retained wholesale leadership, TVS emerged as a major market-share gainer, and smaller EV manufacturers recorded strong growth. The top three OEMs collectively controlled 73.1% of the wholesale market in October 2026.
Wholesale Dispatches vs Retail Registrations: Why October 2026 Shows Two Different Trends
One of the most interesting developments in October 2026 is the substantial difference between manufacturers' wholesale dispatches and actual customer registrations.
While dispatches increased 16.1% year-on-year, FADA reported a 28.35% contraction in retail registrations.
Registrations declined from 32,39,949 units in October 2025 to 23,21,419 units in October 2026
OEM-wise Dispatches vs Registrations – October 2026
The comparison reveals several important differences.
Hero leads wholesale dispatches, but Honda leads retail registrations. Hero dispatched 40,253 more units than Honda, whereas Honda registered 39,197 more vehicles than Hero. This indicates a clear difference between the manufacturers' wholesale and retail positions during October.
TVS demonstrated comparatively strong performance across both datasets. While its wholesale dispatches grew 22.1%, its registrations declined 19.9% year-on-year. Nevertheless, TVS gained market share in both measurements, suggesting that its competitive position remained strong relative to other major manufacturers.
The wholesale-retail gap deserves attention. Industry dispatches exceeded registrations by approximately 2.56 lakh units during October 2026. Hero, Bajaj and TVS accounted for substantial positive differences, while Royal Enfield's registrations slightly exceeded dispatches.
However, this gap should not automatically be interpreted as an equivalent addition to unsold dealer inventory. Registration timing, reporting coverage, vehicles in transit and differences in wholesale and retail reporting can influence the comparison.
The exceptionally high October 2025 retail base and potential festive-calendar effects also need to be considered when interpreting the opposing year-on-year trends.
Auto Punditz Analysis
October 2026 presents a mixed picture for India's two-wheeler industry.
A 16.1% increase in dispatches indicates stronger manufacturer-to-dealer movement compared to last year. However, the decline in retail registrations shows that higher wholesale volumes didn't translate into similar growth in customer registrations.
Hero MotoCorp leads in wholesale volume, while Honda is stronger in retail. TVS Motor improves its market share in both areas, reinforcing its competitive position.
The gap between dispatches and registrations raises questions about dealer inventory. Higher wholesale supply might reflect stock replenishment, anticipated demand, or inventory build-up. Without dealer stock data, it's unclear if October's dispatch growth represents sustainable demand.
Yamaha, Suzuki, and emerging electric manufacturers show growth opportunities beyond the three largest brands.
Looking ahead, November 2026 registrations, wholesale trends, and dealer inventory data will be key to assessing if October's divergence was temporary or a sign of a sustained supply-demand imbalance.
Conclusion
India's two-wheeler industry recorded a healthy 16.1% increase in wholesale dispatches during October 2026, with volumes reaching 25.78 lakh units. Hero MotoCorp maintained leadership, TVS Motor strengthened its market position and several smaller manufacturers reported impressive growth.
However, FADA's 28.35% decline in registrations provides a contrasting perspective on retail performance.
The key takeaway is that wholesale growth alone does not establish stronger
consumer demand. For a clearer assessment of market health, dispatch volumes must be evaluated alongside registrations, inventory trends and the broader festive-season sales cycle.

evidence.title: Lakshmi Venu seeks partition of assets of Venu Srinivasan branch of TVS family
evidence.text:
Lakshmi Venu, the daughter of TVS Holdings chairman Venu Srinivasan, has sought formal partition of assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family by issuing a legal notice to her father.
The Venu Srinivasan branch controls TVS Motor Company, India’s third largest two-wheeler manufacturer by market share worth over $20 billion. It is currently headed by Ms. Lakshmi Venu’s younger brother Sudarshan Venu, who is the CMD of TVS Motor Company, and was named the Significant Beneficial Owner in April 2025, signalling that he would inherit the larger chunk of the businesses under TVS Holdings. A senior executive privy to the family dispute, but who did not wish to be named had told The Hindu attempts to seek clarity by Ms. Lakshmi Venu on the April 2025 SBO disclosure had been met with “silence”.
The Hindu had reported on the differences that had appeared over the division of assets in October, when it was still unclear whether the matter would reach the courts. With the filing of a caveat in the Madras High Court by Mr. Srinivasan, followed by the notice issued by Ms. Lakshmi Venu to her father, it is now clear that the differences over the division of property have not been resolved amicably and will most likely be fought in the courts.
In her statement to the media, Ms. Lakshmi Venu has cited the Hindu Succession Act 1956, which was amended in 2005 to include Section 6, enabling women to be equal inheritors of family property.
Ms. Lakshmi Venu has said she “is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property”. The statement goes on to state, “Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India. The rights of daughters to joint family property, she maintains, cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements,” citing the April 2025 decision to include her brother Mr. Sudarshan Venu as Significant Beneficial Owner of TVS Motor Company.
Ms. Venu has sought the partition of of asets that include the the VS Trust, whose trustee is Venu Srinivasan, and through which TVS Holdings owns 50.26% of TVS Motor Company. Ms. Venu has effectivdly sought the partition of assets allotted to the Venu Srinivasan branch of the family under the 2020 TVS family arrangement, including interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton.
Dr. Lakshmi maintains that the larger TVS family arrangement did not constitute a partition within the Venu Srinivasan family. No settlement or partition of the assets within her immediate family was ever initiated, let alone concluded. In her view, management does not confer exclusive ownership or extinguish lawful rights of other family members.
Crucially, this statement has the endorsement of Ms. Lakshmi Venu’s mother Mallika Srinivasan. The statement reads: “Mrs. Mallika Srinivasan, supporting Ms. Venu’s legitimate right in the family assets, said, ‘It is unfortunate that requests for an amicable settlement have not so far progressed in a meaningful and timely way. As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not inequal to that of Sudarshan’s. I reiterate that this is a matter to be settled, in the interests of all stakeholders, through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. I sincerely hope that we can move forward constructively, with grace and dignity.’”
Shares of TVS Motor Company closed at ₹4,453 apiece on the NSE signalling no material impact on account of the legal notice so far.

evidence.title: What is happening at the TVS Motor Company: Read how a family feud over asset control has taken a legal turn
evidence.text:
The succession battle within the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family has moved from boardroom manoeuvring and court caveats to a formal demand for partition, with Lakshmi Venu seeking an equal share in the joint family assets controlled by her father.
In a partition notice addressed to Venu Srinivasan, chairman emeritus of TVS Motor Company, Lakshmi has asked him to discharge his fiduciary duties as head of the family and give effect to a “fair and lawful partition.” The notice, confirmed by a statement from her office, covers family interests held through the VS Trust and other holding structures, including stakes in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton businesses and assets allotted to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the wider TVS family arrangement of 2020.
Lakshmi, managing director of Sundaram-Clayton and vice-chairman of TAFE, has invoked Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005, which recognises daughters as coparceners with rights equal to sons in qualifying joint family property. Her position is that the 2020 division of the larger TVS Group did not amount to a partition within her immediate family, and that no settlement or division of assets within Venu Srinivasan’s family was ever initiated, let alone completed.
Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, chairman and managing director of Tractors and Farm Equipment, has publicly backed the claim. “As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of Sudarshan’s,” she said, while calling for a settlement through transparent dialogue.
The move sharpens a dispute that surfaced publicly in October after TVS Holdings disclosed that Sudarshan Venu, Lakshmi’s brother and the person who leads TVS Motor, had been identified as a significant beneficial owner through trust structures. Lakshmi and Mallika questioned those arrangements, and all four family members Venu Srinivasan, Mallika, Lakshmi and Sudarshan filed caveats in Chennai courts, signalling preparations for possible litigation even as both sides publicly favoured an amicable resolution. The four represent the third and fourth generations of T.V. Sundaram Iyengar, founder of the TVS Group.
What the whole dispute is about
At its core, the fight is over whether the Srinivasan family’s economic interests have actually been divided and, if not, whether Lakshmi is entitled to an equal share of assets that she says are joint family property.
Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan maintain that a separation has already been carried out. They point to a memorandum of understanding signed by all four family members in March 2024, and to the broader 2020 TVS family arrangement, as evidence that the economic split is complete. Venu Srinivasan has said the businesses and assets were his, that he had the liberty to deal with them as he thought best, and that the separation gave Lakshmi the Sundaram-Clayton business while Sudarshan got the motors business. “The separation was always about ownership and control,” he has said, adding that both children were given a fair share on which to build.
Lakshmi and Mallika reject that characterisation. They argue that the March 2024 MoU was primarily a limited-term agreement on the use of the TVS brand and trademarks, along with non-compete obligations, and cannot be treated as an economic settlement. They say no transparent valuation, discussion or mutual consent took place to divide the family’s economic interests, and that management or control of a business does not confer exclusive ownership or extinguish the legal rights of other family members.
Lakshmi has alleged that beneficial interest in the family assets has been concentrated in favour of Sudarshan at the expense of her own lawful rights, describing it as both a breach of law and a breach of trust. Her statement put the broader argument bluntly: “Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India.”
The legal question is not simply whether a daughter can inherit. The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act made daughters coparceners in joint family property, and Lakshmi’s case rests on that right. But the dispute will turn on whether the assets in question are indeed joint family or coparcenary property, whether the 2024 MoU operated as a partition, and how the trust structures that hold the family’s stakes in listed and unlisted companies are treated. Because the VS Trust holds a 66.55% stake in TVS Holdings, which in turn owns a majority stake in TVS Motor, any partition or reallocation could have consequences for ownership and control of one of India’s best-known automakers.
For now, the notice is a legal escalation rather than a filed suit. Lakshmi has said she prefers an amicable and equitable resolution, and the family has publicly maintained that dialogue is the preferred route. But with a partition notice on the table and caveats already filed in Chennai courts, the TVS family feud has entered a phase where the next move may well be judicial.

evidence.title: TVS Family Feud: Who Is Lakshmi Venu, Seeking Share In Venu Srinivasan Family Assets? Here's All About Her
evidence.text:
TVS Family Feud: Who Is Lakshmi Venu, Seeking Share In Venu Srinivasan Family Assets? Here's All About Her
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of TVS Motor Company chairman emeritus Venu Srinivasan, has reportedly sought a formal partition of her father's family assets, bringing questions over wealth distribution and succession within the prominent TVS family into focus. The move concerns the Venu Srinivasan branch of the family, which is closely associated with TVS Holdings and TVS Motor Company, one of India's leading two-wheeler manufacturers with a market value of more than $20 billion.
TVS Family Feud: Lakshmi Venu Seeks 'Fair And Lawful' Partition Of Assets
According to reports, Lakshmi has issued a notice to her father seeking a partition of family assets. In the notice, she reportedly called on him, as the head of the family, to fulfil his fiduciary responsibilities and ensure a "fair and lawful partition".
Venu Srinivasan, meanwhile, has filed a caveat before the Madras High Court. The filing indicates that he wants to be heard before any order is passed if a related legal proceeding comes before the court. The step does not, by itself, mean that the court has ruled on the dispute.
Who Is Lakshmi Venu; Seeking Partition of Venu Srinivasan Family Assets
Lakshmi Venu is an Indian business executive whose career spans the automobile components and agricultural equipment industries. She is the daughter of Venu Srinivasan, chairman emeritus of TVS Motor Company and Mallika Srinivasan, who is associated with Tractors and Farm Equipment Limited (TAFE).
Rather than being known only through her family connections, Lakshmi has held leadership positions in businesses linked to India's manufacturing sector. She is the vice chairman of TAFE, a major tractor and agricultural equipment manufacturer, and has also served as a director of TAFE Motors and Tractors Limited (TMTL).
She has been associated with Sundaram-Clayton Limited (SCL), a manufacturer of automotive components, where she has held a senior leadership role as joint managing director. Her professional responsibilities have placed her in an industry closely connected to the wider TVS business network.
Her reported demand for a partition has now put her family interests alongside her business career in the public eye.
Lakshmi Venu Education
Lakshmi's education took her from India to two prominent universities overseas. She studied Economics at Yale University in the United States before pursuing a doctorate in Engineering Management at the University of Warwick in England.
The combination of economics and engineering management provided an academic foundation relevant to the industrial businesses in which she later worked. Her career has since included responsibilities in automotive components and agricultural equipment, two sectors that play an important role in India's manufacturing economy.
Her educational background is also a notable part of her profile as a member of the next generation of the TVS business family.
Lakshmi Venu And Sudarshan Venu: Two Siblings In TVS Business Family
Lakshmi's younger brother, Sudarshan Venu, heads TVS Motor Company as its chairman and managing director. His leadership places him at the centre of one of the family's most prominent businesses.
Sudarshan was named a Significant Beneficial Owner in April 2025, a development cited in reports surrounding the family dispute. The contrast between the siblings' business roles has added to the attention on the family's ownership arrangements, although the reported partition notice concerns the assets of their father's branch.
The central issue is the division of family wealth, rather than a confirmed change in the management or ownership of TVS Motor Company. The precise assets covered by the notice and the eventual outcome of the dispute remain unclear from the available information.
TVS Family's 2020 Settlement
The latest development comes several years after the wider TVS family agreed to reorganise its business holdings. On December 10, 2020, four branches of the family reached an agreement to simplify their ownership structures, reduce cross-holdings and align corporate interests more closely with the businesses managed by each branch.
The restructuring followed a valuation and settlement exercise and was intended to make the group's ownership arrangements more straightforward. However, the reported dispute involving Lakshmi relates specifically to the division of assets within the Venu Srinivasan branch.

evidence.title: TVS family dispute: What the law says about a daughter’s inheritance rights
evidence.text:
The dispute within the TVS family over the distribution of its assets among the next generation took a legal turn on Monday, with Dr Lakshmi Venu sending a notice to her father and TVS Holdings Chairman Venu Srinivasan.
Through the legal notice, Lakshmi has called for a “fair and lawful partition” of the assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the Chennai-based TVS family, and contends that “the concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her (younger) brother,” Sudarshan Venu, was to the exclusion of her own lawful rights.
Lakshmi is the MD of auto parts maker Sundaram-Clayton, with a market cap of over Rs 2,000 crore, while Sudarshan is the chairman and MD of two-wheeler maker TVS Motors, which has a market cap of over Rs 2 lakh crore. Sudarshan is also MD of TVS Holdings, the holding company, which is headed by their father, Venu. Venu’s wife, Mallika Srinivasan, is the chairperson and MD of tractor manufacturer TAFE, where Lakshmi is vice-chair.
In April last year, Venu named his son and current CMD of TVS Motor, Sudarshan, as the Significant Beneficial Owner. This would mean that he would inherit the larger portion of the businesses and assets of TVS Holdings.
Lakshmi contends that no settlement of the assets within her immediate family was ever initiated, and says that she is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property. Citing the Hindu Succession Act 1956, which now recognises daughters as equal inheritors of property in an undivided Hindu family, Lakshmi has asked her father to “discharge his fiduciary duties” and effect a fair and lawful partition. She has asked for a fair partition of the family assets which includes Venu Srinivasan's interest in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton.
“Dr Lakshmi contends that she is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property… She regards these actions not only as a breach of law but also as a breach of trust. Patriarchy has no place in law or in a progressive India. The rights of daughters to joint family property, she maintains, cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements,” reads Lakshmi’s statement to the press regarding the matter.
Her request for equal inheritance has also been backed by her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, who said a son and daughter are equal and that Lakshmi is entitled to an equal share.
“It is unfortunate that requests for an amicable settlement have not so far progressed in a meaningful and timely way. As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not inequal to that of Sudarshan’s. I reiterate that this is a matter to be settled, in the interests of all stakeholders, through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. I sincerely hope that we can move forward constructively, with grace and dignity,” Mallika says in the statement.
As the dispute continues, here is an overview of what the law recognises as a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) and how succession works within it.
Hindu Undivided Family
An HUF is a distinct legal entity comprising people who have all descended from a common ancestor, including their wives and unmarried daughters. It is not necessary for all family members to live under the same roof for an HUF to exist.
The family is managed by the eldest male member, though a senior female member can also assume the role. Such a head is called the Karta. A woman can also become a Karta if she is the eldest surviving child of her father.
Lineal descendants who hold a birthright in the ancestral property and have the right to claim a partition are called Coparceners. Until 2005, only male members of the family were entitled to claim equal inheritance. An Amendment to the Hindu Succession Act in 2005 changed that, empowering women also to be coparceners with a right to claim ancestral property and ask for partition.
The Amendment placed thrust on the position of daughters in an HUF. Though it is not applicable retrospectively, the law has placed safeguards to ensure that a daughter is not denied her rights.
The law says that a daughter cannot reopen a partition that was already legally completed before December 20, 2004, when the Amendment was not in effect. However, to block a daughter's claim, the earlier partition must have been executed through a registered partition deed or a final court decree. Informal or oral family arrangements before that date do not take away her right.
Inheritance
The principal legislation governing the inheritance among members of an HUF is the Hindu Succession Act of 1950. The law makes distinctions between ancestral coparcenary property and an individual's self-acquired or separately owned property.
Under the amended Section 6 of the Act, sons and daughters have equal rights in ancestral coparcenary property. The daughter has the same right as the son to claim partition and receive her legally determined share. She does not lose her rights upon marriage or because she is living separately from the family.
Property purchased or acquired independently by an individual does not automatically become property of the family simply because the person belongs to an HUF.
Partition
A partition, like the one now asked by Venu Srinivasan’s daughter, Lakshmi, refers to the division of joint family property either through a mutual agreement among the members or through court proceedings.
A coparcener can demand a partition, and after the 2005 Amendment to the Hindu Succession Act, a daughter is also eligible to demand a partition. When family members dispute their entitlements or cannot come to terms through a mutual agreement, a civil court can determine their shares and order partition.

evidence.title: Auto sector on track to meet FY27 growth target; Elara favours TVS, Eicher Motors
evidence.text:
Auto sector on track to meet FY27 growth target; Elara favours TVS, Eicher Motors
- Edited byalphadesk
- Published OnNov 17, 2026 | 11:07 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 17, 2026 | 11:07 IST
Elara Capital expects India's passenger vehicle and two-wheeler industries to achieve FY27 growth targets as festive demand and dealer inventories remain supportive. The brokerage prefers TVS Motor, Eicher Motors and select auto ancillary stocks, while remaining cautious on commercial vehicles.
Auto sector is on track to achieve financial year 2026-27 (FY27) growth targets as festive demand remains resilient, while passenger vehicles (PVs) and two-wheelers are likely to outperform commercial vehicles (CVs), according to Jay Kale, Director at Elara Capital.
Kale said healthy retail demand during the festive season, comfortable dealer inventory and improving wholesale prospects support the outlook for the second half of 2026-27.
The brokerage continues to prefer passenger vehicle and two-wheeler companies, along with auto ancillary firms that have multiple growth drivers.
"What this means is that the full-year growth rate numbers of 11%... should be met," Kale said, adding that dealer inventories across most companies remain at comfortable levels.
He said the second half is expected to see healthy wholesale growth as inventory levels are not elevated, although retail demand during the December-March period will remain an important monitor due to a high base.
"We should expect good growth on a high base in the second half in wholesale as well," he said.
Tata Motors: India business remains strong despite JLR challenges
Commenting on Tata Motors, Kale said Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) continues to face pressure from Chinese competition and weaker demand in Europe and the UK, which could keep the luxury-vehicle business under pressure.
However, he said Tata Motors' India passenger vehicle business continues to perform well, supported by steady demand and improving electric vehicle penetration.
"The India business continues to do well at least on the demand side," Kale said. He added that while JLR's issues are likely to persist, they are largely factored into the current stock price.
He expects the India passenger vehicle business to benefit from price hikes planned for the third and fourth quarters, which should support margins.
Preferred auto ancillary and two-wheeler picks
Within the auto ancillary space, Elara Capital prefers companies that can grow faster than the industry through product expansion, new geographies or acquisitions.
Kale's preferred names include Sona BLW Precision Forgings (Sona Comstar), Gabriel India, Minda Corporation and Uno Minda.
Among two-wheeler manufacturers, he remains positive on TVS Motor Company and Eicher Motors, citing market share gains and earnings visibility.
He said TVS continues to gain market share across both electric and internal combustion engine (ICE) segments, while Eicher Motors is expected to benefit from capacity expansion and lean dealer inventories.
Positive view on Ather Energy
Kale also expressed optimism on electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy, saying its business performance and margins remain strong.
"If at all any company within the startup space will stand the test of time, I think one of them is Ather Energy," he said, while noting that valuations remain a factor to watch.
Commercial vehicles less preferred
While commercial vehicle demand has surprised positively in 2026-27, Kale believes the segment is approaching a mature phase of the cycle after crossing pre-pandemic peaks.
He expects only mid-single-digit growth over the medium-term and prefers passenger vehicles and two-wheelers over commercial vehicles from an investment perspective.

evidence.title: TVS to Launch Norton Motorcycles in India by 2027
evidence.text:
TVS to Launch Norton Motorcycles in India by 2027
New Delhi, November 15: TVS Motor Company is set to give a fresh identity to the British bike brand Norton Motorcycles. Since acquiring the brand in 2020, TVS has been consistently investing in it. Now, the company is preparing to introduce Norton’s premium bikes in the Indian market. Recently, Norton patented two powerful motorcycles, the Atlas GT and Manx R, in India. These bikes are expected to be launched in the Indian market by 2027. Let’s delve into the details.
Features of the Bikes
Norton’s portfolio prominently features the powerful Manx and Manx R bikes, which come equipped with a 1,200cc V4 engine generating 206bhp. In the mid-range, the Atlas and Atlas GT adventure and touring bikes are included. The Atlas GT is a more road-focused touring version of the Atlas, featuring alloy wheels at both the front and rear, while the Atlas has wire-spoke wheels. Additionally, the Atlas Apex is a more premium variant.
Powertrain of the Atlas GT
The Norton Atlas GT is powered by a 585cc DOHC parallel-twin engine, producing 69bhp and 57.5Nm of torque. It comes with a 6-speed gearbox, a slip and assist clutch, and a bi-directional quickshifter. The bike features an 8-inch TFT touchscreen display with Bluetooth, navigation, and GoPro control capabilities. It also offers five riding modes, a 15.4-liter fuel tank, a ground clearance of 220mm, and adjustable USD front forks from KYB.
Powertrain of the Manx R
On the other hand, the Norton Manx R is the company’s premium super sport bike. In the UK, its starting price is £20,250, approximately ₹26 lakh. It is powered by a 1,200cc V4 engine that generates 206bhp at 11,500 RPM and 130Nm of torque at 9,000 RPM. This bike comes in four variants: Standard, Apex, Signature, and First Edition. All variants feature a 6-axis IMU, wheelie control, traction control, slide control, and an 8-inch TFT display. It is also equipped with Brembo hyper calipers and Pirelli Diablo Supercorsa tires.

evidence.title: TVS Srichakra Q2 FY27: Stellar Profit Surge Masks Margin Pressures
evidence.text:
The quarter's standout performance was driven by robust top-line expansion, with net sales reaching ₹1,272.63 crores—the highest quarterly revenue in the company's history. This represented a 19.20% sequential increase from Q1 FY27's ₹1,067.61 crores and a substantial 37.36% year-on-year growth. The company's ability to scale revenues whilst simultaneously improving profitability metrics marks a significant operational achievement in the competitive tyres and rubber products sector.
However, beneath the impressive headline numbers lie nuanced challenges. Whilst operating margins expanded to 8.22% from 7.11% a year ago, they remain below the company's historical peak of 8.83% achieved in Q4 FY26. The PAT margin of 3.49%, though substantially improved from last year's 1.18%, still trails the 3.68% recorded in March 2026, suggesting that margin expansion may be plateauing despite strong volume growth.
Financial Performance: Revenue Momentum Meets Margin Scrutiny
The quarter-on-quarter analysis reveals a company firing on multiple cylinders. Net sales of ₹1,272.63 crores represented a robust 19.20% sequential jump, building on the 8.84% growth recorded in Q1 FY27. This sustained momentum pushed the half-yearly revenue for H1 FY27 to ₹2,340.24 crores, marking a 33.74% increase over H1 FY26's ₹1,750.90 crores.
Operating profit before depreciation, interest, and tax (excluding other income) reached ₹104.59 crores in Q2 FY27, the highest quarterly PBDIT in company history. This translated to an operating margin of 8.22%, up from 7.57% in Q1 FY27 and significantly ahead of the 7.11% posted in Q2 FY25. The improvement suggests better cost absorption and operational leverage as volumes scaled.
However, the year-on-year comparison reveals a more complex picture. Whilst net profit surged nearly fourfold from ₹11.11 crores in Q2 FY25, this was primarily due to an exceptionally weak base quarter last year rather than extraordinary current performance. The PAT margin of 3.49%, though improved, remains substantially below the company's FY24 peak of 3.68% and well short of the 3.80% achieved in FY21.
Employee costs rose to ₹119.57 crores in Q2 FY27 from ₹115.20 crores in the previous quarter, reflecting continued headcount expansion to support growth. Interest costs remained stable at ₹11.32 crores, marginally lower than Q1's ₹11.64 crores, indicating disciplined debt management. Depreciation increased slightly to ₹37.71 crores from ₹37.14 crores, in line with ongoing capital expenditure.
The tax rate normalised to 22.42% in Q2 FY27 from 24.80% in the previous quarter, closer to the company's historical average and providing a modest boost to bottom-line growth. Other income contributed ₹2.40 crores, significantly lower than Q1's ₹14.21 crores, suggesting the previous quarter benefited from non-recurring treasury gains or asset sales.
Operational Excellence: Record Volumes, Persistent Margin Constraints
TVS Srichakra's operational metrics paint a picture of a company successfully scaling production and market share, yet grappling with structural margin limitations inherent to the capital-intensive tyre manufacturing business. The company's return on equity stands at a modest 6.31% on average, significantly trailing industry leaders and reflecting the challenges of generating superior returns in this competitive segment.
The company's return on capital employed averaged 7.55% over recent periods, indicating weak capital efficiency despite the recent operational improvements. This suggests that whilst the company is growing revenues, it is doing so at the cost of deploying substantial capital without proportionate returns—a concern for quality-focused investors.
Margin Pressure Points
Operating Leverage Limits: Despite achieving record quarterly revenues of ₹1,272.63 crores, operating margins of 8.22% remain below the company's own historical peak of 10.30% achieved in FY24. This suggests that raw material inflation, competitive pricing pressures, or operational inefficiencies are constraining the company's ability to fully capitalise on volume growth. The decline in annual operating margins from 10.30% in FY24 to 7.80% in FY26 represents a significant erosion of profitability despite revenue expansion.
The balance sheet reveals a company managing debt prudently, with long-term borrowings declining to ₹269.91 crores as of March 2026 from ₹348.94 crores a year earlier. This deleveraging effort, combined with stable interest coverage of 9.24 times in Q2 FY27 (the highest in recent quarters), demonstrates improving financial health. However, the debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 3.11 times remains elevated, indicating that the company still carries substantial leverage relative to its cash generation capacity.
Working capital management appears efficient, with current assets of ₹1,243.83 crores adequately covering current liabilities of ₹1,411.56 crores as of March 2026. Trade payables stood at ₹532.46 crores, up from ₹503.25 crores the previous year, suggesting the company is negotiating better payment terms with suppliers as its scale increases.
Industry Context: Outperforming a Challenging Sector
The broader tyres and rubber products sector has faced headwinds, with the industry delivering a negative 14.24% return over the past year. Against this backdrop, TVS Srichakra's 2.91% one-year stock return represents a relative outperformance of 17.15 percentage points, demonstrating investor confidence in the company's operational trajectory despite sector-wide challenges.
The tyre industry has grappled with volatile raw material costs, particularly natural rubber and crude oil derivatives, which constitute the bulk of manufacturing expenses. Additionally, intense competition from established players like MRF, Apollo Tyres, and CEAT in the two-wheeler and three-wheeler segments has kept pricing power limited. TVS Srichakra's ability to grow revenues by 37.36% year-on-year in this environment suggests market share gains, likely driven by its association with the TVS Group's automotive ecosystem and expanding distribution reach.
Competitive Positioning: Volume Leadership, Value Constraints
TVS Srichakra's strategy appears focused on volume growth in the two-wheeler and three-wheeler tyre segments, where it benefits from captive demand from TVS Motor Company and other group entities. This volume-first approach has delivered impressive top-line expansion but at the cost of margin compression. The company's operating margin of 8.22% in Q2 FY27, whilst improved from last year, pales in comparison to premium players like Balkrishna Industries, which commands significantly higher margins through focus on specialised agricultural and off-highway tyres.
The company's financial trend has been classified as "Outstanding" based on recent quarterly performance, with key metrics including operating profit to interest coverage, net sales, PBDIT, and PAT all reaching historical highs. This marks a significant turnaround from the "Very Negative" trend observed in December 2024, indicating sustained operational momentum over the past three quarters.
Peer Comparison: Premium Valuation, Subpar Returns
When benchmarked against industry peers, TVS Srichakra trades at a premium valuation despite delivering inferior return metrics. The company's price-to-earnings ratio of 32.13 times significantly exceeds the sector average of approximately 22 times, with only Balkrishna Industries commanding a comparable multiple at 30.66 times. However, unlike Balkrishna, which justifies its premium through a stellar 15.15% return on equity, TVS Srichakra's 6.31% ROE represents the weakest performance in the peer group.
The price-to-book value ratio of 2.78 times also appears stretched relative to the company's capital efficiency. Apollo Tyres, with a superior 9.72% ROE, trades at just 1.52 times book value, whilst JK Tyre, delivering 11.92% ROE, commands only 1.73 times book. This valuation disconnect suggests that investors are pricing in significant future margin expansion and return improvement—expectations that the current operational trends only partially support.
On a positive note, TVS Srichakra maintains one of the lowest debt-to-equity ratios in the sector at 0.63 times, indicating a relatively conservative balance sheet compared to peers like JK Tyre (0.96 times) or CEAT (0.81 times). This financial flexibility could prove valuable if the company pursues capacity expansion or strategic acquisitions to enhance market position.
Valuation Analysis: Fair Value, Limited Upside
At the current market price of ₹4,326.70, TVS Srichakra trades at 32.13 times trailing twelve-month earnings, representing a 53% premium to the industry average P/E of 21 times. The company's EV/EBITDA multiple of 13.02 times appears reasonable compared to historical levels, whilst the EV/Sales ratio of 1.04 times suggests modest investor expectations for profitability improvement.
The stock's price-to-book value of 2.78 times compares to a book value per share of ₹1,553.76, implying limited margin of safety for value investors. The PEG ratio of 0.10 appears attractive on the surface, but this metric is distorted by the company's negative five-year EBIT growth of -0.56%, making it an unreliable valuation indicator in this case.
The valuation assessment by market analysts classifies the stock as "Fair" at current levels, having oscillated between "Fair" and "Attractive" over the past year. The stock last traded in "Attractive" territory in October 2025 before reverting to "Fair" valuation. This suggests limited upside potential unless the company can demonstrate sustained margin expansion and return improvement.
The dividend yield of 0.87% offers modest income support, with the company maintaining a generous payout ratio of 62.77%. The latest dividend of ₹37.79 per share, paid in September 2026, reflects management's confidence in cash flow sustainability, though it also indicates limited capital retention for growth investments.
Shareholding Pattern: Stable Promoter Base, Modest Institutional Interest
The shareholding structure reveals a company with strong promoter commitment but limited institutional validation. Promoter holding has remained rock-steady at 45.70% across the past five quarters, with no dilution or increase—a positive signal of long-term commitment from the TVS Group entities that control the company.
However, institutional participation remains anaemic. Foreign institutional investors hold a mere 1.27% as of September 2026, up marginally from 0.92% in the previous quarter. Mutual fund holdings declined slightly to 5.93% from 6.02%, whilst insurance companies maintain zero exposure to the stock. The total institutional holding of just 7.38% suggests that quality-focused institutional investors remain unconvinced about the company's long-term return potential.
The dominance of non-institutional shareholders at 46.92% indicates a retail-heavy investor base, which can contribute to higher volatility and limited liquidity. The absence of insurance company participation is particularly noteworthy, as these long-term investors typically favour companies with stable cash flows and superior return metrics—attributes that TVS Srichakra currently lacks.
Stock Performance: Modest Gains, High Volatility
The stock's performance over various timeframes reveals a pattern of volatility with limited wealth creation. Over the past year, TVS Srichakra delivered a 2.91% return, modestly outperforming the Sensex's -3.42% decline and generating positive alpha of 6.33 percentage points. However, this underperformance becomes stark over longer periods.
The three-year return of -7.58% significantly underperformed the Sensex's 25.65% gain, generating negative alpha of 33.23 percentage points. This poor medium-term performance reflects the margin compression and return deterioration the company experienced between FY24 and FY26, when operating margins fell from 10.30% to 7.80

evidence.text:
TVS Srichakra Q2 Results: Profit jumps nearly four-fold as revenue rises 37.5%
- Published OnNov 14, 2026 | 17:42 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 14, 2026 | 17:42 IST
TVS Srichakra reported a nearly four-fold YoY jump in Q2 consolidated profit attributable to owners to ₹44.43 crore, backed by a 37.5% rise in revenue to ₹1,272.63 crore. EBITDA climbed 60.6% to ₹105 crore, lifting margins by 119 bps to 8.25%, while sequential profit rose 30.6%.
Tyres and tubes manufacturer TVS Srichakra reported an almost four-fold year-on-year jump in profit to ₹44 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026 (Q2FY27), compared with ₹11.1 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue from operations rose 37.5% year-on-year to ₹1,273 crore from ₹926 crore in Q2FY26. Operating performance improved at a sharper pace, with earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) climbing 60.6% to ₹105 crore against ₹65 crore a year ago. Consequently, the company's EBITDA margin expanded by 119 basis points to 8.25% from 7.06% in the year-ago quarter.
Total consolidated expenses increased 33.94% year-on-year to ₹1,217.07 crore from ₹908.65 crore in Q2FY26.
