evidence.title: TVS Motor Accelerates European Expansion at EICMA 2026 with Four Production-Ready Models
evidence.text:
TVS Motor Accelerates European Expansion at EICMA 2026 with Four Production-Ready Models
TVS Motor strengthens its European ambitions with three electric two-wheelers, the RTR 125 motorcycle, an expanding dealership network and a 110% increase in Italian sales.
Indian two-wheeler manufacturer TVS Motor Company is accelerating its expansion into Europe, positioning the region as a strategic pillar of its long-term international growth strategy. At EICMA 2026 in Milan, the company showcased four production-ready models, comprising three electric two-wheelers and one petrol-powered motorcycle, while highlighting its growing distribution network and investments in customer-focused engineering.
The four models — TVS Orbiter, TVS M1-S, TVS X and TVS RTR 125 — underline the manufacturer's ambition to compete across electric urban mobility, premium scooters and entry-level performance motorcycles in developed markets. The European expansion comes as TVS Motor targets a larger contribution from its international operations, with overseas business potentially accounting for 40% of overall revenue by 2030.
Europe Emerging as a Strategic Growth Market for TVS Motor
TVS Motor's European expansion represents an important development in its international business strategy. While the company has established a presence across several emerging markets, its increasing focus on Europe reflects an ambition to strengthen its position in technologically advanced and competitive two-wheeler markets.
The company's strategy centres on three priorities: developing products tailored to local riding requirements, expanding distribution and aftersales infrastructure, and leveraging its global engineering and manufacturing capabilities. Europe presents opportunities across electric mobility, performance motorcycles and premium urban transportation. However, successful expansion also requires competitive pricing, regulatory compliance, reliable aftersales support and sustained brand development. TVS Motor is therefore focusing not just on introducing new products but also on building the infrastructure needed to support long-term customer relationships.
TVS Motor's Italian Sales Grow 110% as Dealership Network Expands
Italy has emerged as a key market in TVS Motor's European operations, with the manufacturer reporting a 110% increase in sales over the past year. The company has expanded its Italian retail footprint to more than 100 retailers, creating a distribution base for its growing portfolio of scooters and motorcycles.
Beyond Italy, TVS Motor has established another 22 retailers across Spain and Portugal, while France and Germany are identified as the next markets for network development.
Reported retailer counts at EICMA 2026. Italy's figure is a minimum, not an exact total.
The expansion is particularly significant because distribution and service availability remain important purchasing considerations in European motorcycle and scooter markets.
A stronger dealer network could help TVS Motor build customer confidence, improve parts availability and support repeat purchases as its product portfolio expands. The company has not disclosed absolute Italian sales volumes alongside the reported 110% growth. Therefore, while the percentage indicates strong momentum, the size of its European business cannot be determined from this growth figure alone.
Four Production-Ready Models Target Different European Customers
TVS Motor's EICMA 2026 product showcase featured three electric models and a lightweight petrol-powered motorcycle. The portfolio is intended to address different commuting requirements and riding preferences.
1. TVS Orbiter – Electric Urban Commuter
The Orbiter is positioned as an accessible city-focused electric scooter. Its European specification offers two removable-battery choices, providing flexibility for customers seeking practical urban transportation. The model is aimed at shorter daily journeys and customers prioritising convenience.
2. TVS M1-S – Electric Maxi-Scooter
The M1-S targets customers seeking a larger, more premium electric scooter for urban and suburban travel. It offers a claimed top speed of 105 km/h and underseat storage capable of accommodating a full-face helmet. The model brings a more substantial scooter format to TVS Motor's European electric portfolio.
3. TVS X – Premium Connected Electric Scooter
The TVS X occupies the premium end of the manufacturer's electric scooter range.
Its technology package includes a 10.2-inch touchscreen display and integrated LTE connectivity, reflecting TVS Motor's focus on connected features and a technology-led riding experience.
4. TVS RTR 125 – Entry-Level Performance Motorcycle
The RTR 125 is designed for European A1 licence holders, making it an entry point into TVS Motor's performance-oriented motorcycle portfolio. The motorcycle targets younger riders and first-time motorcycle buyers, with potential to introduce customers to larger models such as the RTR 310 and RR 310. The presence of three electric products among the four production-ready models demonstrates the importance TVS Motor is placing on electrification in its European strategy. However, European prices and confirmed market-by-market launch schedules for these four products have not yet been announced.
TVS RTX 300 Also Set for European Dealerships
Alongside the four production-ready models displayed at EICMA 2026, TVS Motor confirmed that the RTX 300 adventure motorcycle, introduced at the previous year's exhibition, is scheduled to reach European dealerships. The RTX 300 will strengthen the company's presence in the adventure touring segment and complement its existing European motorcycle portfolio, which includes the RR 310, RTR 310 and Ronin. The broader product strategy indicates that TVS Motor is not limiting its European ambitions to electric scooters. Instead, the manufacturer is developing a diversified portfolio that could serve commuter, leisure and performance-oriented riders.
TVS Motor Offers Test Rides at EICMA for the First Time
One of the important developments at EICMA 2026 was TVS Motor's introduction of test-ride opportunities for visitors. For the first time at the Milan motorcycle exhibition, hundreds of visitors experienced TVS Motor models through actual rides rather than only viewing the products at its exhibition stand.
The initiative marks a shift towards direct customer engagement in Europe, where experiencing vehicle performance, handling and refinement can influence purchasing decisions. For TVS Motor, allowing prospective customers, dealers and media representatives to experience its products could support brand recognition and help establish its credentials in a highly competitive market.
TVS Motor Showcases Racing Heritage with '82 Series Collection
TVS Motor also presented its '82 Series Collection in Milan, comprising four one-off concept motorcycles inspired by the company's racing heritage dating back to 1982.
The collection highlights the connection between TVS Racing's motorsport activities and the development of its road-going motorcycles.
The four concepts include:
- '82 Series RR 310: A racing-inspired sports motorcycle celebrating TVS Motor's competition heritage. 
- '82 Series RTR 310: A performance roadster highlighting technologies such as cornering ABS, traction control and wheelie control supported by a six-axis inertial measurement unit. 
- '82 Series RTX 300: An adventure-focused concept combining off-road capability with road-oriented versatility. 
- '82 Series Ronin 250: A neo-retro concept blending scrambler styling, roadster characteristics and urban usability. 
Unlike the four production-ready vehicles, the '82 Series motorcycles are display-only concepts. TVS Motor has not confirmed their commercial production or launch plans.
International Business Could Contribute 40% of TVS Motor's Revenue by 2030
TVS Motor's European expansion forms part of its broader objective to increase international business contributions to overall revenue. The manufacturer has indicated that international operations could potentially account for 40% of total revenue by 2030.
This is a long-term ambition rather than a confirmed financial forecast. Europe could play an important role in achieving this target by providing access to higher-value mobility segments, including premium electric scooters and performance motorcycles.
However, revenue growth will depend on how successfully TVS Motor converts its expanding distribution network into sustainable retail sales. Pricing competitiveness, product localisation, regulatory requirements and long-term ownership support will be key considerations.
Leadership Transition to Support International Expansion
TVS Motor's international growth strategy also coincides with an upcoming leadership transition. Peyman Kargar, currently President of International Business, has been appointed Director and Chief Executive Officer of TVS Motor Company, effective January 27, 2027. He will succeed K. N. Radhakrishnan.
Kargar brings more than three decades of international automotive leadership experience, and his appointment comes as TVS Motor expands its presence across developed overseas markets. The leadership transition could provide continuity to the company's international expansion strategy while strengthening the integration of its domestic and global operations.
Auto Punditz Analysis: Can TVS Motor Establish a Strong European Presence?
TVS Motor's EICMA 2026 participation reflects an important evolution in the company's global strategy — from primarily exporting two-wheelers to building a more established presence in developed markets through localised products, distribution infrastructure and customer engagement.
Three developments stand out.
- First, the company's emphasis on electric mobility provides an opportunity to diversify beyond its traditional motorcycle business. With three electric models covering different price and customer segments, TVS Motor is attempting to address both practical urban mobility and premium connected transportation. 
- Second, the expansion of its European retail network indicates a long-term commitment rather than a product-led entry strategy alone. More than 100 retailers in Italy and 22 additional retailers across Spain and Portugal represent an initial distribution platform that can support future product launches. However, the reported 110% Italian sales growth needs to be viewed alongside the undisclosed absolute volumes. 
- Third, the diversification of its European portfolio could support higher-value international revenue. Products such as the TVS X, M1-S, RTR 310 and RTX 300 could enable the manufacturer to compete beyond the entry-level commuter segment. 
Nevertheless, European expansion presents challenges. TVS Motor will need to establish brand recognition, maintain product competitiveness, develop a dependable aftersales ecosystem and compete against established Japanese and European manufacturers as well as emerging electric mobility brands. The company's decision to combine dedicated engineering capabilities with local distribution and customer engagement suggests a more comprehensive internationalisation strategy.

evidence.title: TVS Motor to raise Brazil production capacity to 1.3 lakh units by 2027
evidence.text:
TVS Motor Company, part of the TVS Venu Group, is stepping up its expansion in Brazil, backed by higher production capacity, a wider retail footprint and an expanded after-sales service network.
The company currently has an annual production capacity of around 110,000 units in Brazil and plans to increase it to 130,000 units by 2027. It has also opened its first flagship store in São Paulo as part of its long-term commitment to the market.
The expansion plan includes strengthening its retail presence through a partnership with Mottu. TVS Motor plans to renovate existing outlets and open exclusive dealerships, initially focusing on the Southeast and Central-West regions. Three new stores are scheduled to open in 2027.
Through its partnership with Mottu, established four years ago, TVS Motor has access to more than 500 points of sale and 168 service locations across Brazil. The locations authorised to service TVS models will have specialised technical teams trained by the manufacturer and local spare-parts availability.
“Brazil is a strategically important market for TVS Motor and a key pillar of our international growth ambitions,” Peyman Kargar, President, International Business, TVS Motor Company, said in a statement.
He added that through the Mottu partnership, the company is investing in local capacity, expanding its retail footprint and strengthening the service ecosystem required to build a sustainable business for the years ahead.
TVS Motor operates in more than 90 countries and has over 50 million customers worldwide. It has been present in 18 Latin American markets for more than 15 years. The expansion in Brazil is part of its international strategy to strengthen regional operations and consolidate its presence in one of the world’s largest motorcycle markets.
The company is also looking to broaden its product portfolio in Brazil to cater to different consumer segments. The models on offer include the TVS NTORQ 125 scooter with connectivity features, the TVS Raider 125 aimed at urban commuters, the TVS Apache 160 for everyday riding and the TVS Apache 200, which features racing-inspired technologies.

Veeramaneni joins the Indian deep-tech company after nearly five years at Ather Energy, where he led motor engineering and subsequently headed the E-Powertrain team. At Naxatra Labs, he will oversee the company's product roadmap, engineering processes and manufacturing development as it works to scale its electric motor and propulsion technology capabilities.
He holds a PhD in Electric Machines from IIT Gandhinagar and has previously worked with automotive component supplier Varroc in motor design.
In his new role, Veeramaneni will focus on integrating product development, engineering and manufacturing operations. His responsibilities include overseeing the product lifecycle from conceptualisation and prototyping through testing, validation and commercial-scale manufacturing. He will also work on manufacturing quality, production efficiency and product reliability.
Naxatra Labs develops electric motor and propulsion technologies for applications across electric mobility, agriculture, drones, robotics and industrial sectors. The company is focusing on expanding its in-house engineering and manufacturing capabilities to develop application-specific solutions for these markets.
Commenting on the appointment, Abhilash Maurya, co-founder and CEO of Naxatra Labs, said the company intends to strengthen its product roadmap, engineering processes and manufacturing capabilities as applications for electric motor and propulsion technologies expand beyond conventional mobility.
Veeramaneni said his role would involve working across the product lifecycle, from design and validation to manufacturing, with a focus on strengthening engineering processes and developing products that meet performance and reliability requirements across different industries.
Naxatra Labs continues to develop indigenous electric motor and propulsion technologies through in-house design, engineering, simulation, prototyping and testing. The appointment is intended to support the integration of its product, engineering and manufacturing functions as the company works towards scaling production.

evidence.title: NSE could draw about $1.5 billion of passive flows if MSCI adds it in February: JM Financial
evidence.text:
National Stock Exchange of India, listed only two months ago, is a high-probability addition to the MSCI India Standard Index in February, according to JM Financial. The brokerage estimates the inclusion could bring about $1.51 billion of passive flows. That matches the roughly $1.5 billion net inflow JM expects from the entire November review.
JM's note, dated November 19, puts the NSE trade at 66 million shares, or 22 times average daily traded volume. LIC carries the heaviest load among the November additions, at 17 times, JM says. In dollar terms, the NSE estimate is more than twice that of Coforge, which at $679 million is the largest of the four November additions (our calculation).
NSE missed the November cut for a procedural reason. JM says it fell short of MSCI's three-month minimum trading history at implementation. The stock listed on September 24. JM puts its market capitalisation at about $45 billion at listing and about $52.3 billion now.
The other likely entrants are smaller. JM rates four more stocks as high probability, all moving up from the small-cap index. They are ATHERENERG ($320 million), GLENMARK ($317 million), KALYANKJIL ($225 million) and UNOMINDA ($202 million). Together with NSE, these five add up to about $2.58 billion, and NSE accounts for 59% of it (our calculation). SAIL is a medium-probability entrant at $184 million. RADICO, BIOCON, APARINDS and ASTERDM are rated low.
JM also expects float-driven weight increases in MEESHO, LENSKART and GROWW as their IPO lock-ins expire.
On the exit side, JM sees no current constituent close to the size trigger. The fall needed ranges from 9% to 29%. It names ICICILIFE and PAGEIND as the two to watch.
The November review is the backdrop. MSCI announced it on November 11, and the changes take effect at the close of November 30. LIC, Coforge, Adani Green Energy and Meesho join the standard index, and PI Industries leaves it. JM estimates gross passive buying of $1.7 billion and selling of $116 million, for a net inflow of about $1.5 billion.
JM's flow figures assume passive assets of about $135 billion linked to MSCI India benchmarks. They are estimates, not MSCI figures.
MSCI will announce its next review on February 9, after market hours, JM says. Changes would take effect on March 1. The open question is how MSCI treats NSE's free float on the review date, since the flow estimate depends on it.

evidence.title: Beyond the big names: 6 NIFTY 500 stocks that quietly rallied up to 200% in six months
evidence.text:
Market News
7 min read | Updated on November 18, 2026, 15:51 IST
SUMMARY
Cupid, Ather Energy, and Laurus Labs are among the top six stocks which have quietly rallied up to the tune of 200% in the last six months despite market volatility. Here's what investors need to know.
Cupid, Ather Energy are among top six NIFTY 500 stocks which have quietly rallied up to 200% in the last six months as of the trading session on Wednesday, November 18. | Image: Shutterstock
Cupid, Ather Energy, and Welspun Living were among the top six NIFTY 500 stocks which have quietly rallied up to 200% in the last six months as of the trading session on Wednesday, November 18, despite the overall volatility and selling pressure in the Indian stock market.
Data showed that these six companies were among several other large and mid-cap stocks which have outperformed the underlying benchmark index, NIFTY 500, significantly over the last six months.
In the six-month time frame, the NIFTY 500 index has delivered 5% returns to investors, while remaining largely flat in the last three months. NSE data also showed that the NIFTY 500 index has gained nearly 6% in the last one-month period.
The silent outperformance comes against the backdrop of consistent momentum, with the stocks gaining a significant portion of their positive performance since the last week of October 2026.
This return addition comes around the same time the broader market indices NIFTY50 and BSE SENSEX staged a massive recovery after two months of selling pressure from foreign investors, as the beaten-down Indian equities looked far more attractive to FIIs due to strong fundamentals.
NSE data also showed that the NIFTY50 index has gained 6.7% in the same period under review, while the NIFTY 500 index lagged behind the benchmark index with lesser gains in the last six months.
This outperformance shows FIIs pumping money into Indian equities have likely been directed towards the blue-chip large-cap stocks listed on the benchmark exchanges, which were subject to a consistent two-month sell-off until October-end 2026.
Personal care products-making FMCG firm Cupid Limited shares have delivered around 200% returns to investors in the last six months, significantly outperforming the benchmark index, with investors focusing on the company’s strong financials and latest Q2 earnings growth.
Data showed that Cupid recorded a 133% YoY surge in net profits to ₹56 crore in Q2 FY27, in comparison to ₹24 crore in the same period a year ago. Similarly, revenues also increased 122.4% year-on-year to ₹188 crore in the period from earlier ₹84 crore levels in the previous year.
Despite the growth in top-line and bottom-line numbers, the margins of the condom-maker remained under pressure, contracting due to the elevated cost of raw materials in the September quarter.
On a YTD basis, Cupid shares have risen 243% so far this calendar year, according to NSE data.
Two-wheeler EV maker Ather Energy shares have delivered around 110% returns to investors in the last six months, significantly outperforming the underlying benchmark index in the period, with strong buying sentiment among investors.
The stock has shown a consistent rally in the last six months, with Ather Energy’s stock gaining a significant portion of its value since the beginning of November 2026.
The sentiment for the stock was further aided by the company posting its first-ever net profit of ₹1.26 crore against a net loss a year ago, due to the 63% YoY surge in revenue from core operations to ₹1,464 crore.
The strong growth was a result of elevated demand outperforming the overall supply of the company’s products in the market. On a YTD basis, Ather’s stock has risen around 160% in so far in the current year.
Jewellery maker Kalyan Jewellers shares have delivered around 97% returns on their investment in the last six months, significantly outperforming the underlying index as the elevated gold prices and the festive season momentum powered the overall gains.
The strong buying momentum was powered by strong financial performance in the quarterly results and the elevated precious metal gold prices in the market, which, in turn, inflated the company’s profits and margins during the period.
In its latest Q2 earnings, Kalyan Jewellers posted a 64% YoY growth in profits against the backdrop of a 32% increase in topline growth to ₹10,323 crore. The company’s H1 FY27 profits grew 48% to ₹776 crore against ₹525 crore in the year-ago period as it recorded a 38% increase in revenues in the first half of the current fiscal year.
The outlook for gold remains under pressure in the near-term due to the hawkish stance market bets of the US Fed increasing their key interest rates.
Welspun Living shares have gained 91% in the last six months, outperforming the benchmark NIFTY 500 index in the same period, as investors focused on the home textile product maker’s consistent revenue growth and healthy operating profits.
Data showed that Welspun Living recorded a 4.34% sequential growth in profits to ₹169.66 crore in Q2 FY27, from ₹162.61 crore in the first quarter of the current fiscal year. Earlier, in the June quarter results, the company’s profits surged 53% to ₹162.61 crore.
On the revenue front, the company’s revenues were at ₹2,869 crore, up from ₹2,828 crore in the previous quarter of the current fiscal year.
The stock has witnessed significant volume momentum in the last six months, resulting in massive gains on the stock exchange.
Welspun Corp. shares have retracted some gains from their highest level in the last six months, but despite the pullback, the stock has delivered more than 77% returns on their investment, significantly outperforming the NIFTY 500 index.
Although the iron and steel products maker was impacted by the monsoon season downturn in volumes, the revenues witnessed growth to ₹4,698.55 crore in the September quarter, with the company turning in profits of ₹495.09 crore in the period.
Market experts predict that in the third quarter of the current fiscal year, the steel companies will improve their profitability with higher steel prices in the market, softer iron-ore costs and operating leverage expected to outweigh the coking-coal headwind.
On a YTD basis, Welspun Corp. shares have gained nearly 180% this year.
Pharmaceutical and biotechnology company Laurus Labs has delivered more than 76% returns in the last six months, outperforming the NIFTY 500 index as investors were largely focused on the healthcare sector amid the wider market selloff.
Along with the elevated interest for defensive sector stocks like pharma, investors were also focused on the earnings performance and consistent growth of Laurus Labs over the past few quarters.
Data showed that Laurus Labs posted a 20% QoQ growth in profits to ₹436 crore, from ₹362 crore in the previous quarter. The company’s healthy profit growth comes against the backdrop of a 9% sequential increase in overall topline growth to ₹2,219 crore in the September quarter.
Historically, we have seen that in times of volatility, investors have looked for defensive bets in the domestic market. Laurus’s story also comes in line with the market sentiment, which has prompted investors to carry out value buying over the last six months.

evidence.title: Ather’s connected EV strategy faces a tougher test as India’s e2W market expands
evidence.text:
India’s electric two-wheeler market is moving beyond its early subsidy-led phase, with connected software, product dependability and after-sales support becoming more important to buyers, according to an industry analysis published on 16 November 2026. The report estimates that electric two-wheelers accounted for around 6.5% of total two-wheeler registrations in FY2026, while segment volumes grew approximately 22% year on year to about 1.4 million units.
The competitive field includes established manufacturers such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp, alongside electric vehicle companies including Ather Energy and Ola Electric. Reporting on the first half of a recent fiscal year indicated that TVS, Bajaj, Hero and Ather captured nearly all of the segment’s additional growth during that period. Ola Electric, meanwhile, lost market share, suggesting that pricing alone is becoming a less decisive factor in India’s electric scooter market.
Software and charging remain central to Ather’s proposition
Ather, founded in 2013 by Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain, has built its electric scooter business around a combination of in-house hardware and software. The company develops its own battery packs and motor controllers, while its vehicle software platform is branded AtherStack. It also operates Ather Grid, a proprietary public fast-charging network intended to support the use of its electric scooters beyond home charging.
The company’s product line began with the Ather 450, launched in 2018, and later expanded with successive 450-series updates. Its other major product is the Ather Rizta, a family-focused scooter introduced in 2024. According to Ather’s sales disclosures, the Rizta had crossed 300,000 cumulative units and represented approximately 76% of the company’s portfolio volume in FY2026. That makes the Rizta the primary contributor to Ather’s current product volumes, rather than the 450 range alone.
Why the shift matters for Indian buyers
The market’s changing competitive dynamics have implications for electric scooter users in India. A larger installed base makes access to service centres, spare parts, software support and charging infrastructure increasingly important. The analysis identifies reliability, service networks and after-sales experience as areas that are gaining weight alongside the purchase price. For connected electric vehicles, the ownership experience also depends on the software layer and on how effectively the manufacturer maintains the features linked to it.
Ather Energy became a listed company on the BSE and NSE on 6 May 2025, after an IPO priced at ₹321 per share. The offering raised approximately ₹2,980.76 crore, comprising a fresh issue of about ₹2,626 crore and an offer for sale of roughly ₹355 crore. Its listing-day closing figures were slightly below the issue price, reflecting a cautious initial market response even as the company continued to report operating volumes.
For Indian electric two-wheeler customers, the broader takeaway is that the category is becoming more established but also more demanding. Manufacturers now have to compete across the vehicle, the connected software experience, charging access and support after purchase. Ather’s concentration of volume in the Rizta and its continued reliance on AtherStack and Ather Grid show how those elements are being combined within one product ecosystem, while the wider market’s expansion brings stronger competition from both traditional two-wheeler companies and electric vehicle specialists.

evidence.title: Ather Energy Crosses 3 Lakh Electric Scooter Sales in 2026
evidence.text:
Ather Energy has crossed 3 lakh electric scooter sales in a single calendar year for the first time, strengthening its position in India’s rapidly expanding electric two-wheeler market. The Bengaluru-based manufacturer delivered 3,01,133 scooters between January 1 and November 6, 2026, registering 67% year-on-year growth, according to Vahan registration data.
The milestone gives Ather a 16.32% share of India’s electric two-wheeler market, its highest market share to date. The company has become the third Indian electric two-wheeler manufacturer to cross the 3 lakh annual sales mark in 2026, following TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto. Its performance also puts it on track to achieve more than 3.5 lakh sales by the end of the year.
Ather Records 67% Sales Growth in 2026
Ather’s performance reflects a significant improvement in demand for its electric scooter portfolio.
Between January 1 and November 6, the company delivered 3,01,133 units, compared with 2,16,463 units during the entire calendar year 2025.
Its market share increased to 16.32% from 16.12% in 2025, making 2026 its strongest year in terms of market penetration so far.
The company crossed the 3 lakh milestone despite facing manufacturing capacity constraints that have affected the availability of some models.
According to Autocar Professional’s analysis of Vahan data, Ather’s sales also accounted for approximately 36% of its cumulative retail deliveries since entering the electric scooter market in 2018.
Ather Energy’s key sales figures:
The figures represent retail deliveries recorded through November 6, rather than completed full-year sales.
Ather Ranks Third Behind TVS and Bajaj
Ather’s milestone places it among India’s three largest electric two-wheeler manufacturers by retail sales in 2026.
TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto continue to lead the market, while Ather has maintained its third position ahead of Hero MotoCorp’s Vida electric scooter business.
The manufacturer rankings between January 1 and November 6 were:
The figures show that Ather has established a substantial position in India’s competitive electric scooter industry.
The company is still behind TVS and Bajaj in overall volumes, but its 67% annual growth demonstrates increasing demand for its products.
The wider electric two-wheeler market recorded approximately 18.4 lakh retail deliveries during the same period, providing a larger market for established manufacturers and newer EV brands.
Monthly Sales Show Consistent Demand
Ather recorded sales above 28,000 units in most months of 2026, with March emerging as its strongest month.
The company delivered 36,630 electric scooters in March, its highest monthly sales figure during the year.
October also delivered a strong performance, with 31,941 units sold.
Ather’s monthly retail sales in 2026:
Ather crossed the 30,000-unit monthly sales threshold six times during the 13 months leading up to November 2026.
The figures indicate that demand has remained relatively strong throughout the year rather than depending on a single festive sales period.
Rizta and 450 Series Support Ather’s Growth
Ather’s expanding product portfolio has played an important role in its sales performance.
The company operates two major product lines: the Rizta family scooter range and the performance-oriented Ather 450 series.
The Rizta has become an important volume driver since its introduction in April 2024. Designed for everyday family use, it offers a larger seat, practical storage and a more convenience-focused riding experience.
In May 2026, Ather announced that Rizta had crossed 3 lakh cumulative sales within two years of its launch.
The company also reported that Rizta accounted for approximately 76% of its total sales volume in FY26.
Meanwhile, the 450 series continues to attract customers looking for performance-oriented electric scooters.
The combination of these product categories has allowed Ather to reach different customer segments instead of relying on a single model.
Konarc Manufacturing Constraints Limit Additional Sales
Ather introduced its Konarc scooter family in August 2026, targeting a broader section of India’s electric scooter market.
The product was expected to help the company expand beyond its existing customer base and increase sales volumes.
However, manufacturing constraints have limited its contribution so far.
According to Autocar India’s report, the company has faced difficulties meeting demand for its existing scooters while also scaling production of the new model.
Ather has consequently changed its planned launch sequence for the Konarc variants, prioritising mid-range versions ahead of the entry-level variant.
The base version is now expected in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.
The company is also developing its manufacturing capabilities through a new facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra.
Additional production capacity could help Ather improve vehicle availability and support higher deliveries as demand grows.
India’s Electric Scooter Market Becomes More Competitive
Ather’s sales milestone comes amid increasing competition in India’s electric two-wheeler market.
TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto have expanded their electric scooter businesses through their iQube and Chetak product families, respectively.
Hero MotoCorp is also developing its Vida brand, while other manufacturers are competing through new products, pricing and distribution networks.
The market is benefiting from increasing consumer interest in electric mobility, improvements in battery technology and the expansion of charging infrastructure.
However, manufacturers continue to face challenges involving battery costs, production capacity, competition and customer expectations around vehicle range and after-sales service.
For Ather, maintaining its market position will require continued investment in manufacturing, product development and its charging network.
The Bigger Picture
Ather’s achievement highlights the increasing maturity of India’s electric two-wheeler industry.
Crossing 3 lakh annual deliveries indicates that electric scooters are becoming a more established choice for Indian consumers. The growth of family-oriented models such as Rizta also suggests that demand is expanding beyond early adopters and performance-focused buyers.
The competitive landscape is changing as well. TVS and Bajaj have established strong sales positions, while Ather is strengthening its place among the leading manufacturers. As production capacity increases and more affordable models enter the market, competition is likely to intensify.
Looking Ahead
Ather is targeting more than 3.5 lakh electric scooter sales by the end of 2026, which would represent another record for the company. Achieving that target will depend on maintaining demand for the Rizta and 450 series while improving production and availability of the Konarc range. Its manufacturing expansion in Maharashtra could become important in supporting the next phase of growth.
The larger opportunity lies in sustaining market share as India’s electric two-wheeler market expands. Ather has demonstrated strong sales momentum in 2026, but its ability to compete with TVS and Bajaj will depend on manufacturing scale, product pricing, customer experience and continued improvements in its electric scooter portfolio.

evidence.title: Ather Energy's Market Share Push: Growth, Constraints and the Konarc Gamble
evidence.text:
Ather Energy's Market Share Push: Growth, Constraints and the Konarc Gamble
Ather Energy has crossed a significant milestone in India's electric two-wheeler market.
This puts Ather in third place behind TVS Motor (26% share) and Bajaj Auto (22%), with Hero MotoCorp's Vida in fourth at 11%. Yet the headline numbers mask a more complex story of capacity constraints, volatile monthly sales and a carefully staged product rollout that is testing Ather's ability to sustain its momentum.
March 2026 stands out as Ather's strongest month yet, with retail sales hitting 36,630 units. This wasn't a fluke. Q4 FY26 wholesale volumes reached 83,418 units, up 76% year-on-year, with Ather holding an 18.6% market share for the quarter. The Rizta family scooter, launched in April 2024, became the engine of this growth, accounting for about 76% of FY2026 volumes. Ather's distribution network also expanded aggressively, with Experience Centres roughly doubling from 351 to 700 during FY26.
But the months that followed saw volatility. Ather has crossed the 30,000-unit monthly sales mark six times since October 2025, including March, June, July, September and October 2026. Yet August sales fell 6% month-on-month to 28,708 units. The primary culprit wasn't demand—it was supply.
Management estimates about 18,000 to 20,000 units of monthly retail demand remain unmet. Transcript +1
The Konarc series, launched on August 29, 2026, represents Ather's most aggressive move into the mass market. The S variants span three battery options: the S 100 (2.1 kWh, ₹99,999), S 125 (2.7 kWh, ₹1.22 lakh) and S 161 (3.5 kWh, ₹1.45 lakh), all ex-showroom Bengaluru. A range-topping S 200 km variant is expected in Q3 2027, while the feature-rich Z line (125 km and 161 km) is slated for Q2 2027.
Pricing is sharp. The Konarc undercuts the TVS iQube by about ₹18,375 at the base level, with a claimed range of 100 km against the iQube's 94 km. The Bajaj Chetak starts around ₹1.19 lakh, while Hero Vida's VX2 Go FB is priced at ₹1.13 lakh. This positions Konarc to compete directly in the ₹1–1.25 lakh mass segment, where Ather has historically been less present.
However, the rollout is deliberately staggered. Only the S 125 and S 161 variants are currently available, with deliveries beginning in September 2026. The entry-level S 100 is deferred until Q4 FY27 (January–March 2027), and management has made it clear this variant will launch only once the Aurangabad (AURIC) capacity is online.
The capacity crunch is real. Ather's board approved a ₹122 crore expansion package to scale annual manufacturing capability from 9.20 lakh to 11.45 lakh units. This includes ₹58 crore at Hosur (adding 6,000 units per month) and ₹64 crore at AURIC Phase 1. Trial production at AURIC is expected in Q3 FY27, with full capex installation by Q4 FY27. Until then, Ather is leaving sales on the table. Investor Presentation +1
Despite these constraints, Ather crossed the 3 lakh annual sales milestone for the first time in 2026 and is on track to reach 3.5 lakh units by year-end. The company has delivered 3,03,092 units between January 1 and November 9, 2026. This achievement underscores the strength of underlying demand—enquiries rose about 109% to over 10 lakh, and pre-orders doubled to about 1.8 lakh in Q2 FY27. Transcript
Ather's infrastructure strategy differs markedly from its competitors. In Delhi-NCR, a key northern market, Ather has built 17 experience centres and 209 fast-charging Ather Grid points. This network supported a single-day handover event of 500 Konarc scooters in late October, highlighting surging urban adoption. Ather riders also have access to more than 5,000 public fast chargers pan-India, combining Ather Grid points with partner chargers using the LECCS connector.
TVS partners with Jio-bp for public charging, while Bajaj relies on home chargers and dealer-based fast charging for its Chetak 35-series. Both legacy players bet that their extensive dealer networks and home-charging-first approach are sufficient for city riders. This strategy has worked so far—TVS holds 27% market share in October 2026, and Bajaj 21.9%, both ahead of Ather's 14.2%.
Ather's regional focus is also shifting. The Konarc rollout prioritises northern and western markets (Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Punjab), with southern markets following once AURIC is live. This phased expansion aims to reduce Ather's historical dependence on its southern home markets, where it has been strongest. Transcript +1
Ather's profitability is improving but remains fragile. Q2 FY27 adjusted gross margin was 24.0%, up from 22% a year earlier, with EBITDA margin reaching 5%—the first time the business achieved positive EBITDA excluding other income. Net profit turned positive at ₹1.26 crore, compared to a loss of ₹154.07 crore a year earlier. Transcript +1
The margin improvement came despite a 9.4% hit from commodity inflation. Structural gains of 5.3% from price hikes, value engineering and permanent cost reductions offset some of this pressure, while 2.7% came from SKU management and reduced incentives—a more temporary benefit.
However, working capital is tightening. Working capital days narrowed from (50) to (36) in Q2 FY27, meaning the supplier-funded cushion has reduced. Staggered variant launches mean Ather must invest in parts and tooling ahead of deliveries, while the entry variant waits for capacity. This creates cash flow pressures that diversified competitors like TVS and Bajaj, with their large internal combustion engine businesses, are better positioned to absorb. Investor Presentation
Hero Vida remains the immediate threat in the race for third place. In October 2026, Vida recorded 29,958 registrations, narrowing the gap with Ather to just 1,875 units. Vida's sales grew 81.6% year-on-year, and its VX2 Go FB and Plus variants, supported by a battery-as-a-service option, are gaining traction.
TVS and Bajaj continue to dominate. TVS strengthened its leadership with 60,494 registrations in October, while Bajaj held second with 49,127 units. Both companies are also expanding capacity—Bajaj is raising Chetak capacity to 80,000 units per month by Q4 FY27, and its overall company capacity is expected to rise from 6.25 lakh to 7.75 lakh units per month over the next 6 to 9 months. Transcript +1
Ather's path to sustaining its 16.3% market share hinges on execution. The AURIC Phase 1 expansion is critical—without it, the entry-level Konarc S 100 cannot launch, and Ather risks ceding ground in the mass segment. The Z line and S 200 km variants, launching in 2027, will test Ather's ability to differentiate on range and features against Vida and others.
The company has deliberately paused experience centre expansion to avoid dealer inventory pile-ups, with plans to restart additions from Q4 FY27. Hundreds of location agreements are on hold until capacity improves. Transcript +1
In the end, Ather's story in 2026 is one of demand outstripping supply. The 3 lakh milestone and record market share are achievements, but they also highlight the constraints holding the company back. As capacity ramps and the full Konarc portfolio rolls out, the real test begins: can Ather convert its engineering-led brand into a mass-market scale player without sacrificing the profitability it has only just begun to achieve?

evidence.title: Ather Energy Sales October 2026: Dispatches Rise 31% to 33,786 Units, Konarc Records 83% Monthly Growth
evidence.text:
Ather Energy Sales October 2026: Dispatches Rise 31% to 33,786 Units, Konarc Records 83% Monthly Growth
Ather Energy's October 2026 electric scooter dispatches reached 33,786 units, registering 30.8% year-on-year growth over 25,829 units in October 2025. Volumes also increased 12.2% month-on-month from 30,121 units in September 2026.
Rizta remained Ather's largest contributor, accounting for nearly 58% of total dispatches, despite a marginal decline in both annual and monthly comparisons. Meanwhile, Konarc emerged as the strongest sequential growth driver, with dispatches increasing 83% over September.
Ather October 2026 – Model-wise Sales
- Rizta: Recorded 19,505 units, declining 2% YoY and 2% MoM. Despite the marginal contraction, Rizta remained Ather's highest-volume model, contributing 57.7% of total October dispatches. 
- Konarc: Dispatches reached 7,562 units, rising 83% from September's 4,140 units. The model added 3,422 units sequentially, accounting for most of Ather's net monthly volume increase. 
- 450: Registered 6,719 units, reflecting 9% MoM growth over 6,168 units in September. The model contributed approximately 19.9% of Ather's October volumes. 
Auto Punditz Take
Ather's October performance highlights growing volumes beyond its established Rizta portfolio. While Rizta continued to account for the majority of dispatches, its marginal decline contrasted with strong sequential growth in Konarc and the broader 450 category.
Konarc was particularly important to October's performance, contributing almost the entire net month-on-month increase. However, Rizta's 57.7% share indicates that Ather remains significantly dependent on its largest-selling product.
The key trend to watch is whether Ather can sustain growth across multiple models while maintaining Rizta's volumes. Consistent demand beyond its flagship family scooter would help strengthen the company's position in India's increasingly competitive electric two-wheeler market.

Shares of electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy Ltd. gained another 7% on Tuesday, October 27, extending the previous session’s 17% rally after the company reported its first-ever quarterly net profit and turned EBITDA-positive in Q2 FY27.
Brokerages remained positive on the stock, with HSBC retaining its ‘Buy’ rating and raising its price target to ₹1,800. Nomura also maintained a ‘Buy’ recommendation, with a target price of ₹2,070.

However, a muted market response to the Konarc scooter range remains a near-term risk.
Nomura highlighted Ather’s better-than-expected average selling prices (ASPs) and margins, along with stronger bookings. The company’s EBITDA margin came in at 0.8%, against Nomura’s estimate of -2.6% and the consensus estimate of -2.7%.
The brokerage said the Konarc rollout improves growth visibility and reaffirmed Ather as its top pick in the two-wheeler space.
Nomura also considers Ather’s valuation attractive at 4 times its estimated FY29 enterprise value-to-sales, given its higher growth potential relative to peers.
Ather Energy Q2 FY27 results
Ather Energy reported a net profit of ₹1.26 crore for the quarter, compared with a net loss of ₹154 crore in the year-ago period. EBITDA stood at ₹11.3 crore, against a loss of ₹133 crore a year earlier, while the EBITDA margin came in at 0.77%.
Revenue rose 62.8% year-on-year to ₹1,464 crore from ₹899 crore, supported by a 42% increase in volumes to 93,000 units.
Separately, Ather Energy’s board approved capacity expansion at its manufacturing facilities in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, to support higher production and meet future demand.
Capacity expansion plans
Ather expects trial production at Phase 1 of its Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar facility to begin in the coming weeks, with capex and capacity installation scheduled for completion by Q4 FY27. The company’s additional capacity of 6,000 units per month at Hosur is expected to become operational this quarter.
Phase 1 at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar is slated to add capacity of 12,500 units per month by Q2 FY28. With these additions, Ather’s total installed annual capacity is expected to reach 11.4 lakh units by Q2 FY28.
Ather has initially launched the mid-range SR2 and SR3 variants of Konarc, with the entry-level version scheduled for Q4 FY27. Management expects the entry-level variant to contribute higher volumes.
The rollout will expand from Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Punjab, before reaching southern markets. The southern expansion is expected to follow the commissioning of the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar facility. Ather expects its addressable market to widen over the next 12–18 months as additional Konarc variants are introduced.
Ather does not plan to increase ex-showroom prices further over the next few quarters and has ruled out additional hikes this quarter. Management said a like-for-like comparison could eventually see Konarc deliver 6–10% higher gross margins than the Rizta. However, volatility in component costs makes the near-term cost outlook difficult to predict.
Ather has deliberately moderated its dealer network expansion to avoid leaving dealers with inventory that cannot be served by available supplies. The company expects to resume a more aggressive expansion pace from late Q3 or Q4 FY27 as additional manufacturing capacity comes online.
Management did not provide a launch timeline or guidance for an electric motorcycle, saying development and technology work remains ongoing.

evidence.title: Ather Energy Reports ₹1.26 Crore Profit In Q2 FY27, Plans 2.25 Lakh Units Capacity Expansion By FY28
evidence.text:
Mumbai: Ather Energy on October 26, 2026, announced a consolidated profit after tax of ₹1.26 crore for the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q2 FY27). This compares to a loss of ₹154 crore in the same quarter last year. The company's total income for the quarter stood at ₹1,527 crore, marking a 62% increase year-on-year.
Operational Highlights
The electric two-wheeler manufacturer reported a 42% year-on-year increase in volumes, reaching 93,211 units in Q2 FY27. EBITDA for the quarter was ₹74.2 crore, making it the second consecutive EBITDA-positive quarter for Ather Energy, with the EBITDA margin improving by approximately 1,450 basis points year-on-year to 4.9%.
Capacity Expansion Plans
To meet rising demand, Ather Energy plans to increase its annual production capacity by 2.25 lakh units across its Hosur and AURIC facilities. This expansion will bring the combined installed annual capacity to approximately 11.4 lakh units by Q2 FY28. The company will invest about ₹122 crore in these capacity enhancements.
Demand and Orders
Customer interest showed a sharp rise, with enquiries increasing by 109% year-on-year to about 10 lakh in Q2 FY27. Pre-orders more than doubled to 1.80 lakh units during the quarter. The Hosur facility operated at 98% capacity utilisation.
New Product Launch
During the quarter, Ather launched Konarc, its first scooter built on the new EL platform, at Ather Community Day on August 29, 2026. Konarc features a metal body, long-travel suspension, and a 14-inch front wheel. It also includes new technologies such as MagicKey keyless access, AutoPop hands-free seat opening, and AirWalk motor assist.
Management Commentary
Tarun Mehta, Co-founder and CEO, Ather Energy, said the company delivered a strong quarter with topline growth and a positive bottomline despite commodity prices and supply chain disruptions. Mehta added that demand more than doubled year-on-year and that the company is augmenting production capacity to meet this growth.

Battery cells produced in India are expected to cost roughly 20% more than Chinese imports, Anurag Choudhary, Chairman, Managing Director and CEO of Himadri Speciality Chemical Ltd, a battery cell component maker, told BT earlier in October. But cell producers say mandating localization of cells is critical build an ecosystem in the country. “We have start mandating more localisation...Otherwise, the entire story starts to fall apart,” Vikramadithya Gourineni, executive director of Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, told BT earlier this year.
Gourineni, however, agrees that India is a price-sensitive market and for OEMs cost and pricing will dominate the decision-making. “My customer is only willing to pay so much, and their will already be a premium because I will have to charge a higher cost because my own industrialisation is just starting. If you add domestic materials to that, it all adds up,” he adds. Amara Raja has partnered with Ola Electric’s rival Ather Energy to develop and supply Nickel Manganese Cobalt (NMC) and Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) lithium-ion battery cells for Ather's electric two-wheelers.
Meanwhile, Ola Electric is also targeting a gradual increase in cell production and manufacturing yields as it scales operations. Aggarwal said NMC cell yields were already in the mid-70% range, with a roadmap to improve them to the mid-80s over the next few months.
Ola Electric said its LFP technology is ready and that it has begun scaling up production this quarter. The company expects manufacturing yields to reach around 70% by the end of Q4FY27, when it plans to start integrating its in-house LFP cells into its vehicles. Yields are projected to improve further to approximately 90% in Q1FY28.
The company said achieving a 70% yield would make manufacturing its own cells cost-neutral compared with sourcing them from external suppliers. At an 85% yield, in-house production could deliver cost savings of around 10-15% over externally procured cells.
Ola Electric expects its automotive business to consume 2–3 GWh of cell capacity in FY28.

evidence.title: Ola Electric Shuts Stores, Shifts To Dealers: What Changes For Customers Buying And Owning Its E-Scooters?
evidence.text:
Ola Electric Mobility is shutting down most of its company-owned retail outlets across India by December 2026 to transition entirely to an independent dealer-led sales and service network.
The electric two-wheeler maker stopped accepting vehicle orders through its direct-to-consumer (D2C) stores on 1 November, aiming to slash fixed operating expenses by around ₹50 crore and improve working capital. While Chairman and Managing Director Bhavish Aggarwal maintains that customer demand outstrips supply and operations have stabilised, market analysts point to a 39 per cent year-on-year revenue drop in Q2 FY27 and persistent after-sales bottlenecks.
For existing Ola scooter owners, the shift means routine maintenance, warranty claims, and spare parts support will progressively move from company-run experience centres to authorised third-party dealerships, which are targeted to expand to over 700 outlets by March 2027.
Inside the Numbers, Reassurances
Speaking during the company’s Q2 FY27 earnings call on 12 November, Ola Electric CFO Deepak Rastogi confirmed that the transition began on 4 September and had already scaled to 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores across the country by 8 November.
The company plans to grow this dealer footprint to 450 outlets by December 2026 and more than 700 by the end of the financial year in March 2027. Addressing concerns over slowing momentum—after quarterly vehicle registrations slipped 19.5 per cent year-on-year to 41,653 units—Bhavish Aggarwal stated, “Demand is no longer our constraint… Business has stabilised, the balance sheet has stabilized, and operations have stabilized.”
From Direct-to-Consumer Pioneer
When Ola Electric entered India’s electric mobility market, it aggressively championed a Tesla-inspired D2C model, bypassing traditional middlemen to sell scooters exclusively online and through company-owned experience centres.
However, as sales volumes grew, the lack of decentralised service infrastructure led to widespread consumer complaints over delayed repairs, software glitches, and spare-part shortages. By August 2026, facing stiff competition from legacy automakers such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto, and Hero MotoCorp alongside rival Ather Energy, Ola announced it would open both sales and service operations to franchise partners. Under the revised structure, independent dealers bear showroom overheads and purchase inventory upfront, relieving Ola of heavy retail lease and staffing burdens.
What Existing Owners Should Do
Automotive retail analysts note that while shifting to local dealers could eventually bring service bays closer to riders in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns, the immediate transition carries execution risks.
Consumer mobility experts advise current Ola Electric owners to keep digital copies of their purchase invoices, extended warranty certificates, and service histories handy on the Ola Electric app. Before visiting a neighbourhood outlet for repairs or battery checks, riders are encouraged to verify whether the centre has transitioned into an authorised partner dealership to avoid wasted trips during the December store-closure window.
The Logical Indian’s Perspective
At The Logical Indian, we believe that genuine innovation in clean mobility must go hand-in-hand with accountability and empathy toward everyday consumers.
While transitioning to a dealer-led network is a pragmatic business step for Ola Electric to stay financially resilient, the hundreds of thousands of early adopters who trusted the brand deserve seamless, stress-free after-sales support during this handover. True progress in India’s green transition depends on transparent communication, reliable service, and putting customer dignity ahead of rapid expansion targets. As Ola Electric rewrites its retail playbook, we hope this partnership model fosters stronger local accountability and restores rider confidence. If you own an electric two-wheeler, how has your after-sales service experience been—and do you think local dealerships will improve customer care?

evidence.title: Ola Electric hands the keys to dealers. What led to this shift in gears?
evidence.text:
Ola Electric hands the keys to dealers. What led to this shift in gears?
For long, Ola Electric ran its own showrooms and sold directly to customers. Now it is shifting to a dealer-led model with plans to have 700 dealer outlets by March 2027. What prompted this reset and what should the company do for it to work?
On November 1, Ola Electric stopped taking orders at its own showrooms. Most of them will be shut by December, as Ola moves away from the direct-to-consumer model that defined the company and turns to a dealer-led business.
Ola has recorded this in its investor presentation filed with the NSE and BSE on November 12 under Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. The document covers the unaudited standalone and consolidated results for the second quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026.
In its Q2 FY27 shareholders' letter, dated November 12, the company calls the move towards a dealer-led model a "reset". What prompted this 'reset'?
The numbers tell part of the story. Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs 828 crore in Q1 FY26. It fell to Rs 690 crore in Q2, then Rs 470 crore in the next quarter, and bottomed out at Rs 265 crore in Q4 FY26.
Interestingly, the electric two-wheeler market has been growing in recent times. In Q2 FY27, industry volumes reached 5,99,317 units, up 82.7% year on year, and EV penetration in the two-wheeler market touched 11.2%. However, Ola's Q2 revenue fell 39% to Rs 421 crore in FY27.
The service record behind the reset
The shareholders' letter says little about why the direct model had to go, but public records give an indication.
The problems began with service. Between September 2023 and August 2024, the maker of electric two-wheelers received 10,644 complaints through the National Consumer Helpline. Of these, 3,389 concerned service delays and 1,899 were about delayed deliveries, according to media reports.
On October 7, 2024 the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) issued a show-cause notice giving the company 15 days to respond, and the complaints it cited included charges during the free service period, refusals or delays in warranty work, and unsatisfactory repairs.
Ola's response was that 99.1% of the complaints had been resolved to the customer's complete satisfaction. But the regulator reportedly found that 80% of those claimed resolutions had not been implemented, and the CCPA widened its inquiry.
Founder Bhavish Aggarwal promised the backlog would clear soon, and said the company would double its own service network to 1,000 centres by December 2024. Around the same time, a public spat erupted between Aggarwal and the comedian Kunal Kamra, who had taken up the customers' service complaints.
Subsequently, the company-owned store network ran into another problem. In March 2025, Bloomberg reported that only about 100 of Ola's roughly 3,400 showrooms displayed the trade certificate that the Motor Vehicles Act requires. Ola called the report misplaced and prejudiced.
Transport officials raided at least 26 stores in Maharashtra and six in Madhya Pradesh and impounded 60 scooters. Maharashtra's transport minister later said that of 432 stores inspected in April 2025, only 47 held valid certificates, and that the other 385 were shut.
The shareholders' letter does not connect any of this to the move towards a dealer network.
A new front end, built in eight weeks
The first set of dealer outlets became operational on September 4, on Janmashtami. By Diwali, on November 8, Ola says it had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 sales outlets. The company is planning about 450 outlets by December 2026 and 700 by March 2027.
Volumes through the new channel have climbed quickly. Wholesale orders were 3,955 vehicles in September and 13,505 in October. Ola expects 16,000 in November and 20,000 in December. Production is meant to keep pace, from 9,235 vehicles in August and 14,092 in October to about 25,000 in December.
The case Ola makes for dealers is financial as much as commercial. Under the old model, the company owned the stores, and carried the stock and the working capital. Now, it says, dealers pay for vehicles when they order them and hold the inventory in their own outlets.
Auto borrowings have fallen from Rs 2,422 crore in December 2024 to Rs 337 crore in September 2026, helped by a QIP and rights issue, and the company expects the auto business to generate free cash flow in the near term.
Operating expenses are meant to fall by a further Rs 50 crore as the company-owned stores close.
What the letter does not hide
The letter is candid in places. Inventory in the dealer channel built up through October and November, and registrations were a little slower in October. Ola puts channel inventory at about 15 days, and under a week in the earliest showrooms. It says that in markets where dealers opened early and have settled in, its market share is now well above pre-transition levels, though the company doe not give any figure.
There is also a supply problem. About 5,000 vehicles with paid orders in September were delayed by a week, running into October, because chargers were unavailable. The company says it is facing a paid order backlog and the constraint is its supply chain, not its plant, which it says can build well above the current output.
Hence the letter's headline claim: demand is no longer the constraint, supply is. The claim deserves attention. Wholesale figures count vehicles sent to dealers, not vehicles sold to riders, and the letter admits slower registrations in October.
The margin trade
Dealers do not come free. Ola says gross margin, which held at about 29.9% in Q2, will dip a little in Q3 and Q4 because of the dealer rollout, while operating margin should improve meaningfully. Excluding PLI incentives, Q2 gross margin was 26.5%. Gross margin per unit was roughly Rs 35,000, against an average selling price of about Rs 1,21,000, down from about Rs 1,68,000 in FY23.
The losses remain large. Operating EBITDA was a loss of Rs 218 crore in Q2FY27, wider than Rs 165 crore in Q1, and the loss after tax was Rs 362 crore. Consolidated free cash flow was negative Rs 371 crore, with the auto segment accounting for Rs 134 crore of that and the cell business most of the rest. Total borrowings are down from Rs 3,132 crore to Rs 1,819 crore.
The product roadmap
Going forward, Ola is betting on two things to win customers back: a cheaper scooter and its own batteries.
The cheaper scooter is the S1Z, which is expected to be delivered to customers by March 2027. It uses a battery type that Ola says costs less to build. The company plans to fit the same battery to its existing models. It also says that, as dealers open, demand will shift towards its premium scooters and motorcycles.
The batteries come from Ola’s own factory, which has reached its first 6 gigawatt-hours of capacity ahead of schedule. The government has extended a production incentive for the plant to 2031, and Ola expects the payments to kick in from January to March.
According to the company, making its own batteries costs the same as buying them, if about 70% of those made pass quality checks, and 10 to 15% less if 85% of them pass checks.
What to watch out for
A company not only owns its product but also owns every complaint that comes with it. While dealers will now share that responsibility, Ola cannot simply wish away all issues with a reset. It has to address the structural challenges that led to the bottlenecks and delays.
The success of the transition hinges on three major factors.
The first is sell-through: whether registrations keep pace with wholesale dispatches as the dealer network grows from 319 outlets to 700. The second is supply: whether production really reaches 25,000 a month, and whether suppliers and chargers keep up with it. The third test is margin: whether the cost savings from closing company showrooms outweigh the gross margin given up to dealers.
Ola has moved quickly, and the early numbers seem to be favourable. But they are the company's own, and they cover only a few weeks. The real proof will come in the Q3 results.
(Disclaimer: Shradha Sharma, Founder and CEO of YourStory, is an independent director at Ola Electric.)
Edited by Swetha Kannan

evidence.title: Ola Electric Shuts Direct Stores, Shifts to Dealers: What Its Shareholders’ Letter Reveals
evidence.text:
Ola Electric is making a major change to its retail strategy, moving away from its company-operated direct-to-consumer (D2C) stores towards a dealer-led distribution network. In its November 12, 2026, shareholder letter, the electric two-wheeler manufacturer said it had stopped accepting orders through its own stores from November 1 and plans to close most of these outlets by December. The company had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores as of November 8, with ambitions to expand the network to 450 stores by December and 700 by March 2027.
The shift comes as Ola Electric attempts to reduce operating expenses, improve working capital and regain market share after facing increasing competition from established two-wheeler manufacturers. The company reported September-quarter revenue of ₹421 crore, down 39% year-on-year, while its consolidated net loss narrowed to ₹362 crore. Its shareholder letter describes the dealer transition as an important part of rebuilding the business, with management arguing that demand is no longer its biggest constraint. Instead, the company says its supply chain needs to scale up to meet orders.
Why Is Ola Electric Moving to a Dealer-Led Model?
Ola Electric originally built its sales network around company-operated stores and a direct relationship with customers. This gave the company greater control over the customer experience, product demonstrations and sales process.
However, operating a large retail network also involves substantial expenses, including store rentals, employee salaries, infrastructure and other administrative costs.
The dealer-led model changes this structure. Independent dealer partners take responsibility for operating retail outlets, selling vehicles and holding inventory.
Under the arrangement, dealers pay for vehicles when placing orders and maintain stock at their own stores. This can reduce the amount of working capital Ola needs to finance its distribution network.
The company also expects to reduce operating expenses by approximately ₹50 crore as it closes its company-operated stores.
Ola stopped taking orders through its D2C outlets on November 1, with most closures expected by December. All new vehicle production is now being routed through dealer partners.
Ola Electric Targets 700 Dealer Stores by March 2027
The dealer network has expanded rapidly since the first outlets opened on September 4, 2026.
According to the shareholder letter, Ola had appointed 255 dealer partners operating 319 stores by November 8.
The company has outlined an ambitious expansion schedule.
The expansion is intended to increase Ola’s physical presence across markets while reducing its dependence on company-operated retail infrastructure.
The company also reported that dealer partners were placing repeat orders, suggesting that wholesale activity was increasing as the network matured.
However, dealer appointments and store openings alone do not establish retail demand. The more important measure will be how quickly dealers sell vehicles to customers and replenish their inventory.
Ola reported that dealer channel inventory stood at approximately 15 days, with some of its earliest outlets holding less than a week’s stock.
The company described dealer sell-through as strong and improving.
Wholesale Orders Increase as Ola Ramps Up Production
The shareholder letter indicates that wholesale orders through the dealer channel have increased considerably since September.
The November and December figures are company projections, not completed monthly results.
Ola also expects production to increase as suppliers improve their ability to deliver components.
The company reported the following production figures:
The company said production had remained broadly flat for several months before beginning to increase.
Management believes its manufacturing facility can produce considerably more vehicles than its current output. The immediate challenge, according to Ola, is expanding supplier capacity rather than increasing factory capacity.
It also disclosed that approximately 5,000 vehicles with paid orders in September were delivered a week late because of charger unavailability, pushing those deliveries into October.
This highlights an important issue: even when customer demand exists, shortages of components and supporting equipment can delay deliveries and affect sales performance.
Lower Operating Costs and Improved Working Capital
Reducing the cost of running its retail network is one of the central financial objectives of the dealer transition.
Ola reported consolidated operating expenses of ₹369 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with ₹390 crore in the previous quarter, excluding a one-time non-cash reversal of ₹57 crore in Q1.
The company expects another reduction of approximately ₹50 crore as its company-operated stores shut down.
Its borrowing position has also improved.
The dealer model could improve cash flow because dealers pay for vehicles when ordering them and hold inventory themselves. This reduces the amount of money Ola needs to commit to its distribution network.
However, the transition does not automatically guarantee profitability. The company still needs to improve production efficiency, manage supplier costs and convert dealer orders into actual customer sales.
Ola Electric Still Faces Market Share Pressure
The restructuring comes at a challenging time for Ola Electric.
Competition from TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto, Ather Energy and Hero MotoCorp has intensified, pushing Ola down to fifth position in monthly electric two-wheeler registrations, according to The Economic Times.
The company’s September-quarter financial performance also reflects the pressure.
Revenue declined 39% year-on-year, although the consolidated net loss narrowed.
The company said its market share had improved in several markets where dealer outlets opened earlier and stabilised. However, this is management’s assessment, and broader registration data will be important in determining whether the recovery is sustained.
Ola also acknowledged that gross margins could decline slightly during Q3 and Q4 FY27 because of the dealer rollout, even as operating margins are expected to improve.
Battery Cell Manufacturing Remains Ola’s Second Growth Engine
Beyond electric scooters and motorcycles, Ola Electric is also investing in its battery cell manufacturing business.
The company said it achieved scheduled commercial operation for 6 GWh of cell manufacturing capacity ahead of schedule.
It plans to gradually integrate its own lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells into existing vehicles from Q4 FY27.
Ola expects its automotive business to consume approximately 2–3 GWh of cells in FY28.
The company also provided details about its expected manufacturing yields:
- NMC cell yields were approximately 70–75%, with a target of 80–85% by the end of Q3 FY27.
- NMC yields are expected to approach 90% in Q4 FY27.
- LFP yields are targeted to reach approximately 70% by the end of Q4 FY27 and around 90% in Q1 FY28.
Ola said that using its own cells could achieve cost parity with external purchases at approximately 70% yield. At 85% yield, it expects savings of around 10–15% compared with buying cells externally.
These are company projections, and actual cost benefits will depend on manufacturing yields, production volumes and raw material expenses.
The battery business could become an additional source of growth if Ola successfully scales production and improves manufacturing economics.
The Bigger Picture
Ola Electric’s dealer pivot represents a fundamental change in its business model. The company is moving from owning and operating much of its retail infrastructure towards a distribution structure in which independent partners handle sales and inventory. This could lower fixed costs, improve working capital and make expansion across India easier.
However, the success of the strategy will depend on execution. Dealer expansion must translate into actual customer registrations, repeat orders and reliable after-sales service. Ola also needs to address supply-chain bottlenecks that have delayed deliveries despite its claims of strong demand.
The battery cell business adds another dimension to the restructuring. If Ola can improve manufacturing yields and integrate its own cells into vehicles at competitive costs, it could strengthen its position beyond electric vehicle assembly. But both businesses require sustained investment and operational improvements.
Looking Ahead
The next few quarters will be important for evaluating Ola Electric’s transformation. Investors will watch whether the company reaches its 450-store December target, expands to 700 stores by March 2027 and achieves its production projections. The dealer network’s ability to convert wholesale orders into retail sales will be particularly important in assessing whether the new distribution model is working.
For Ola Electric, the immediate priority is to reduce costs, improve deliveries and regain market share while building its battery manufacturing business. The dealer pivot offers a potential route towards a more financially sustainable operating model, but its success will ultimately depend on stronger customer demand, reliable supplies and consistent execution.
