evidence.title: Neutral Exide; target of Rs 381: Motilal Oswal
evidence.text:
Motilal Oswal's research report on Exide
Exide’s (EXID) 2QFY27 PAT of INR3.9b came in above our est. of INR2.9b. Strong double-digit YoY growth was observed across key segments, which led to 20.3% YoY growth in revenues, beating our expectations. The outlook for the lead-acid business remains positive across the auto and industrial segments (excluding telecom). However, we remain cautious about the long-term returns from the lithium-ion business. Moreover, the stock, trading at ~21.3x/19.1x FY27E/28E EPS, appears fairly valued. We reiterate our Neutral rating with an SoTP-based TP of INR381. We value the core (lead acid) business at 14x FY28E EPS. We add a value of INR71 per share for the EV business (based on book value) and INR45 per share for its stake in HDFC Life.
Outlook
We reiterate our Neutral rating with an SoTP-based TP of INR381. We value the core (lead acid) business at 14x FY28E EPS. We add a value of INR71 per share for the EV business (based on book value) and INR45 per share for its stake in HDFC Life.

Exclusive: Deepak K Khare To Join Exide As COO
Former Agratas manufacturing operations head brings nearly three decades of experience across automotive manufacturing, electric vehicles and battery gigafactory development.
Deepak K Khare has joined Exide Energy Solutions as Chief Operations Officer (COO), Autocar Professional has exclusively learnt from sources. He moves to the battery manufacturer after serving as Vice President, Manufacturing Operations and Site Head at Agratas, the Tata Group’s battery manufacturing business.
The appointment brings an executive with experience in automotive manufacturing, greenfield plant development and electric vehicle production to Exide Energy Solutions. Khare has worked on manufacturing projects in India and overseas, including battery cell manufacturing and electric vehicle assembly facilities.
At Agratas, where he worked from October 2023 to November 2026, Khare was involved in developing the company’s battery gigafactory at Sanand, Gujarat. His responsibilities included land acquisition, recruitment, onboarding design and construction partners, and overseeing the development of the facility. In a recent LinkedIn post announcing his departure, Khare said process equipment was being commissioned at the site, marking an important stage in the project’s development.
Before joining Agratas, Khare served as Head of Manufacturing Operations at Lucid Motors from August 2022 to September 2023. During his tenure, he was involved in establishing the luxury electric vehicle manufacturer’s manufacturing operations in Saudi Arabia, including preparations for the commencement of vehicle production.
Khare brings nearly three decades of experience across automotive manufacturing, plant operations, supplier development and quality management. Earlier in his career, he held senior manufacturing responsibilities at Ford Motor Company, including managing vehicle production operations at its Sanand facility, where he led a workforce of more than 1,800 employees. His responsibilities covered production, quality, safety, cost management and operational improvements.
He also worked with Airbus as Director, Procurement Quality, and held engineering roles at Caterpillar. His career spans automotive, aerospace and industrial equipment manufacturing, with experience in production management, supplier quality and manufacturing operations.
Khare’s appointment comes as Exide continues its expansion into lithium-ion battery manufacturing through its subsidiary, Exide Energy Solutions. His background in developing battery manufacturing facilities and managing automotive production operations is particularly relevant to the company’s ongoing investments in advanced battery manufacturing.

evidence.title: Exide Industries invests ₹150 crore in subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions
evidence.text:
Exide Industries invests ₹150 crore in subsidiary Exide Energy Solutions
- Published OnOct 27, 2026 | 22:22 IST
- Last Updated OnOct 27, 2026 | 22:22 IST
The fresh capital infusion will ramp up lithium-ion battery cell and module production at the subsidiary's greenfield Bengaluru plant, scaling up manufacturing capacity for electric vehicles. Discover how management plans to offset ongoing bottom-line losses as EV adoption accelerates.
Exide Industries Limited has invested nearly ₹150 crore in its wholly owned subsidiary, Exide Energy Solutions Limited (EESL), through a rights issue, taking its total investment in the subsidiary to ₹5,352.23 crore.
The company invested ₹149.99 crore on October 27, 2026, by subscribing to 4.29 crore equity shares of EESL on a rights basis. The shares were allotted on the same day, according to an exchange filing.
The latest investment is intended to meet EESL’s funding requirements for its greenfield plant in Bengaluru, which will manufacture and sell lithium-ion battery cells, modules and packs for electric vehicles and stationary applications.
Following the investment, Exide Industries’ shareholding in EESL remains unchanged at 100%. The investment includes the amount invested in the erstwhile merged subsidiary, Exide Energy Private Limited.
EESL, incorporated on March 24, 2022, is engaged in manufacturing and selling lithium-ion battery cells, modules and packs. Its operations also cover battery cells of different chemistries and form factors, including cylindrical, pouch and prismatic cells.
As of March 31, 2026, EESL had a paid-up equity share capital of ₹1,661.36 crore and a net worth of ₹3,991.06 crore. Its turnover stood at ₹157.56 crore in FY26, while it reported a loss after tax of ₹248.16 crore.
EESL’s turnover stood at ₹116.89 crore in FY25 and ₹239.14 crore in FY24, according to the filing.
Exide Industries said the transaction constitutes a related-party transaction and was conducted at arm’s length. No governmental or regulatory approvals were required for the investment.
The shares were issued at ₹35 each, comprising a face value of ₹10 and a premium of ₹25 per share.
Exide Industries shares closed at ₹336.10 on October 27, down 0.24%, or ₹0.80.

evidence.title: Exide Industries Surges 8% as Q2 Profit Jumps 65%; Can Its New Lithium-Ion Plant Boost Growth?
evidence.text:
Shares of Exide Industries attracted buying interest on Wednesday after the battery manufacturer reported stronger quarterly earnings and highlighted progress in its lithium-ion manufacturing business. The results show improving profitability in the established battery operations, while the recently commissioned cell plant marks a significant step towards a new growth opportunity. 
With a market capitalization of Rs. 31,471.25 crore, the shares of Exide Industries Ltd were trading at Rs. 370.25 per share, up 6.90% from its previous closing price of Rs. 346.35 apiece. The stock trades at a P/E of 33.6x on a consolidated basis. The shares touched an intraday high of Rs.375.90, up 8.53%
Consolidated Earnings Improve
The company’s consolidated revenues grew 21.3% YoY to Rs.5,291.87 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs.4,364.51 crore in the same quarter last year. Consolidated net profits were up 65.4% at Rs.287.14 crore against Rs.173.64 crore.
Consolidated operating EBITDA was up 43.5% at Rs.561.51 crore against Rs.391.42 crore. EBITDA Margins improved to 10.6% from ~9.0% indicating an increase in operating profits faster than sales. Pre-tax profits increased by 67.3% to Rs.423.73 crore.
Consolidated revenues increased by 19.4% to Rs.10,820.25 crore in the first half of FY27. Net profits increased by 42.4% to Rs.638.44 crore. Calculated operating EBITDA increased by 27.2% to Rs.1,182.99 crore. However, EBITDA for Q2 was down from the previous quarter’s calculated EBITDA of Rs.621.48 crore.
What Is Driving the Core Business?
The growth was driven by good demand, GST rationalisation and price increases. Revenue for automotive OEM business grew by over 25% YoY for the 4th quarter in a row. The two wheeler and four wheeler replacement businesses grew by double digit for the 4th quarter in a row.
Home inverters and solar had growth of over 20% for the second quarter in a row. This was driven by seasonality and government backed adoption of rooftop solar. Exports also grew by over 20% (on a lower base). The company also entered a long term cooperation agreement with ExCom Energy Solutions of Germany to expand its portfolio of industrial batteries and energy storage solutions in the European Economic Area.
However, input costs are a concern for the business. Geopolitical factors, higher crude oil prices and a weak rupee have limited benefit from the lower international lead and antimony prices. Improved margins will depend on our ability to manage these pressures.
Lithium-Ion Plant Enters Production
A key strategic milestone was achieved with the commissioning of Exide Energy Solutions Limited’s 6 GWh lithium-ion cell gigafactory in Bengaluru on September 23, 2026. The facility can be expanded to 12 GWh and will produce lithium iron phosphate and nickel manganese cobalt cells for electric mobility and stationary storage applications.
Exide also made an additional investment of Rs.550 crore in the subsidiary between April and October 2026, with cumulative equity investment now standing at Rs.5,352 crore. The milestone shows that manufacturing has been achieved, but at an early stage for commercialisation.
The company has provided samples to EV two-wheelers and telecom customers. Key priorities moving forward include stabilising the lines, increasing yields and gaining approvals from customers. The company has not yet provided details on volumes of cells being supplied, large orders from customers or when they expect to see meaningful earnings contribution.
Cash Flow Remains a Key Test
While accounting profits have improved, the consolidated cash flow from operations fell to Rs.437.99 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs.1,423.19 crore in the previous year, representing a decline of ~69%. Inventory utilised Rs.211.98 crore while it released Rs.675.62 crore in H1 FY26.
Operating cash flow, after capital expenditure of Rs.591.71 crore on property, plant and equipment was negative to the tune of ~ Rs.153.72 crore. While this does not negate the earnings upside, it demonstrates that working capital management and capital allocation are important to note in this phase of our lithium ion business.
Also Read: Saregama Shares Surge 14% as Live Events Revenue Jumps 101%: How Did Music and Video Perform?
Outlook
Exide has a strong existing battery business driving revenue growth and margin improvement but also has exposure to a potentially much bigger storage opportunity with its new cell plant. However, it is important that capacity being commissioned can be turned into profitable sales.
The key will be getting orders from customers, good yields, good utilisation and conversion of earnings into cash. Once the Li-ion business is contributing to revenue and not putting pressure on cash in the consolidated group then it will be a more convincing story.

Exide Industries Limited announced its unaudited financial results for the quarter and half-year ended 30th September 2026, showcasing robust growth across key financial metrics. evidence.title: Exide Industries Q2 FY27: Standalone PAT Rises 75% on Strong Revenue Growth and Margin Expansion
evidence.text:
Exide Industries has reported a strong standalone performance for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, with revenue rising 20.3% year-on-year to ₹5,026 crore and profit after tax increasing 75.1% to ₹386 crore. The results reflect healthy demand, effective cost optimisation, calibrated price increases, and improved operating leverage.
Q2 FY27 performance
Standalone revenue from operations grew to ₹5,026 crore in Q2 FY27 from ₹4,178 crore in Q2 FY26, representing a 20.3% year-on-year increase. EBITDA rose 53.6% to ₹606 crore from ₹395 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded by 270 basis points to 12.1% from 9.4% in the year-ago quarter.
Profit before tax increased 75.5% year-on-year to ₹522 crore, compared with ₹298 crore in Q2 FY26. Profit after tax rose 75.1% to ₹386 crore from ₹221 crore, while earnings per share for the quarter stood at ₹4.55, against ₹2.60 in the corresponding period last year.
H1 FY27 performance
For the first half of FY27, standalone revenue increased 18.9% year-on-year to ₹10,331 crore from ₹8,688 crore in H1 FY26. EBITDA grew 33.8% to ₹1,262 crore, and the EBITDA margin improved by 130 basis points to 12.2% from 10.9%.
Profit before tax for the six-month period rose 46.5% to ₹1,066 crore, while profit after tax increased 46.7% to ₹794 crore from ₹541 crore. Earnings per share for H1 FY27 stood at ₹9.34, compared with ₹6.37 in H1 FY26.
Drivers of profitability
The sharp improvement in profitability was supported by cost-optimisation initiatives, calibrated price increases, and volume growth. The company noted that input costs remained elevated due to prolonged geopolitical challenges, but pricing actions and operational efficiencies helped expand the EBITDA margin by 270 basis points year-on-year in Q2.
The performance also reflects the benefits of the company’s operating model and stronger execution across its businesses. Demand remained broad-based, supporting revenue growth during the quarter despite the challenging input-cost environment.
Exide’s Q2 results indicate that the company has been able to convert revenue growth into disproportionately higher earnings growth, with PAT rising nearly four times faster than revenue on a year-on-year basis. The 12.1% EBITDA margin in Q2 and 12.2% margin in H1 suggest improving operational efficiency, although sustained margin performance will depend on raw-material costs, pricing, and demand conditions.
The company’s financial release page lists its FY27 disclosures, including its earlier Q1 FY27 release highlighting revenue growth of 17.6% and PAT growth of 27.1%, indicating that the strong earnings momentum has continued into the September quarter.
Commenting on the performance, Mr. Avik Roy, MD & CEO, said: "We have sustained our growth momentum in the second quarter, with most of the businesses growing in double digits. Demand held up well across our end-markets, as the affordability benefits of GST rationalisation continued. We were further aided by favourable seasonal demand for Home UPS business. Growth opportunities remain encouraging across Automotive OEMs, Replacement, Home Inverters, Solar, Infrastructure and Exports.
The Automotive OEM business grew by over 25% for the fourth consecutive quarter, and the 2W/4W Replacement business sustained its double-digit growth. Home Inverters and Solar also had a strong quarter, growing over 20%. Exports grew by over 20% YoY on a low base, and our long-term strategic cooperation agreement with ExCom Energy Solutions GmbH, Germany, strengthens our presence in the European Economic Area.
Input costs remained elevated vs last year, due to prolonged geopolitical challenges, especially across West Asia. Crude oil prices went up significantly, resulting in an overall inflationary environment. On a sequential quarter basis, the full benefits of softer Lead LME and antimony prices could not be fully realized due to continuous weakening of Rupee against US Dollar.
The Company undertook various cost optimisation initiatives to absorb this cost pressure. Further, calibrated price increase and operating leverage enabled EBITDA margin expansion in Q2 and H1 of FY27.
We enter the festive season with healthy demand indicators. At the same time, we remain mindful of the high base of last year's post-GST demand surge as well as continue to closely monitor input costs.
23rd September 2026 marked a defining milestone in our New Energy business’ journey, as EESL completed the commissioning of 6 GWh of lithium-ion cell gigafactory in Bengaluru. Our focus over the coming quarters is on stabilising the lines, improving yields and completing customer qualifications. These achievements reinforce our confidence in building a strong foundation in the New Energy business."

evidence.title: RIL, Amara Raja, Exide, among 22 companies to bid for 10 GWh battery storage capacity PLI
evidence.text:
The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) on Thursday said it has received 22 bids for 10 GWh of advanced chemistry cell (ACC) manufacturing capacity under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme from companies including Reliance Industries, ACME Solar Holdings, Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, Exide Energy Solutions, JSW Neo Energy, and Vikram Solar.
The 10 GWh capacity is earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications and forms part of the overall targeted 50 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity under the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage.
“The allocation of 10 GWh for GSSS applications is expected to support the country’s rapidly growing energy-storage requirements arising from the expansion of renewable energy. It will contribute to enhancing energy security and deepening the domestic value chain for ACC technologies,” the MHI said.
In May 2021, the Cabinet approved the scheme, with a total budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore. It seeks to enhance the domestic ACC manufacturing capabilities and encourage large domestic and international players to establish a globally competitive ACC manufacturing ecosystem in India, MHI said.
The request for proposal (RFP) was floated on the Central Public Procurement (CPP) portal on July 15, 2026, while the pre-bid conference was held on July 29. The last date for bid submission was November 10, and the technical bids were opened the following day in the presence of bidders at the MHI, it said in a statement.
“The bidding is being conducted online through a transparent two-stage Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) mechanism,” the Ministry said, adding that the strong participation in the tender reflects growing industry interest in India’s ACC manufacturing potential and reinforces the government’s commitment to building a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive and sustainable ACC ecosystem.
Other bidders include Avaada Electro, Fujiyama Power Systems, Megha Engineering and Infrastructures, Waaree Energy Storage Solutions, Godawari New Energy, Renew Photovoltaics and Sun Drops Energia. The list also carries names such as GK Energy, JPM Energy Solutions, Lineage Power, Mahendra Sponge and Power, Nsure Reliable Power Solutions, Sai Bioenergy, Shirdi Sai Electricals, Utex New Energy, and Zetsol Energy.

evidence.title: Exide, Amara Raja rush to monetize $1 billion Li-ion cell lines as investor questions mount
evidence.text:
India’s top battery makers, Exide Industries Ltd and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Ltd, are rushing to operationalize their lithium-ion cell lines amid investor pressure over returns on more than $1 billion in investments. Exide has invested $632 million so far, while Amara Raja has deployed $248 million and approved an additional $247 million this month. The push comes as both firms await large orders from car and two-wheeler makers, despite having secured preliminary tie-ups with Hyundai-Kia and Ather.
The two companies are taking distinct paths to generate early revenue from their plants. Exide is starting with cells for electric rickshaws and telecom towers, while Amara Raja is focusing on battery energy storage system (BESS) projects.
The delay in electric vehicle (EV) programmes has increased pressure on both companies, as Exide had planned to start the first 6GWh of its cell plant by FY25 but only did so in September 2026. Amara Raja, which had earlier expected commercial cell production by FY26, is now targeting Q2FY28 for its first 2GWh line.
Amara Raja shares are down 18% so far this year while Exide shares are up 6%. The Nifty Auto index has gained 0.15% over this period.
Alternative routes
For Exide, initial revenue is coming from lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, which require shorter approval cycles than the nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) cells common in electric two-wheelers. The company is deploying its 102Ah LFP cells in its own e-rickshaw battery packs and has dispatched samples to telecom operators.
Lithium ion cells that power electric vehicles are mostly imported from China. LFP cells are cheaper and longer-lasting, while NMC cells perform better but do not last as long as LFP cells.
Exide managing director and chief executive Avik Roy said the company started earning revenue from LFP cells in October, while its NMC cells are still being tested by customers.
“Performance testing has been very satisfactory. We got positive feedback,” Roy said during the company’s earnings call on 5 November. “Lifecycle testing takes time, and once lifecycle testing is over, they will do the pack and the vehicle-level testing. That is the next phase.”
Amara Raja, meanwhile, plans to start commercial operations in BESS before its EV cell business begins. The company has finished checking its machines at its 5GWh pack assembly plant and expects test runs in December, followed by commercial operations in January or February.
“We don't foresee a challenge with respect to utilization of the plant,” chief financial officer Y. Delli Babu said, pointing to demand from grid-scale storage and commercial and industrial customers. The company expects to use 50-60% of the facility’s capacity in FY28 and reach full utilization by FY29.
Its cell program remains at the customer approval stage. Amara Raja has made nearly 2,000 NMC cells at its customer qualification plant, which are being tested internally. Delli Babu said the company expects to send samples to potential original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in the next few months. LFP cells are still being developed.
Both companies are building bigger manufacturing plants while trying to earn money soon from other uses. Exide has started a 6GWh lithium-ion cell plant in Bengaluru, while Amara Raja is developing its Giga Corridor in Divitipally, Telangana. Its bigger plan includes 16GWh of cell capacity and 5GWh of pack assembly.
Both companies first worked with Chinese technology partners to build their cell businesses. Amara Raja’s 2024 licensing deal with Gotion for LFP technology, however, faced problems after Beijing tightened rules on technology transfers, forcing the company to rely more on its own research and development. Exide's China partner is Svolt.
The two companies have also signed preliminary agreements with vehicle manufacturers, but these have yet to translate into final supply orders. Exide signed an agreement with Hyundai Motor and Kia in 2024 to develop and supply locally made LFP cells, while Amara Raja signed an agreement with Ather Energy to develop and supply NMC and LFP cells for two-wheelers.
Roy said the product roadmap under the Exide-Hyundai-Kia partnership had not been finalised and that the companies would make a joint announcement once they reached a milestone. He added that discussions had accelerated after slowing in recent months.
China cost & validation barrier
However, even after local cells become available, vehicle manufacturers may not switch suppliers immediately. Ather Energy chief business officer Ravneet Phokela told Mint in an interview in October that domestic sourcing was driven more by supply security than by cost savings, with Indian cells likely to be 20-30% more expensive than Chinese alternatives initially. “China's cost structure is very different. They have already scaled up, their yields are very high, plants are depreciated, lithium is local,” Phokela said.
He said switching cell suppliers required extensive testing and validation, making it difficult for vehicle makers to shift quickly even when a domestic option became available.
“It's not a hot-swap,” Phokela said. “There is a design, development, testing and validation cycle. It takes almost a year.”
Analyst estimates point to a gradual ramp-up. Nuvama Institutional Equities wrote in a 5 November note that Exide is targeting 20-25% utilization of its NMC capacity by Q4FY27, with further orders expected in subsequent quarters. Analysts at Anand Rathi said in a 4 November note that they expected Amara Raja’s BESS plant to reach 50% utilization of its initial 5GWh capacity within six to seven months of commercial production. They also estimated the company’s NMC cell plant would be ready by Q1FY28.

evidence.title: Exide beats Amara in Q2, but returns from lithium-ion investments will decide the winner
evidence.text:
Automotive battery makers Exide Industries and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility posted contrasting results for the September quarter (Q2FY27). Exide’s standalone Ebitda rose nearly 54% year-on-year to ₹606 crore as revenue improved 20% to ₹5,026 crore. In contrast, Amara saw Ebitda fall 5% year-on-year to ₹386 crore—hurt by a sharp increase in input costs such as metal alloys and sulphuric acid—even as revenue grew 13% to ₹3,843 crore.
Exide’s Ebitda growth reflects strong market demand and its ability to pass on cost inflation. It hiked prices of four-wheelers by about 10% and two-wheelers by 5% during January-October. Q2FY27 gross margin rose 75 basis points (bps) year-on-year to 30.6%. Other costs dropped by over 170 basis points, though this came on a high base created when consumers deferred purchases ahead of last year’s GST rate cut, resulting in adverse operating leverage. Amara Raja managed only limited price hikes — 2% in Q2 after 3% in Q1 — causing its gross margin to shrink by about 300 basis points to 29.8%.
Betting big on lithium-ion
With the industry transitioning from lead-acid to lithium-ion technology, both companies are investing heavily to keep pace. Exide commenced commercial production at its lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery plant and began recognising revenues in October. Meanwhile, its wholly owned subsidiary, Exide Energy Solutions Ltd (EESL), commissioned a 6 GWh lithium-ion cell facility in Q2. EESL manufactures and supplies advanced-chemistry cells, modules, and battery packs for both electric vehicles (EVs) and stationary energy storage systems.
India’s growing demand for electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) provides scope for growth. Monthly E2W sales have touched about 200,000 units this year, compared with 120,000 units last year, Exide said. So far in FY27, the company has invested ₹5,352 crore in EESL. “With EV inflection, Exide can gain significantly in the medium term if it executes well on Li-ion cell production, though it may take one or two years for yields to stabilise and to achieve the right scale,” said Nomura Global Markets Research.
Amara’s 10GWh battery energy storage solution plant is expected to start commercial production in Q4FY27. It also announced an investment of ₹2,320 crore to set up a 5 GWh LFP battery manufacturing facility and increase the capacity of its Li-ion factory. So far, it has invested ₹2,100 crore in total in the new energy business, which accounts for about 6% of consolidated revenue and encompasses lithium-ion technology, clean energy storage, and electric mobility solutions.
Both battery makers face significant risks due to their heavy capital commitments, as the long-term commercial viability of lithium-ion technology remains unproven. Also, because global lithium-ion cell manufacturing is inherently low-margin, the pivot could dilute returns. For Amara Raja, higher procurement costs for alloys, sulphuric acid and polypropylene, coupled with rising interest expenses from debt-funded investments in its new energy division threaten to weigh on profitability, said Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
While Exide can fund its LFP cell localization partnership with Hyundai-Kia through internal accruals, Motilal Oswal highlights significant hurdles in its lithium-ion cell venture. The brokerage said most domestic passenger vehicle manufacturers already have in-house battery plans or existing tie-ups, limiting Exide’s total addressable market. Also, Exide is not participating in the production linked incentive (PLI) scheme, which could undermine its cost competitiveness against peers that quality for it.
Both stocks have corrected 29% from their respective 52-week highs in August. So far this calendar year, however, Exide is down just 3%, compared with a 22% drop in Amara Raja. The stocks currently trade at 20 times and 17 times their estimated FY27 earnings, respectively, according to Bloomberg data.

evidence.title: Exide shares surge 6% in 6 months, beats Amara in Q2 with 54% profit
evidence.text:
According to latest market data, Exide Industries shares have demonstrated robust performance with a 6% increase over the past 6 months and a 3.55% decline over the last year. As of November 8, 2026, the stock closed at ₹366.35 with a market capitalization of ₹31,139.75 crore. The company's 52-week high stands at ₹496.40 while the 52-week low was ₹287, reflecting significant volatility in recent months. The stock currently trades at a PE ratio of 29.67 and PB ratio of 2.25, with analysts maintaining a 'Buy' rating for long-term investment. In contrast, Amara Raja Energy & Mobility shares are down 18% so far this year, significantly underperforming the broader market.
According to reports from Stock Market News, Exide Industries delivered strong September quarter results with standalone Ebitda rising 54% year-on-year to ₹606 crore as revenue improved 20% to ₹5,026 crore. In contrast, Amara Raja Energy & Mobility saw Ebitda fall 5% year-on-year to ₹386 crore despite revenue growing 13% to ₹3,843 crore. The contrasting performance was driven by different pricing strategies and cost management approaches between the two automotive battery manufacturers.
As reported by Stock Market News, Exide's Ebitda growth reflected strong market demand and its ability to pass on cost inflation through strategic pricing. The company hiked prices of four-wheelers by about 10% and two-wheelers by 5% during January-October. In contrast, Amara Raja managed only limited price hikes — 2% in Q2 after 3% in Q1, causing its gross margin to shrink by about 300 basis points to 29.8%. Exide's Q2FY27 gross margin rose 75 basis points year-on-year to 30.6%.
According to Mint, both companies are taking distinct approaches to generate early revenue from their lithium-ion investments. Exide is starting with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for electric rickshaws and telecom towers, deploying its 102Ah LFP cells in its own e-rickshaw battery packs and dispatching samples to telecom operators. As per Exide MD Avik Roy, the company started earning revenue from LFP cells in October, with NMC cells still undergoing customer testing. Amara Raja is focusing on battery energy storage system (BESS) projects, having finished machine checks at its 5GWh pack assembly plant with test runs expected in December and commercial operations in January or February. The company expects to use 50-60% of the facility's capacity in FY28 and reach full utilization by FY29.
As reported by Mint, both companies face significant challenges in monetizing their lithium-ion investments amid sluggish EV adoption and long testing cycles. Exide has invested $632 million so far while Amara Raja has deployed $248 million and approved an additional $247 million this month. The delay in EV programmes has increased pressure, with Exide originally planning to start its first 6GWh cell plant by FY25 but only achieving this in September 2026. Amara Raja, which expected commercial cell production by FY26, is now targeting Q2FY28 for its first 2GWh line. Despite preliminary agreements with Hyundai-Kia and Ather Energy, vehicle manufacturers may not switch suppliers immediately due to extensive testing and validation cycles requiring almost a year.

evidence.title: Amara Raja organises three-day health and awareness drive in Hyderabad
evidence.text:
Amara Raja organises three-day health and awareness drive in Hyderabad
                Amara Raja Energy & Mobility organised a three-day health and awareness drive in Hyderabad's Vanasthalipuram, benefiting over 500 people through free health and eye check-ups. The initiative also featured truck inspections and sessions on road safety, fleet management and operational efficiency
                
                                        
                    Published Date - 7 November 2026, 03:50 PM 
                 
                                    
                                                
                
                            
Hyderabad: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Limited, the manufacturer of Amaron Batteries, in association with its franchise partners, the Telangana State Lorry Owners Welfare Association, and Auto Nagar New Stand Lorry Owners Association Hyderabad, organised a three-day health and awareness drive at Vanasthalipuram.
As part of the initiative, a free health and eye check-up camp was conducted, benefiting more than 500 people. The initiative focused on raising awareness among truck drivers about the importance of regular health check-ups and eye care, enabling them to work safely while maintaining better health.
                            
                                            
                
                
    
The drive also included technical inspections of trucks and awareness sessions for transporters and fleet owners on reducing operational costs, improving fleet management, enhancing vehicle efficiency and increasing profitability. A Transporters’ Meet was also organsied bringing together key stakeholders from transportation sector to discuss industry issues, road safety, and fleet operations.
Manish Tuli, Sales Head and Spokesperson, Amara Raja, said, “Our endeavour is to understand the health and operational needs of the transportation community and provide them with practical solutions.”

evidence.title: What Investors Got Wrong About Amara Raja Before The Drop
evidence.text:
If you only glanced at headlines, Amara Raja Energy & Mobility looked fine. Revenue and profit in the latest quarter were higher than a year earlier, even as net margin slipped a little. Holding Amara Raja Energy & Mobility over the past year would have meant a 30.8% loss, including dividends. If you had been weighing a position back on 30 October 2025, what clues, if any, pointed to this kind of outcome?
On Simply Wall St, a Narrative is an investor's thesis written down: the reasoning, plus the numbers it rests on. Run those numbers and you get an estimated Fair Value.
The easy part of this move is behind Amara Raja Energy & Mobility. Zero in on 199 high quality undervalued stocks for companies trading below our estimates.
The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On Amara Raja Energy & Mobility
The shares cost ₹1,017 at the start of the period, and you were choosing between two very different stories for Amara Raja Energy & Mobility.
The bullish narrative put Fair Value at ₹1,163, with optimism built on heavy spending into lithium batteries and energy storage projects that were expected to reshape the product mix.
The bearish view set Fair Value at ₹925, stressing the risk that 95 to 96% of revenue still came from lead-acid batteries while large new-energy capex could strain returns if execution faltered.
What The Results Changed For Amara Raja Energy & Mobility
For Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, the clearest datapoint was the Q1 2027 print. Revenue moved to ₹42,145.4m while net income reached ₹1,909.4m, which leaned toward the bullish story that expected a healthier profit pool. Net margin slipping from 4.8% to 4.5% challenged the idea of cleaner profitability, so the evidence cut both ways.
The key lesson is simple. When a thesis hinges on margin improvement, do not just track sales or earnings. Watch the net margin line every quarter and test whether profitability is actually moving toward the forecasted level.
What The Fall In Amara Raja Energy & Mobility Now Asks You To Believe
Amara Raja Energy & Mobility now trades at ₹687, with the past year meaning a loss of 30.8% for holders. The selected Narrative still puts Fair Value above the current price and focuses on how lithium cells, BESS projects and recycling could reshape earnings quality.
The real test for anyone considering that view is whether heavy FY27 capex and ongoing lithium R&D genuinely turn into higher and steadier margins rather than a drag from extra costs and weaker free cash flow.
"The main thing that has to go right is that in-house manufacturing, government support and R&D efforts on lithium cells, BESS and recycling translate into higher and more stable margins over time despite ongoing input cost and capital intensity pressures."

Published: Nov 3, 2026 6:20 PM | 1 min read
- Amara Raja Group has appointed Dheeraj Jain as Head of Corporate Affairs, effective November 2, 2026.
- Jain will lead government and regulatory engagement, policy advocacy, and corporate reputation management for the Group.
- He has over 25 years of experience in corporate affairs and public policy, having worked with companies such as Santos International, Vestas, and Hitachi Energy.

Amara Raja Group today announced the appointment of Dheeraj Jain as Head, Corporate Affairs. Dheeraj assumed charge on November 2, 2026, and will lead government and regulatory engagement across the Group's businesses.
He will also oversee policy advocacy and corporate reputation management, ensuring the Group's external engagement moves in step with its strategic business priorities.
Dheeraj brings over 25 years of cross-sector experience in corporate affairs, regulatory strategy and public policy, with a record of navigating complex regulatory environments and building the institutional relationships that turn business ambition into growth.
His earlier career includes Santos International, ReGen Powertech, Vestas and GE Renewable Energy and most recently Hitachi Energy.
Speaking on his appointment, Dheeraj Jain, Head, Corporate Affairs, Amara Raja Group, said, "Amara Raja has earned four decades of trust in India's energy story, and it is now writing the next chapter. I am excited to join at this defining moment and to help build the partnerships and policy frameworks that will enable adoption of new energy technologies at speed and scale."

evidence.title: Amara Raja Energy & Mobility reports 13% increase in Q2 FY27
evidence.text:
The Company reported an Earnings Per Share (EPS) of ₹10.29 for Q2 FY27, along with an interim dividend of ₹4.30 per equity share.
Performance was driven by strong double-digit growth in aftermarket and OEM in automotive batteries, and the Home Energy business. The new energy business also witnessed good growth in stationary telecom battery pack demand.
Speaking on the results, Mr. Harshavardhana Gourineni, Executive Director- Automotive and Industrial, said, "Robust OEM demand across 4W and 2W, together with healthy aftermarket volumes, drove domestic revenue growth of over 10%, while Industrial UPS grew over 7%. International demand remains strong, but geopolitical shipping disruptions have temporarily limited our ability to fulfil it. As logistics normalize, we are confident of accelerating growth."
Mr. Vikramadithya Gourineni, Executive Director – New Energy Business, said, “We continue to see strong volume growth, led by the stationary segment, while our Giga Factory-1 in Telangana remains on track. With the Telecom sector rapidly shifting to lithium, we are confident of sustaining our market leadership through this technology transition. Our BESS plant is also expected to come online next month, further strengthening our capabilities across the energy storage value chain.”
Mr. Jayadev Galla, Chairman and Managing Director, said, “We delivered a solid performance this quarter. Our Lead Acid Business continued to perform strongly, supported by broad-based traction across segments, while the New Energy Business maintained its growth momentum. The progress on our Giga Factory remains on track, reinforcing our confidence in building a strong, future-ready energy platform.”

evidence.title: Amara Raja Energy Q2: Profit drops 45% despite 18.5% revenue growth, board declares dividend
evidence.text:
Amara Raja Energy Q2: Profit drops 45% despite 18.5% revenue growth, board declares dividend
- Published OnNov 2, 2026 | 22:13 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 2, 2026 | 22:13 IST
Margin compression squeezed earnings despite double-digit revenue growth driven by strong automotive demand and expanding new energy segments. To capture future demand, the board approved a major lithium iron phosphate cell facility and pack assembly expansion. Find out how management plans to overcome ongoing export logistics hurdles.
Battery maker Amara Raja Energy & Mobility reported a 44.9% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to ₹153 crore for the September quarter, compared with ₹277 crore in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue from operations rose 18.5% to ₹4,109 crore from ₹3,467 crore a year earlier. Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), however, fell 3.4% to ₹362 crore from ₹374 crore. EBITDA margin narrowed to 8.8% from 10.8%.
The company said demand from original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) grew at a double-digit pace across the two-wheeler and four-wheeler segments. It also gained market share in the home energy segment, supported by its distribution network and brand reach.
Domestic aftermarket volumes grew modestly, while the industrial uninterruptible power supply (UPS) business recorded steady growth, driven by demand from data centres. Exports continued to face challenges amid geopolitical uncertainty.
New energy business
Amara Raja said sustained supplies of telecom and electric vehicle (EV) battery packs helped drive revenue growth of more than 30% in its new energy business.
The company has invested ₹2,100 crore in Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies (ARACT), its wholly owned subsidiary. Its E+Ve Lab was commissioned in October 2026 to support technology development.
The board has approved a 5 GWh cell manufacturing facility using lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry. It has also cleared an expansion of pack assembly capacity from 4 GWh to 9 GWh.
The company said its first giga factory in Telangana remained on track. Its battery energy storage systems (BESS) plant is expected to begin operations next month.
Management commentary
Harshavardhana Gourineni, executive director for automotive and industrial businesses, said strong OEM demand across two-wheelers and four-wheelers, along with aftermarket volumes, helped drive domestic revenue growth of more than 10%. Industrial UPS revenue grew more than 7%, he said.
Geopolitical disruptions to shipping temporarily restricted the company’s ability to meet international demand, Gourineni said. He added that growth was expected to accelerate as logistics conditions normalise.
Vikramadithya Gourineni, executive director for the new energy business, said volume growth continued to be led by the stationary segment. The company’s giga factory project was progressing as planned, he added.
The board declared an interim dividend of ₹4.30 per equity share, with a face value of ₹1, for FY27. The dividend will be paid on or before December 1, 2026.

evidence.title: Amara Raja Q2 Profit Down 44.8%; Plans New Battery Service Unit
evidence.text:
Amara Raja Q2 Profit Down 44.8%; Plans New Battery Service Unit
Amara Raja Energy & Mobility reports 44.8% Q2 profit decline due to higher costs. Company to launch new battery service subsidiary & expand battery manufacturing.
				
		Key Points
- Amara Raja's Q2 consolidated net profit declined by 44.8% to Rs 152.5 crore.
- The profit drop was primarily attributed to higher raw material costs, increasing total expenses.
- The company plans to establish a wholly-owned subsidiary for automotive and battery services under the Amaron Assist brand.
- Amara Raja will invest Rs 2,320 crore to expand battery pack manufacturing to 9 GWh and fund an LFP cell plant in Telangana.
For the quarter ended September, revenue from operations increased to Rs 4,108.7 crore from Rs 3,467 crore in the same period last year.
EBITDA declined 3.4 per cent to Rs 361.6 crore from Rs 374.3 crore, and EBITDA margin narrowed to 8.8 per cent from 10.8 per cent, according to the company's investor presentation.
Higher raw material costs resulted in higher expenses during the quarter, impacting its profitability. Total expenses increased by 20.6 per cent to Rs 3,922.8 crore from Rs 3,252 crore, mainly due to higher raw material costs.
Meanwhile, the board approved setting up a wholly owned subsidiary with an initial investment of up to Rs 100 crore in equity, loans or other securities, in one or more tranches.
Amara Raja noted that this subsidiary will provide automotive, battery and spare-parts services under the Amaron Assist brand. The business will focus on automotive maintenance, battery services, vehicle care and mobility assistance.
The company also said its subsidiary, Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies, has approved capital expenditure of Rs 2,320 crore. This will expand battery pack manufacturing capacity to 9 GWh from 4 GWh and fund the LFP cell manufacturing plant at its Giga Corridor in Telangana.
